- [x] **`deploy-pi.sh` updates itself mid-run, so a change to it takes effect ONE DEPLOY LATER - and nothing says so.** Found 2026-10-18 by the `0.36.1` release, the first to ship #708's Pi safety work. **What happened:** #708 added a swap precondition, a `.next.prev` fallback and an automatic asset check to `deploy-pi.sh`. `0.36.1` shipped all three and **none of them ran**, on either clone: no `.next.prev` was created, no swap gate reported, no asset check output. The new script *is* on disk afterwards and `scripts/pi/check-assets.mjs` exists, and the clone is at the release SHA - it was checked out and simply not used. **Mechanism:** `deploy-pi.sh` runs `git fetch` and checks out the target ref near the top, which **replaces the very file bash is executing**. Bash reads a script incrementally, so it carries on with the copy it already had open. **A self-updating deploy script always runs the OLD version on the deploy that introduces the new one.** **Why it matters:** the two things #708 exists to prevent - a half-written `.next` under a running service, and a poisoned year-long asset cache - were both unprotected on the very deploy that shipped their protection, and nobody would have known. The asset check was run by hand instead and passed on both environments, so no harm this time. **It also means any future fix to `deploy-pi.sh` is untested on the release that adds it**, which is the opposite of what a release manager assumes when reading "this is now guarded". **Options:** (a) **Accept and document it** - add a line to `docs/pi-hosting.md` and `docs/release-procedure.md` saying a `deploy-pi.sh` change takes effect on the NEXT deploy, and have the release manager run the new checks by hand on the release that ships them. Cheapest, no code, but relies on someone remembering. (b) **Re-exec after checkout**: once the ref is checked out, `exec "$0" "$@"` with an env guard (e.g. `DEPLOY_PI_REEXECED=1`) so it runs the new script and cannot loop. Small and self-correcting, but `exec` mid-deploy needs care with the log redirect and the `setsid nohup` wrapper the runbook uses. (c) **Split the script in two**: a thin stable launcher that fetches, and a payload script it then invokes - the launcher rarely changes, the payload is always the new one. Most robust, most churn. **Whichever is chosen, say explicitly what happens to the launcher's own updates**, since (c) only moves the problem to a smaller file. Needs a test plan that proves a change to the payload takes effect on the same deploy. See `docs/releases/2026-10-18.md` Defect 1. -> *Deployment (before go-live)*

- [ ] **A Pi deploy can poison Cloudflare's cache with a broken stylesheet, and `immutable` keeps it broken for a YEAR. Found live on 2026-10-17 by Lutan, minutes after `0.36.0` shipped (BLOCKING-ADJACENT: it reached a real user on a real phone).** **Symptom:** the app renders with no styling at all - white background, default serif text, no orange - while the page *content* is current and correct. Lutan saw it on his iPhone; the laptop looked perfect throughout. **It survived clearing Safari's cache**: it came back right, then lost the styling again minutes later, which is what ruled out a one-off stale browser cache and made it a server-side finding. **Mechanism:** `/_next/static/**` is served `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, so Cloudflare caches it for a year and never revalidates. `deploy-pi.sh` builds into a fresh `.next` and then **swaps it**, so there is a window in which a request for an asset can be answered with a 404 or a half-written file. **Whichever Cloudflare location serves that request caches the failure for a year.** Because a phone on mobile data and a laptop on wifi can reach different Cloudflare locations, the result looks like "it is only broken on mobile" and is invisible to whoever is checking from the laptop - which is exactly how it played out. **Evidence gathered at the time:** the stylesheet at origin was complete and byte-identical to test (92,570 bytes) on 20 consecutive fetches; the Bangkok edge held a good copy with `CF-Cache-Status: HIT, Age: 26158`; the page referenced exactly that file; a fresh browser rendered it correctly at desktop AND at 375 px with a phone user agent. So nothing was wrong with the build, the HTML, the CSP or the file - only with what some edge nodes had stored. **Resolved on the day by Lutan purging the Cloudflare cache** (Caching -> Configuration -> Purge Everything). **Why this needs a permanent fix: it will recur on every single Pi deploy**, the window is invisible, and the blast radius is a year of broken styling for whoever is unlucky. **Options, in rough order of preference:** (a) **Purge the cache automatically at the end of `deploy-pi.sh`** (Cloudflare API, `purge_everything` or by prefix) - simplest, and it closes the window whatever caused it; needs an API token on the Pi, so weigh that against `docs/security/`. (b) **Make the swap atomic from the edge's point of view** - build into `.next.new`, then `mv` into place in one operation, so no request can ever see a half-written file; cheap, no credentials, but it does not help the 404 window if the directory is briefly absent. (c) **Serve assets from the Worker only**, so a Pi rebuild cannot affect them at all - biggest change, best end state. (d) At minimum, **a post-deploy check that fetches the referenced stylesheet and asserts its length**, so the release manager finds this rather than a user does. **Whatever is chosen, add the purge step to `docs/release-procedure.md`** - there is currently no purge anywhere in the runbook, and `docs/release-smoke-test.md` only mentions a purge in passing for public pages. **Note for whoever picks this up:** there is no purge script in the repo and no Cloudflare dashboard access from a session, so today this is a step only Lutan can do - which is itself an argument for (a) or (b). See `docs/releases/2026-10-17-0-36-0.md`. -> *Deployment (before go-live)*

Do: have `deploy-pi.sh` bound or prune `.next/cache` (and say what the ceiling should be), and establish whether it grows every release or did so once. **The cheap diagnostic to write into the runbook: when one clone builds and its twin does not on the same machine, `du -sh .next .next/cache node_modules` on both before theorising about the machine** — one command, and it would have ended this at the first failure instead of the fourth. Cost: three unplanned interventions from Lutan, two of them on wrong diagnoses. `docs/releases/2026-10-19.md`. **Moved to Next up 2026-10-19** from Deployment, because this is the actual fix for the Pi deploy blocker while the item it supersedes sat above it still saying the cause was unknown. **It supersedes the peak-memory measurement and the `ignoreBuildErrors` route on *The Pi build runs out of memory…*, both withdrawn there.** Drop the peak-memory step from `docs/release-procedure.md` in the same PR, and say in the decision file why a build cache is invisible to `free`.

- [ ] **The Pi build runs out of memory at the TypeScript stage and deploys can no longer get through — CAUSE FOUND 2026-10-19: the Turbopack build cache, not the typecheck. NOT BLOCKING any more; the fix is owned by the cache item in Next up and what is left here is bookkeeping.** Found 2026-10-17 by the release. `./scripts/pi/deploy-pi.sh` compiled successfully (55s production, 51s test) and was then killed by the kernel during `Running TypeScript ...` on **both clones, on the first attempt**, succeeding on a plain retry with nothing changed. The Pi has 4 GB RAM and 2 GB swap; `free -m` showed **174 MB free** mid-build and 3.5 GB available after the kill, so the build itself exhausted memory. **Eleven previous releases built fine - nothing about the Pi changed, the app did**: this release added the 121-screen phone-width sweep, the stories pages and the name-card scanning routes, so the typecheck holds more than it ever has. Two clones failing first time is not bad luck; **expect it to fail from now on.** **Why it matters more than a retry suggests:** `deploy-pi.sh` builds into a fresh `.next` before swapping, so the service keeps serving and **a failed build is quiet** - `lanna-care` stayed `active`, the clone source was already fetched to the release SHA, and only the *served version* gave it away (the runbook's "a git-updated clone is not a deployed clone" trap, met for real). During the window production served `0.34.0` from the Pi while the Worker served `0.35.0` **and the mail announcing `0.35.0` had already gone out**, so the announcement briefly preceded the thing it described. Nothing broke for users, and schema ahead of code is the safe direction. **Deliberately not done during the release:** no `NODE_OPTIONS` cap, no swap change, no `deploy-pi.sh` edit - changing how production builds to work around a fault found in that release is how a small problem becomes a shipped one. **Options to weigh in the PR:** (a) cap V8's heap for the build (`NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=...`) so it collects rather than grows until the kernel kills it - cheapest, and the standard fix for an OOM-kill; (b) enlarge the Pi's swap; (c) **drop the typecheck from the Pi build entirely**, since `gates.mjs` and CI have both already typechecked the same commit before it can be deployed, which removes the heaviest stage rather than accommodating it. (c) looks strongest but needs a clear answer to "what if someone deploys a ref CI never saw", which `--ref` makes possible. **Whichever is chosen, make a failed build loud**: the release manager should not have to notice it from `/api/version`. Needs a test plan that exercises a deliberately failing build and shows the operator is told. **ESCALATED 2026-10-17, same day: a later deploy was killed THREE TIMES IN A ROW and the release stalled.** The morning's "succeeds on a plain retry" is **no longer true** — the production release manager session hit attempt 1, 2 and 3 all killed, with the test Worker finishing clean alongside. **So this is now a blocker, not a nuisance, and retrying is not a workaround.** **Two corrections to the options above, both found while advising on the stall:** (1) **There is no separate typecheck step to drop.** `deploy-pi.sh` runs `npm ci` then `npm run build`, and `build` is plain `next build`; the "Running TypeScript ..." stage is *inside* it. So option (c) is **not** deleting a line from the script — it means `typescript: { ignoreBuildErrors: true }` in `next.config.ts`, which today carries a deliberate `tsconfigPath` switch keyed on `NODE_ENV` and a comment explaining why. Any such change must be **gated so it only applies to the Pi build** and must not weaken `gates.mjs` or CI, and the `--ref` hole ("what if someone deploys a ref CI never saw") still needs its answer — most cheaply by making `deploy-pi.sh` refuse, or warn loudly, for a ref CI has not passed. (2) **The immediate workaround recommended was MORE SWAP, not a build change** (`fallocate` a temporary 4 GB `/swapfile2`, `swapon`, retry, and `swapoff`/`rm` afterwards), precisely because it leaves the build untouched — same inputs, same artefact, just headroom — where a `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size` cap changes how the build runs even though it should not change what it produces. If swap turns out to be what unblocked it, say so in the PR: it is evidence the fix is about headroom rather than a runaway. **Still true and still the point: make a failed build LOUD.** The morning's half-deployed state (Pi on `0.34.0`, Worker on `0.35.0`, announcement already mailed) was only visible from the served version, and this second failure was again found by a person watching, not by the tooling. **OUTCOME 2026-10-17, `0.36.0` shipped: MORE SWAP WAS RIGHT, and this item is now about writing it down.** The swap recommendation above is exactly what unblocked it, so record the evidence: the test clone was killed **four times running** (attempts 2-4 identical re-runs, two dying earlier than the first, during `Creating an optimized production build` rather than the typecheck), with **3.5-3.6 GB of the Pi's 4 GB free between attempts** and the largest processes on the box being the Next server at 74 MB and `cloudflared` at 30 MB. So it was never contention or a leak - the build's appetite exceeds the machine. **Lutan then increased swap from 2 GB to 6 GB** (a 4 GB file-backed `/swapfile2` beside the existing 2 GB of zram, in `swapon --show`); the next test build completed and the production build succeeded **first time**. **This is evidence the fault is headroom, not a runaway**, as the swap recommendation predicted - and note zram is compressed RAM and adds little real headroom, so it is the **file-backed** swap that did it. **A restart was asked about and correctly rejected**: it reclaims memory that is already free, the box had been up 15 days without leaking, and it briefly drops the Pi as production's origin for no gain. **WHAT IS LEFT, and it is urgent for a different reason than before:** the fix is **deployed by hand and undocumented**. `/swapfile2` is not in `scripts/pi/setup.sh` or `docs/pi-hosting.md`, so **a rebuilt Pi goes straight back to failing and nothing in the repo explains the number**. (1) Put the swapfile in `setup.sh` and document *why* that size. (2) Make `deploy-pi.sh` (or `guard-release.mjs`) **refuse or warn loudly below ~6 GB of swap** - that is the cheapest way to satisfy the standing "make a failed build LOUD" requirement, because the precondition is checkable before the build rather than after. (3) The `ignoreBuildErrors` route is still worth doing on its merits: swap only buys headroom and the app grows every release. See `docs/releases/2026-10-17-0-36-0.md` Defect 1, and note the `0.36.0` handover **withdraws "budget one retry"** as a remedy. **CONFIRMED 2026-10-17 evening: a temporary 4 GB swap file got the deploy through, first try, with nothing else changed.** Lutan: *"yes it made it through after we added the swap"*. **That is the strongest evidence on this item and it points at (c), not (a).** The reasoning, so nobody re-runs it: the Pi has **4 GB RAM + 2 GB swap = 6 GB**, and the build was killed **three times in a row** at that size, then succeeded once ~4 GB more swap was available. **So the build's peak is somewhere above 6 GB** — on a 4 GB machine. Consequences for the three options: **(a) capping V8's heap looks WRONG, or at least unproven** — a cap below what the typecheck genuinely needs converts a kernel kill into a clean heap-OOM, not a success, and nothing here suggests a runaway that would collect if pushed; **(b) enlarging swap permanently WORKS but means a 4 GB machine permanently carrying 4+ GB of disk-backed memory** for one stage of one command, slow and wearing on the disk; **(c) dropping the typecheck from the Pi build removes the demand instead of housing it**, and the same commit has already been typechecked twice (local `gates.mjs`, then CI) before it can be deployed. **(c) is now the recommendation, not merely "looks strongest".** **One measurement would settle it and nobody has taken it:** capture the actual peak on the next Pi build (`/usr/bin/time -v npm run build` reports *Maximum resident set size*, or sample `free -m` through the run) and write the number on this item. If the peak turns out to be only a little over 6 GB, (b) is defensible as a stopgap; if it is well over, (c) is the only honest answer. **Do the measurement before the fix, not after** — the morning's item already guessed at causes twice and was corrected twice. **PARTLY CLOSED 2026-10-18 (claude/pi-deploy-safety): (1) done - `/swapfile2` is in `setup.sh` step 2b and `docs/pi-hosting.md` "Swap" explains the size; (2) done - `deploy-pi.sh` refuses below ~5.5 GiB of swap, and refuses a production/uat commit not on `origin/main`. STILL OPEN: (3) `ignoreBuildErrors` waits on the peak-memory measurement, now a step in `docs/release-procedure.md`; threshold in `docs/decisions/2026-10-18-pi-deploy-safety.md`. Not run on a real Pi yet.** **CAUSE FOUND 2026-10-19 (Lutan, during `0.37.0`), and it supersedes the recommendation above: the Turbopack build cache was starving the machine, not the app’s appetite.** The production clone’s `.next/cache` had reached 4.4 GB on a 4 GB Pi while the test clone’s was 1.2 GB and built first time every attempt; clearing it took `.next` from 4.9 GB to 450 MB and the next build compiled in 52 s. The fix now belongs to **`deploy-pi.sh` lets the Turbopack build cache grow…** (moved to Next up, 2026-10-19). **Three conclusions on this item are WITHDRAWN, do not act on them:** (1) **the peak-memory measurement is no longer worth taking** — it would have measured a machine starved by a cache, not a build needing more than 6 GB, and the cache item withdraws it as a step from `docs/release-procedure.md`; (2) **option (c) `ignoreBuildErrors` is not the answer**, because the kills happened during *compilation*, before the typecheck ran at all — so it would not have saved a single one of them; (3) **“the build’s peak is somewhere above 6 GB” is wrong**: the extra swap that appeared to fix `0.36.0` bought headroom against the same growing cache, which is why more swap and a reboot both failed on 2026-10-19. **What this item keeps, and why it stays open:** the `/swapfile2` entry in `setup.sh` and the pre-build swap check in `deploy-pi.sh` are done, are cheap, and stay — but the standing **“make a failed build LOUD”** requirement is still unmet in the case that actually happened, since four kernel kills were again noticed by a person watching rather than by the tooling. That is all that is left here.

- [x] **`git show <rev>:<path>` silently returns an error instead of the file when the path starts with a dot, and the error reads exactly like "the content is not there".** Found 2026-10-13 while checking whether a merged change had survived on `main`. Git Bash's MSYS layer treats an argument containing `:` as a Windows path-list and rewrites it — `/` becomes `\`, `:` becomes `;` — so `git show origin/main:.claude/skills/plan-day/SKILL.md` reaches git as `origin\main;.claude\skills\plan-day\SKILL.md` and dies with *fatal: ambiguous argument*. **Measured, and the trigger is narrow:** `package.json`, `docs/backlog.md` and `src/lib/status/health.ts` all work; `.claude/skills/plan-day/SKILL.md` and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` both break. It is the **leading dot** — which is exactly where the skills, the workflows and the settings live. **Why it is worth an item rather than a shrug:** the failure is *invisible* when piped. `git show <rev>:<path> | grep -c "something"` prints `0`, which is indistinguishable from the file genuinely not containing it, and `| grep ...` with no match prints nothing at all. On 2026-10-13 this had me conclude that PR #557's pre-push test-plan block had been reverted from `main` by `ecfa5da5` three hours after it merged. **It had not** — `git grep -c "pre-push" origin/main -- .claude/skills/plan-day/SKILL.md` returns `1`, and `ecfa5da5` changed nothing in that file except backslash paths. A session that did not double-check would have "found" a regression that never happened, and the obvious next move — restoring the block — would have been a real corruption of `main`. **Three fixes, all verified on the failing path 2026-10-13:** prefix the command with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1`, or with `MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*'`, or avoid the colon form altogether — `git grep <pattern> <rev> -- <path>` and `git ls-tree -r <rev> --name-only -- <path>` are both immune and are usually what you actually wanted. **Done when:** the rule is written where a session reads it before reaching for the colon form (`AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`), stated as "never trust an empty result from `git show <rev>:<path>` in this shell — use `git grep`/`git ls-tree`, or prefix `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1`". This is the same family as the backslash-eating bug fixed by `ecfa5da5` on 2026-10-12: **the shell rewrites arguments before the program sees them**, and both bugs cost real time because the symptom pointed at the wrong thing. [done 2026-10-13: rule + reproduction in `CLAUDE.md` ("A trap in this shell"), `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` / `git grep` / `git ls-tree`.]

- [x] **BUG: the Website visitors tile still says *Not set up* on production, and `0.25.0`'s release note told every admin it works.** Reported by Lutan 2026-10-10, straight after the `0.25.0` deploy, and **confirmed on the Pi the same day**. **This is not the bug #518 fixed.** #518 (`pi-visitor-count`, in `0.25.0`) fixed the *plumbing*: one shared `OPTIONAL_SECRETS` list so `scripts/pi/write-env.mjs` copies optional secrets into the Pi's `.env.production.local`, which it had not been doing (`docs/decisions/2026-10-10-one-optional-secrets-list.md`). **That half works** — `BACKUP_DRIVE_FOLDER_ID` is in the Pi's generated file today, proving the mechanism. **What was never checked is whether the two Cloudflare values exist anywhere `write-env.mjs` can see them. So `write-env.mjs:95` (`PI_OPTIONAL_SECRETS.filter((k) => env[k])`) has nothing to write, `src/lib/status/usage.ts:108-109` reads `undefined` for both, and the tile correctly renders its grey *Not set up* state. **The tile is behaving exactly as designed; the values are simply not there.** **The likely root cause** is that the pair was only ever set as **Cloudflare Worker secrets** (`wrangler secret put`), which `scripts/deploy.mjs` hands to the Worker directly. The Worker is the *fallback*; the **Pi serves the pages**, and the Pi cannot read a wrangler secret — it reads local env files. The decision note's phrase "with both values configured" means configured *as Worker secrets*, and that is the gap. **Fix:** (1) confirm whether the pair exists as Worker secrets at all (`npx.cmd wrangler secret list --env production`) and whether the token is still valid — it may never have been created, or may have expired; (2) put both into the Pi's `.env.deploy.production` (the production values file, mode 0600, gitignored) so `write-env.mjs` picks them up on the next `deploy-pi.sh`; (3) **add a check that fails loudly rather than rendering grey** — the whole failure mode here is that "not configured" and "configured but not reaching the reader" look identical on screen. `src/lib/status/run.ts:79` already knows the key name; the System status page should distinguish *no token set* from *token set but the API refused*. (4) re-run `scripts/pi/deploy-pi.sh` and confirm a number appears. **Also decide what to do about the note.** `0.25.0` is a major release, so its note *"Settings → System status: the Website visitors tile now shows how many people visited the website, instead of saying Not set up"* was **mailed to every admin and is false**. The mail cannot be unsent. Either fix this before anyone looks, or carry a correcting line in `0.26.0`'s notes. **Lesson for the release checklist:** a release note that asserts a *configuration-dependent* thing now works needs someone to look at the live screen before the cut, not after. `docs/test-plans/pi-visitor-count.md` left exactly that as `pending:` and it was shipped on the ship-and-record call. **[FIXED 2026-10-10, same day, configuration only — no code change, no release, no version bump.]** The diagnosis above was right: both values were present on the PC in `.env.deploy.production` (which is how the Worker had them) and absent from the Pi, which is what serves the pages. Before changing anything the token was verified against Cloudflare’s API — `user/tokens/verify` returned `status=active`, and the app’s own GraphQL query returned real numbers — so the fix could not land into the same grey state. The two lines were then copied to the production Pi’s `.env.deploy.production` (piped over ssh so no value was ever printed; the file was backed up first as `.env.deploy.production.bak-20261010` and its `0600` mode is unchanged), and `scripts/pi/deploy-pi.sh --ref 590a9d35` was re-run — **pinned to the `0.25.0` release commit, so no unreviewed code shipped with the config fix.** Verified three ways: the generated `.env.production.local` now carries both keys; the app’s exact query, run on the Pi itself against the Pi’s own generated env, returned **5364 page views and 663 uniques over 7 days**; and **Lutan confirmed in chat that the tile is live**. **`0.25.0`’s fifth note is therefore true and needs no correcting line in `0.26.0`.** **Two things deliberately NOT done, both still open and worth their own items:** (1) **test is still unfixed** — the test Pi has neither value and there is no `.env.deploy.test` on the PC, so `test.lannacare.org` still shows *Not set up*; the token is zone-wide so the same pair would work. (2) ~~**The screen still cannot distinguish “no key set” from “key set but the API refused”**~~ — **WRONG, corrected 2026-10-11. #522 already did this, in this same stream. Do not file it and do not build it.** `src/lib/status/usage.ts` now returns which of the two key names is missing, which machine answered (`worker` / `pi` / `local`, the Pi marked by `PHOTO_CACHE_DIR`, which `write-env.mjs` gives only a Pi) and the file to fix; **on production a missing value is red, not grey**, because the count was promised there, and **one of the pair without the other is red anywhere**. An API refusal was already red, carrying Cloudflare's own message. So the two states are distinguishable and carry different text. See `docs/decisions/2026-10-10-visitor-count-live.md`, §*The tile now says where the value is missing*, and the comment at `usage.ts:125-131`, which says it in as many words: *"not configured" and "configured on the wrong machine" must not look the same*. Keep the postcode and country on the wrap so both tax regimes see a complete address. **DECIDED 2026-10-09, and it REVERSES the line above: the receipt does NOT read `site_content.contact_address`. Hard-code the issuer address in the code.** Lutan: *"keep that address separate to the website field, too dangerous for someone to accidentally change the field and corrupt receipts start being produced."* **His reasoning is the right way round and should not be re-litigated:** Settings → Website is editable by management for public-facing copy, and a receipt is a financial document that may go to a tax authority. Sharing one field means a harmless website tidy-up silently changes every receipt issued afterwards, and **nothing on any screen would report it** — the receipts would simply be wrong, after they had been sent. The value of a setting is that it is easy to change; that is precisely the property a registered address must not have. **The cost, accepted: changing it needs a developer and a deploy.** That is proportionate for an address that changes about once a decade, and the deploy is the review step. **THE REAL RISK IS NOW A FUTURE SESSION "FIXING" THIS.** A hard-coded address looks exactly like an oversight, and the obvious improvement is to move it into Settings, which would reintroduce the hazard without anyone noticing. So **every Drive upload on that environment is failing** (resident photos, hero, logos, project photos, backups), not just this one. Different from the dev-only `invalid_client` seen 2026-09-24 (a dead client); `invalid_grant` means the refresh token itself was revoked or expired. Usual reasons: the OAuth consent screen of the Drive client's project is in *Testing* (refresh tokens die after 7 days), the Google account's password was changed or access removed, or a newer refresh token was issued for the same client and account (Google keeps a limited number). **Fix:** (1) find the reason in the Drive client's Google Cloud project (under the account that owns the Drive; see the 90-day-token item too), publish the consent screen if it is in Testing, (2) mint a new refresh token and set it as the Worker secret for the affected environment (and `.dev.vars` / `.env.local` locally), (3) redeploy and retry the logo upload. **Code follow-ups, same PR or next:** show staff a plain message ("Photo storage is not connected — tell an admin") instead of Google's raw text, and make sure a failed logo upload doesn't throw away the rest of the Shelter Friend form; report it on the release/health check (e.g. a Drive token check in `scripts/` or the admin page) so an expired token shows up before a user hits it. **Fixed 2026-09-25 (token):** cause confirmed. The Drive client "Lanna Care Drive Access" (Desktop, created 2026-09-18) lives in the lanna account's project **Lanna Care - Dev** (`lanna-care-dev`), which was still in *Testing*, so its refresh token expired 7 days later, on 2026-09-25. The v0.5.0 deploy was not involved (no secret changes in `wrangler deployments list`). Published the project (logo removed, since a logo forces verification; home page `https://lannacare.org` and privacy `https://lannacare.org/privacy` added; `lannacare.org` added as an authorised domain), minted a new token, and set it in `.env.local` and as `GOOGLE_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN` on the `production` and `test` Workers. Also removed a stray space after `=` on the Google keys in `.env.local`. Lutan retested the Shelter Friend logo upload on lannacare.org 2026-09-25: works. **Code follow-ups done 2026-09-26** (`claude/drive-upload-errors`): a dead token or client now raises `DriveNotConnectedError`, and every upload (logo, Website photos, resident/project/maintenance photos, attachments) and Drive folder sync says "Photo storage is not connected — tell an admin.", with Google's text going to the server log. The form itself was never lost (the logo uploads on its own, apart from Save, and the draft survives), but its message showed below Save, out of sight; it now sits by the logo. Settings (`/admin`) shows whether Drive is connected, and `scripts/check-drive-token.mjs` checks an env file.

Overlaps Dashboard follow-ups (g) and part 4 of the redesign. **SUPERSEDED IN PART 2026-10-07:** the Director and Lutan answered the "decide the source of each" half — **enter a baseline and a date in Settings and count forward** (see *Impact figures as a baseline plus a live count*, Management), and **community/temple dogs need building first** (see *Record community and temple dogs helped*, Resident operations). **What is left here is the band itself** once those two land. **THE HOOK-LINE HALF IS DONE — `2449d7b0` (2026-09-27, "Pet of the week card shows the resident's hook line"), verified 2026-10-08 by `/plan-day` before a stream was created.** `src/app/page.tsx:174` has `hook_line` in the `public_resident_profiles` select, line 185 reads it with `localizedField(locale, featured?.hook_line, featured?.translations, "hook_line")`, and line 186 keeps `bodyLead(bio, 160)` as the fallback — all three things this item asked for, shipped **eleven days** before the note describing them as outstanding was still being read as current. **The rest of this item stands:** the three missing figures, of which *rehomed* is answered by `impact_baselines` / `public_impact_figures` (`0156`), *sterilisations* has no source (checked — nothing records them), and *community and temple dogs* need the Resident-operations item built first. **The new wrinkle worth carrying: this was a stale HALF of a live item, not a stale item.** The staleness sweep ticked whole items and could not see this. **When checking an item, check each of its parts.** **UPDATE 2026-10-08 — the second of the three figures now has a source, leaving one.** *Rehomed* was already answered by `impact_baselines` / `public_impact_figures` (`0156`). ***Sterilisations* was recorded here as having no source at all ("checked — nothing records them"); the Director's answers to the community-dogs paper give it one**: every outing note carries a *sterilised* tick, and she ruled both that "sterilised should count towards web totals" and that temple sterilisations count in this figure as well as in the community-dogs one. So the sterilisations figure becomes a count over the same outing rows, and **both remaining figures now depend on the single community-dogs build** rather than on two separate unknowns. Nothing here can be built until that lands. **UPDATE 2026-10-09 (`community-dogs-schema`, migration `0169`): both remaining figures now have their source in the database.** `public_impact_figures` counts `community_dogs` as `sum(dog_count)` and `villages_sterilised` as `sum(sterilised_count)` over `community_dog_outings` after each baseline date. A ticked *sterilised* also records how many dogs, so an outing that feeds twenty dogs and sterilises three adds three, not twenty. Both figures stay hidden until someone enters a baseline, and no outing can be recorded until the phone form (`community-dogs`, batch 81) exists. **What is left here is the band itself:** two more tiles in `src/lib/site/impact.ts`, read from `public_impact_figures`. **DONE 2026-10-09 (`community-dogs`): the band takes all three figures.** Both remaining figures read `public_impact_figures` through the existing `impactFigureStats()`, so no new tile code was needed; the band itself now wraps up to seven tiles in rows of four with a centred last row (`src/app/page.tsx`), checked at 375 px and desktop with six. *Sterilisations in local villages* counts outreach notes' `sterilised_count` (verified on dev: a 12-dog note with 3 sterilised moved 300 to 303). - [x] **Give the public site some life: spring motion on text and content blocks.** Lutan, 2026-09-26: some public websites have a "springy" feel to their text blocks, and the public pages should feel less static. **What it means here:** headings, text blocks and cards ease into place as they scroll into view (a short rise and fade with a slight spring overshoot, staggered within a group), and interactive cards (the "How you can help" cards, resident cards, Shelter Friend logos, buttons) give a small springy lift on hover and press. Subtle, not a show: short distances, around 300 to 600 ms, each block animates once. **How:** prefer plain CSS with the `linear()` easing function (it can express a real spring curve) and an `IntersectionObserver` that adds a class, so there is no animation library and almost no bundle cost. Reach for a library (e.g. `motion`) only if something needs physics CSS cannot fake, and say why in `docs/decisions.md`. **Must:** respect `prefers-reduced-motion` (no movement at all, content simply present), never hide content from anyone without JavaScript or from search engines (start visible and animate only once JS has run, or make the no-JS state the final one), no layout shift, and keep the staff app itself calm (public pages only). **When:** build it on the redesigned components, so after `public-site-shell` (batch 2 of the 2026-09-25 plan). It can ride with or follow `public-site-home`. First, agree the feel with Lutan on one section (e.g. the "How you can help" cards) with two or three variants in a preview before rolling it across the site. Reference sites Lutan likes would help; ask for a link.

Draw an original dog (ideally the shelter's logo dog, or a dog and a cat taking turns) as a looping run cycle. **Format:** an animated SVG (CSS keyframes on a few shapes) or a Lottie file rather than a GIF, so it is tiny, crisp at any size, recolourable to the redesign palette, and can be paused. **Where it shows:** the public pages' `loading.tsx` (Next's route-level loading UI) and client-side route changes, plus any wait over about a second such as a form submit or a photo upload. The staff app gets it too (Lutan, 2026-09-26): a small inline version for uploads and slow pages, not a full-screen overlay. **Behaviour:** appear only after a short delay (about 300 ms) so fast navigations don't flash it, and have an accessible label ("Loading", en and th) with `role="status"`. - [ ] **Who does what: the purchasing job KEEPS reading stock receipts through `stock.delivery`'s table — DECIDED 2026-10-19 by Lutan. NO SCHEMA. What is left is teaching the probe that the read is shared, which is a scripts-only change.** `stock_receipts_select_perm` asks `stock.delivery` OR `stock.purchasing`, on purpose: `0143` and `scripts/check-2ic-role.mjs` rely on a role with only the purchasing job reading what it needs. The cost is that `check-who-does-what.mjs` reports `stock.delivery` as impossible to take away from Management and the 2IC, and the grid cannot show that. **Decide:** keep it (and teach the probe that the read is shared), or give the purchasing job its own read, such as a view of receipts since the last count, so the table policy can ask `stock.delivery` alone. Also record that `reference.add_while_recording` is not a defect: a medication insert is legitimately open under `stock.medications` Edit as well, so the probe cannot tell the two cells apart; give the probe a way to say so, or accept it as a standing entry. **DECIDED 2026-10-19 (Lutan): *"yes fine to keep."*** So `stock_receipts_select_perm` stays as it is, asking `stock.delivery` OR `stock.purchasing`, and **the second branch of this item — giving the purchasing job its own read, such as a view of receipts since the last count — is dropped. Do not build it, and do not reopen the question.** `0143` and `scripts/check-2ic-role.mjs` keep working untouched, and **there is no migration here**: what looked like "decision, then maybe schema" is now scripts only. **What is left, and it is small:** `scripts/check-who-does-what.mjs` currently reports `stock.delivery` as impossible to take away from Management and the 2IC, because the shared read makes the probe unable to tell the two cells apart. **Teach the probe to say "this read is shared with `stock.purchasing`, on purpose" rather than reporting it as a cell that cannot be removed**, and make the grid able to show that, so a true statement replaces a misleading one. **Do `reference.add_while_recording` in the same change** — this item already pairs them, and it is the identical shape: a medication insert is legitimately open under `stock.medications` Edit as well, so the probe cannot distinguish the two cells there either. **Give the probe one way to express "deliberately shared" and use it for both**, rather than special-casing each. If a standing entry turns out to be the honest answer for either, say so in the PR with the reason instead of engineering around it. **Sizing:** scripts only, no schema, no app change, no migration — a quick win, and a good fold with other `scripts/` work.

## Security

- [x] **Replace the service-role client in the Add Shelter Photos route with narrow database functions (security hardening; Lutan, 2026-10-17).** `src/app/api/photos/shelter/[id]/route.ts` used the RLS-bypassing client only to read, and when null write, `residents.drive_folder_id`. Protection was a convention ("asks for one column"), on the volunteer path. Replace with functions that check `photos.shelter_add` inside and keep the null guard, then remove the file from the allow-list in `eslint.config.mjs`. Migration 0219. **Done: 0219, PR for `claude/service-role-folder-schema`; the file is off the allow-list.**
- [x] **Two check harnesses CRASH before asserting anything, and neither runs in CI, so the protections they guard are unwatched (scripts; found 2026-10-16 by `/plan-day`).** Distinct from *Thirteen dev check harnesses still red*, which lists reds that each need a decision: these two never get as far as an assertion, and neither needs a ruling. (a) **`check-cards-schema.mjs`** dies immediately with `Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module 'C:\Development\Animal_Shelter_App\src\lib\permissions\jobs' imported from src/lib/permissions/cards.ts` — an extensionless import that Next's resolver accepts and plain `node` does not, so the script cannot load `cards.ts` at all. **This is the guard on the card set**, which `CLAUDE.md` and the planner handover both say must stay at twenty-one and must never grow on a stream's initiative; it has been unwatched for an unknown period. (b) **`check-permission-parity.mjs`** dies with `harness did not return a result (status 400): Failed to run sql query: ERROR: 23505: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "residents_resident_code_key"` — its `do $$ … $$` harness inserts a test resident whose code already exists on dev, so it is stale dev data from an earlier run that did not roll back, not a code fault. Note this script is ALSO listed in the thirteen-harnesses item for a real content red (the recorded paper-vs-draft doctor disagreement, 21 lines); that red is a separate matter and is **not** in scope here — the job is only to make the harness run again so the content red becomes visible. **Both were hit independently by `calendar-and-weigh-schema` (#655), which reported them in its PR, and confirmed still broken on 2026-10-16.** **Do:** (1) fix (a) by giving the import an extension or whatever the repo's other scripts do to load `src/` modules under plain node — check how a working `check-*.mjs` does it rather than inventing a pattern; (2) fix (b) by making the harness's fixture resident code unique per run, or by deleting its leftover row first, so it is re-runnable — the existing harnesses' `begin … rollback` pattern is the model; (3) **decide whether either belongs in CI.** Neither is in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` today, which is why both could break silently; if a guard on the card set is worth having, it is worth running. Say what you concluded either way, because "not in CI" is currently indistinguishable from "deliberately local". (4) Run each and confirm it goes **green or reaches a real assertion**, not merely that it starts — the lesson of `check-harness-repair`. **Blocks** *Retire the `facility.map` activity*, which has to edit fixtures in `check-cards-schema.mjs`, `check-perm-convert-settings.mjs` and `check-permission-parity.mjs` and cannot verify them while two of the three will not run. → *Security* **Done 2026-10-16 (`claude/check-harness-crashes`).** (a) loads via the same resolver hook as `check-multi-role-build.mjs`; reports the set is still twenty-one, and goes red with a 22nd. (b) fixture residents get explicit per-run codes; it now runs and reports RED for the recorded 21 doctor lines plus four `[STALE]` N4 entries and `maintenance.bills` unprobed, which are for the thirteen-harnesses item. Neither goes in CI (needs the dev token): `docs/decisions/2026-10-16-check-harness-crashes.md`. **Unblocks** *Retire the `facility.map` activity*.
- [x] **Run the twenty-one-card count in CI without a database (scripts/CI; found 2026-10-16 by `check-harness-crashes`).** `check-cards-schema.mjs` needs the dev token, so CI cannot run it, but its first assertion (`CARD_KEYS.length === 21`, and every card names a real activity) reads only `cards.ts` and `catalogue.ts`. Split that part into a DB-free script and add it to `ci.yml` as an advisory job (not a required check; that is branch protection and Lutan's call). Decision: `docs/decisions/2026-10-16-check-harness-crashes.md`. → *Security* **DONE 2026-10-16:** `scripts/check-cards-count.mjs` plus a `cards-count` job in `ci.yml` (no `continue-on-error`; not a required check — Lutan's call). `docs/decisions/2026-10-16-cards-count-in-ci-and-worktree-ports.md`.
- [x] **The three website tables (`site_content`, `site_pages`, `site_content_photos`) are readable by every login, not just the website editors — including the public-viewer and clinic logins, and including `clinic_visit_estimate`, which the public view hides.** From the 2026-10-13 database review (F2), ranked its second finding. `public_read_site_*` (`0018`, `0059`) are `using (true)`; `0122` only revoked `anon`, so every authenticated role still reads them. Replace them with `(select has_permission('website.content', 'read'))`; the `public_site_*` views keep the public read, so nothing a visitor sees changes. **Migration: yes, small. Read needs website.content Read or reports.cashflow Read, because the forecast reads the estimate.**

No script sets app.actor yet; the fallback is ready for them.**
- [x] **`maintenance_bills.bill_date` defaults to the UTC day, and two round-status views nobody reads filter on `CURRENT_DATE`.** From the 2026-10-13 database review (W1). `0189` wrote `default current_date` where `0073`'s `shelter_today()` is the rule; the forms send a date, so **only a direct insert is dated a day early, and only before 07:00 Thai**. `prescription_round_status`, `resident_diet_round_status` and `frequency_round_status` (`0137`/`0138`) **have no reader anywhere in `src/` or `worker/`**: drop them, or move them to `shelter_today()` if they are wanted — say which and why. **Migration: yes, about ten lines. Ten minutes.** **Filed 2026-10-14 on Lutan's instruction.** **Fold this into the same schema PR as F2 and F4** — all three are small migrations and only one may be in flight at a time. → *Security* **Done: 0195. Views kept and moved to shelter_today(): scripts read them.**

- [ ] **The app's `x-origin-key` check is in the code but NOT yet active on the Pi — it needs a Pi deploy (found 2026-10-12 while closing review S1).** #551 added the check to `src/proxy.ts` so the Pi refuses a request that reaches `pi.lannacare.org` without the shared secret, rather than trusting the Cloudflare WAF rule alone. `pi-token-off` then copied `ORIGIN_KEY` into the Pi's `.env.deploy.production` on 2026-10-12, so the value is in place. **But the Pi is serving `0.27.0`, which predates #551, so nothing on the Pi checks the header today.** It starts working at the next Pi deploy (`./scripts/pi/deploy-pi.sh`) and not before. **Why this is worth its own item:** the protection reads as shipped — the code is on `main`, the secret is on the Pi, the PR is merged and its test plan is signed — and the only record that it is not yet live is one row of that test plan's manual table, where no planner or release pass would ever see it. Until the deploy happens, an edited, disabled or displaced WAF rule still puts the Pi's `next start` in front of anyone who finds the hostname, which is precisely what #551 was for. **Done when** a Pi deploy carrying #551 has happened and a request to the Pi without the header is confirmed refused (the test clone uses the same key, so it can be checked there first). No code change expected. See `docs/decisions/2026-10-12-pi-checks-origin-key.md` and `docs/test-plans/pi-token-off.md` row 5. **Staleness sweep 2026-10-14:** the Pi deploy this waits for has happened: the Pi served `0.28.0` (`b5fd020d`) and then `0.29.0` (`9cb36eea`) on 2026-10-13 (`docs/releases/2026-10-13.md`), and both contain #551. So "the Pi is serving 0.27.0" is out of date. What remains is the confirmation: a request to the Pi without the header is refused. No release record or test plan shows that yet.

**Moved above Deployment on 2026-09-30 (Lutan): severity governs here, not
file position.** The review appended this section at the end of the file,
which by this file's own convention ("ordered by suggested priority") read as

From the 2026-09-30 security assessment (`docs/security/security-assessment-2026-09-30.docx`, `.pdf`; commit d26103b, release 0.10.0). Finding IDs (DB-n, CODE-n, WEB-n) are the report's. No Critical finding; one High. Items are grouped so each is one stream; schema items are `claude/<name>-schema` PRs first, per the migrations rules. Effort is the report's. None of these makes the app harder for field staff.

- [x] **A vet login can read, rename, add and delete every project and maintenance photo record (Medium).** **Done 2026-10-09** (`0174_close_the_remaining_over_grants.sql`, `claude/close-the-remaining-over-grants`; `docs/decisions/2026-10-09-clinic-login-allow-lists.md`): the four `doctor_*_attachments` policies name only `resident`, `blood_test` and `procedure`, `doctor_can_write_attachment()` ends `else false`, and `doctor_read_translations` reads residents only. Proved under a doctor JWT by `scripts/check-clinic-allow-lists.mjs` (9 failures before, 18 of 18 after) and the surface probe (doctor attachments read 160 → 14, update/delete 158 → 12, translations 46 → 0). Found 2026-10-09 by the dynamic half of the security assessment (`permission-measure-and-probe`, `scripts/probe-role-surface.mjs`; `docs/security/security-assessment-2026-10-09-dynamic.md`, which has the evidence). The four `vet_*_attachments` policies (`0110`, carried unchanged by `0167`) let a clinic login through for any `owner_type` **not** in `('resident', 'blood_test', 'procedure')`, and `vet_can_write_attachment()` ends `else true`, so project and maintenance photos fall through. Under a vet's JWT on dev it read 144 project and 2 maintenance rows, renamed all 144, deleted all 146 and inserted a new project attachment. `vet_read_translations` has the same shape (`table_name <> 'residents'`), so the vet also reads the Thai text of maintenance jobs, recurring jobs, project folders, Shelter Friends and site pages. Not in the roles paper's C table, and not what the 2026-10-07 "leave vets as they are" decision was about: that kept the vet's clinical access, and project photos are the public site's pictures. **DECIDED 2026-10-09 by Lutan: no — lock it to clinical records only.** Turn the five policies into allow-lists naming only `resident`, `blood_test` and `procedure`, drop the `else true` from `vet_can_write_attachment()`, and close `vet_read_translations` the same way — a clinic login has no reason to read the Thai text of maintenance jobs, recurring jobs, project folders, Shelter Friends or site pages. Project photos are the public site's pictures. The original framing is kept below for the reasoning: should a clinic login see project and maintenance photos at all? If not, turn the five policies into allow-lists (name the three clinical types, drop the `else true`) in one small re-runnable migration with a harness under a vet's JWT; about an hour. Does not give the vet any cells. **Raised with Lutan 2026-10-09 by `close-the-over-grants`; not built, waiting for his answer** (the recommendation stands: no, allow-lists). **Names since 0172 (2026-10-09, vet-to-doctor-rename):** the vet login is the **doctor** login, the policies are `doctor_*_attachments` / `doctor_read_translations`, and the function is `doctor_can_write_attachment()`; the rename changed no behaviour here, so the finding stands.

- [x] **`reset_prescription_rounds()`, `reset_frequency_rounds()` and `reset_diet_rounds()` can be called by any signed-in login (Medium-low; silent).** Found 2026-10-09 by the dynamic half of the security assessment (`permission-measure-and-probe`, `scripts/probe-role-surface.mjs`; `docs/security/security-assessment-2026-10-09-dynamic.md`, which has the evidence). They run as their owner, ask nothing about the caller, and are granted to `authenticated` (`0137`, `0138`); only triggers call them, no app code does. As a login with **no role** (which reads 0 prescriptions) `reset_prescription_rounds(<id>)` replaced a prescription's custom rounds with its frequency's defaults: the medication list then shows a dose at the wrong round, and nothing says so. Needs the id (a UUID), so the realistic caller is an archived former volunteer or a vet who has seen one. `check-medication-rounds.mjs` asserts `norole` cannot write `prescription_rounds` through the table, which holds, and never looked through the function. **Fix:** `revoke execute … from authenticated` on the three (the triggers that call them also run as owner, so nothing in the app changes) plus a line in `check-medication-rounds.mjs`. Schema PR; ten minutes. **CLOSED 2026-10-09 (`close-the-over-grants`, `0170` §2, commit 4586418f):** execute revoked from `authenticated` (and `public`, `anon`) on all three; `service_role` keeps it. `check-medication-rounds.mjs` now calls each function under every login with a real id, before it replays `0137`/`0138` (the replay re-grants them inside its transaction): 18 red before, green after.

- [x] **The facility map tables answer every signed-in login, including the public viewer and archived people (Low).** Found 2026-10-09 by the dynamic half of the security assessment (`permission-measure-and-probe`, `scripts/probe-role-surface.mjs`; `docs/security/security-assessment-2026-10-09-dynamic.md`, which has the evidence). `facility_maps_read` (`0142`) and `map_rooms_read` (`0157`) are `to authenticated using (true)`, kept on purpose when the writes converted (`0150`, `0158`), but that reaches `public_viewer`, a login with no role and an archived person, which the app-access gate keeps out of every other internal table. It is the shelter's layout, not personal data. **Fix:** add `has_app_access()` (or `has_shelter_floor()`) to the two read policies, and the two tables to `check-app-access-gate.mjs`. (`rounds` is open the same way, but `check-medication-rounds.mjs` asserts it deliberately and it holds only round names: leave it.) **CLOSED 2026-10-09 (`close-the-over-grants`, `0170` §3, commit f08de41f):** both read policies ask `private.has_app_access()`; `check-app-access-gate.mjs` lists both tables (red before: archived, roleless and `public_viewer` each read 3 `facility_maps` rows; green after). `rounds` left open as the item says.

- [x] **A vet login lists every person with a login, with their role (Low).** **Done 2026-10-09** (`0174`, same PR): `private.app_users` shows a clinic login only itself and the doctors at its current clinics; the volunteer case is unchanged (the harness asserts the volunteer still sees every login an admin does, without emails). The role enum column stays for `perm-drop-enum`. Found 2026-10-09 by the dynamic half of the security assessment (`permission-measure-and-probe`, `scripts/probe-role-surface.mjs`; `docs/security/security-assessment-2026-10-09-dynamic.md`, which has the evidence). `app_users` (`0146`) blanks emails for vets and volunteers but not names, roles or `archived_at`, so an outside clinic sees all 57 logins and who is Admin. - [x] **Next 16.3.5 carries a Critical RCE advisory; the fix is a patch bump that is "outside the stated dependency range" (Critical).** Surfaced 2026-10-01 by the new `audit` job on PR #265, which is — as far as the run history shows — the first PR to execute it: `next 16.2.0 - 16.3.5`, **critical**, *"Next.js: Remote Code Execution in next/og ImageResponse"*, [GHSA-vcvr-r3jv-pc5j](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vcvr-r3jv-pc5j), `fix available via npm audit fix --force`, `Will install next@16.3.8, which is outside the stated dependency range`. `package.json` pins `"next": "16.3.5"`, so **`main`, test and production are all affected equally** — this is not a property of the PR that found it. **Worth putting beside the 2026-09-30 assessment, which recorded "No Critical findings":** that was true of the code, and the first Critical to appear came from the supply chain instead, caught by a job the same security batch added. The chain is what the review could not see by reading the repo. **The mitigating fact, and it is a real one:** `next/og` and `ImageResponse` appear **nowhere** in `src/` or `worker/` (grepped 2026-10-01), so the vulnerable entry point is not reachable in this app — the dependency is vulnerable, the code path is unused. That is the difference between "patch on the next convenient day" and "stop and patch now", and it is why this is a backlog item rather than a hotfix. Do not treat it as safe indefinitely, though: a future feature that wants an Open Graph image would reach for exactly that API, and the person adding it will not know this. **Why it is not a one-line bump:** `AGENTS.md` opens by saying this is a modified Next whose APIs, conventions and file structure may differ from training data, and npm itself reports `16.3.8` as outside the declared range. So it needs its own PR: read `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` and the upstream notes for 16.3.6–16.3.8, bump, run the full gates, and **check the two things this project has already been bitten by around builds** — that `strip-baked-env` still finds and empties `next-env.mjs` (its shape is an OpenNext implementation detail), and that `getSiteOrigin()`'s header reading still behaves on the Pi behind cloudflared, since a sign-in outage on 30 September came from exactly that area. **Also fix the reporting gap this exposed:** `audit` is `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'`, so a push to `main` skips it and nothing reports a new advisory between PRs — an advisory published on a quiet day is invisible until someone happens to open a PR. Its `continue-on-error: true` is correct and should stay (the job's own comment argues the case well, and contrasts it with `test-plan`), but "reported, not enforced" only works if it is actually reported: consider running it on a schedule as well, so a Critical lands somewhere a person sees without a PR to carry it. **Status 2026-10-02:** the bump landed (#268, Next 16.3.8) and the reporting gap is closed by `.github/workflows/advisories.yml` (daily, fails on purpose; docs/decisions/2026-10-02-scheduled-audit-fails-on-purpose.md). **Still open, so not ticked:** `getSiteOrigin()`/sign-in on the Pi behind cloudflared has not been confirmed on 16.3.8 (#268 verified sign-in on a local production build only, and was not deployed). **Status 2026-10-06 (verified by `/plan-day`, not ticked): the Critical is RESOLVED.** `48b1a27a` *"Bump next and eslint-config-next to 16.3.8 for GHSA-vcvr-r3jv-pc5j"* landed the fix, so `package.json` now pins **`next: 16.3.8`** — the version the advisory names — and `npm audit --audit-level=critical` reports **no critical vulnerabilities**. `next/og` and `ImageResponse` are still absent from `src/` and `worker/`, so the re-grep the item asked for still holds. **The 5 high-severity advisories that remain are dev-only:** `npm audit --omit=dev` finds **0 vulnerabilities**; the highs are `fast-glob` reached through `@next/eslint-plugin-next` → `eslint-config-next`, i.e. the lint toolchain, not anything shipped. **Left unticked deliberately** — the item also carries the standing warning that a future Open Graph feature would reach for exactly that API and the person adding it will not know this, so whoever owns Security should decide whether that warning belongs somewhere more durable than a closed backlog item before ticking. **Closed 2026-10-07 (claude/next-og-warning-durable):** the standing warning now has a durable home — `scripts/check-next-og.mjs`, run by `npm run lint`, fails if `next/og`/`ImageResponse`/an OG convention file appears while Next is below 16.3.8 (docs/decisions/2026-10-07-next-og-warning-lives-in-lint.md). Re-verified: `npm audit --omit=dev` 0 vulnerabilities, no `next/og` in `src/` or `worker/`. Not confirmed: `getSiteOrigin()` on the Pi behind cloudflared on 16.3.8 — file separately if still wanted.

- [x] **Encrypt the weekly backup and keep session tables out of it (DB-1, High).** **Done 2026-10-02** (rollout in `docs/decisions/2026-10-02-backup-encryption-rollout.md`, code in #243): key pair made by Lutan, private key in two places only; first encrypted production run on the Pi (`.dump.age`, link not logged); a decrypt rehearsal gave a valid archive with the session and MFA tables absent; old plaintext dumps deleted on the Pi and in Drive, `backup.log` truncated; `Backups/` moved to `Admin/Backups`, shared with Lutan only; every production session and refresh token rotated. - [x] **A high advisory in `sharp` reaches the production tree through the Cloudflare build chain, and the only fix npm offers is a breaking `wrangler` change.** Found 2026-10-07 on PR #405's `audit` job, one day after the `source-map-js` high was closed by #398. **The advisory:** `sharp <0.35.5`, **high**, [GHSA-wq5f-xc86-pv6w](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wq5f-xc86-pv6w) — *Vulnerability in librsvg dependency*, CVE-2026-96889. **How it reaches production:** `@opennextjs/cloudflare@1.20.6` is a **`dependencies`** entry (wrangler itself is only a devDependency, which is why this is easy to misread) → `wrangler@4.135.0` → `miniflare@5.x-alpha` → `sharp@0.35.4`; **`next` also pulls `sharp@0.35.4` directly**. So `npm audit --omit=dev` sees it and `npm run audit:prod` fails. **Why it is not a one-liner:** `npm audit fix --force` reports *"Will install wrangler@4.15.2, which is a breaking change"* — a major move of the Cloudflare build chain, which is how the app is built and deployed. **Do not take that fix inside an unrelated PR**, and weigh a narrower route first: a newer `@opennextjs/cloudflare` that depends on a patched wrangler, a `sharp` bump on its own, or an `overrides` entry pinning `sharp >= 0.35.5` (noting an override pins a transitive dependency behind the maintainer's back and needs removing when upstream catches up). **Reachability is worth establishing before urgency:** the flaw is in **librsvg**, i.e. SVG rendering inside `sharp`. Next only processes SVGs through its image optimiser when `dangerouslyAllowSVG` is set — **check whether it is** — and `miniflare` is the local Worker simulator, which does not run in production. If no untrusted SVG reaches `sharp`, this is *"patch on the next convenient day"* rather than a hotfix, which is exactly the judgement the Next RCE item recorded for `next/og`. **Expect `advisories.yml` to be red daily until it is settled** — that is the design (it fails on purpose so a human is emailed), and **the PR `audit` job will be red on every open PR meanwhile, which does not block merging** (`continue-on-error: true`, deliberate; `ci.yml` says *"Do not 'tidy' the two to match"*). **Say so on any PR that meets it**, so nobody re-derives it. **DONE 2026-10-07 (`claude/sharp-override`):** the narrower route this item asked to weigh first was the right one — `"overrides": { "sharp": "^0.35.5" }` in `package.json` plus the lockfile, and `npm run audit:prod` goes from **4 high to 0 vulnerabilities**. The breaking `wrangler` downgrade was **not** taken, and the reason is worth keeping: there is no newer release to move to — `miniflare` pins `sharp` at exactly `0.35.4` and every current `wrangler` pins that `miniflare` — so npm's only route was backwards, and a major regression of the chain that builds and deploys the app is the larger risk by a wide margin. **Reachability was established before urgency, and it is nil:** `next.config.ts` sets `images: { unoptimized: true }` and `dangerouslyAllowSVG` appears nowhere in the repo, so the `sharp`-backed image optimiser is never invoked, and `miniflare` is the local Worker simulator, which does not run in production. Hygiene, on the same reading the `next/og` item recorded. `docs/decisions/2026-10-07-sharp-override.md` has the argument and the condition under which it expires. Verified with `npm run opennext:build` as well as the three gates, because `next build` never loads `wrangler` or `miniflare` and so cannot exercise the pin that was overridden. **What the red cost, now addressed in CLAUDE.md:** it stalled the production release manager for about 45 minutes on 2026-10-07 working out whether the release could proceed, and it had been red on every PR for two days with nobody asking why. CLAUDE.md said nothing about the `audit` job while documenting a red `test-plan` at length, so it now carries a section stating that a red `audit` cannot fail a run or block a merge (measured across the last 30 pull-request runs: not one concluded failure because of `audit`), what a red does ask for, and the two standing do-nots. **Follow-up on the `backlog` branch, not here:** delete the override once `wrangler` and `miniflare` ship a `sharp` past 0.35.5. → *Security*
- [ ] **Delete the `sharp` override once `wrangler` and `miniflare` ship a `sharp` past 0.35.5.** Added 2026-10-07 by `claude/sharp-override`, which put `"overrides": { "sharp": "^0.35.5" }` in `package.json` to clear [GHSA-wq5f-xc86-pv6w](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wq5f-xc86-pv6w) (`sharp <0.35.5`, high, a flaw in the librsvg copy `sharp` bundles) out of the production tree. **Why it is a follow-up and not a defect:** an `overrides` entry pins a transitive dependency behind its maintainer's back — `miniflare` asked for exactly `0.35.4` and is getting `0.35.5` anyway. That is sound for a patch bump and nothing more, and it is not a licence to hold the pin for good: left in place it will one day silently hold `sharp` *back* from a version the chain actually wants, and that failure is much harder to read than the advisory it fixed. **The check:** when `npm ls sharp --omit=dev` shows the chain resolving to 0.35.5 or later on its own, delete the `overrides` block, run `npm install`, and confirm `npm run audit:prod` is still clean. `npm run opennext:build` is the gate that matters, not just `npm run build` — `next build` never loads `wrangler` or `miniflare`, so it cannot exercise the pin. **Not urgent, and do not chase it:** the advisory is not reachable in this app (`images: { unoptimized: true }`, no `dangerouslyAllowSVG`, and `miniflare` is the local simulator), so nothing is at risk either way; this is tidying a deliberate temporary measure. `docs/decisions/2026-10-07-sharp-override.md` has the full argument. → *Security*
- [x] **Two `public-views` failures overnight on 2026-10-07 that nothing explains.** **Explained 2026-10-07 (`public-views-overnight`):** both failed only on `is_admin(): anon EXECUTE is refused — HTTP 200: false`; 0153's first draft granted `is_admin()` to `anon`, was applied to dev at 00:19:57Z and corrected by hand by ~00:36Z. A real grant on dev, not a flaky check; production never had it. `apply-migrations.mjs` now refuses a file `check-migration-grants` rejects, and `check-public-views` repeats its failures at the end. `docs/decisions/2026-10-07-public-views-overnight.md`. Found while fixing the daytime flood (PR #420), and deliberately **not** folded into it — recorded as open defect 2 in `docs/test-plans/public-views-impact-figures.md`. **The runs:** `37552423077` (00:31Z) and `37551809878` (00:24Z), both `pull_request`, on `claude/worktree-held-reason` and `claude/photo-routes-off-predicate` respectively; `public-views` failed on both and the job was green again by morning. **Why the obvious answer is wrong:** the daytime failures were `0156` granting `public_impact_figures` to `anon` without declaring it in the allowlist, but `0156` only merged at 06:56 on 2026-10-07, hours *after* these. So this is a second, unidentified cause. **Why it is worth an hour:** `public-views` is the check that the anonymous tier of the database can read the `public_*` views and nothing else — it is not `continue-on-error`, it fails the run, and it is the one check whose red could mean real exposure. A failure that comes and goes on its own is exactly the shape nobody chases, and it is also the shape a genuine intermittent leak would have. **Where to start:** read the failed step's log on both runs (`gh run view <id> --log-failed`), which says which object or probe failed; then whether anything was applied to dev around 00:20–00:35 (`apply-migrations.mjs --status`, and the two branches' own migrations), and whether the two branches shared a migration. Rule out the mundane explanations first: Supabase rate-limiting or a cold start answering a probe with a 5xx the script reads as a failure, and the secrets being momentarily absent (the job exits 0 and warns in that case, so it should *not* present as a failure — if it did, that is itself the bug). **If it turns out to be flakiness in the script**, make it distinguish a failed assertion from a failed request, because today they are the same red. → *Security*
- [x] **The next view a migration creates will again be writable by every signed-in login.** **Closed 2026-10-09 by `c67de1b2` (`grants-lint-and-refused-row`): `scripts/check-migration-grants.mjs` now refuses a file above 0160 that creates a public view without revoking insert, update, delete, truncate, references and trigger from authenticated and anon; a `create or replace` of an existing view is exempt, since a replace keeps its grants (`docs/decisions/2026-10-09-view-revoke-lint.md`).** Found 2026-10-07 by `resident-view-grants-0160` (`0160`, `docs/decisions/2026-10-07-view-write-grants.md`). The project's default privileges give `authenticated` insert, update, delete, truncate, references and trigger on every new object, views included; `0160` revoked them from the six views that had them (five inert, one writable but no wider than its table). Nothing stops the seventh. **Fix, cheapest first:** teach `scripts/check-migration-grants.mjs` that a file creating a view must also `revoke insert, update, delete, truncate, references, trigger on <view> from authenticated, anon`, and say so in its header; or change the default privileges for views only, which Postgres cannot do (one setting covers tables and views), so the lint is the realistic route. Low priority: a non-updatable view's grants do nothing, and a writable `security_invoker` one is bounded by its table's policies. → *Security*
- [x] **Placement history can be deleted, though it cannot be edited — decide whether that is intended.** Found 2026-10-09 by `claude/resident-corrections-script`. `0001`/`0119` make `placement_history` rows immutable on UPDATE, but nothing guards DELETE except the deceased lock: `placement_history_admin_delete` (`0153`, kept so Admin did not lose `admin_all_*`'s delete) lets any Admin login delete a living resident's placement rows through the API, and every session on the Management API can too (it runs as the owner, so row security does not apply). Write a one-paragraph `docs/decisions/` file for this in the next PR that touches placements or auditing.

- [x] **`issue_donation_receipt` takes the issuer from the caller, so the API can issue a receipt naming any organisation (found by `multi-tenancy-spike`, 2026-10-09).** **DONE 2026-10-10 (`claude/receipt-issuer-server-side`, migration `0176`):** the RPC now stores `receipt_issuer(country)`, a SQL copy of `receiptIssuer()`, and ignores `p_issuer` (kept in the signature so the deploy order does not matter). `check-donation-receipts-schema.mjs` passes a forged issuer on every issue and fails if it is stored or if the SQL and TypeScript copies differ. `docs/decisions/2026-10-10-receipt-issuer-server-side.md`. The original text follows. The RPC is `security definer` and accepts `p_issuer jsonb` as a parameter; the app passes `receiptIssuer(country)` (`src/app/management/donations/actions.ts:74`), but anyone with `donation.receipt` can call `/rest/v1/rpc/issue_donation_receipt` directly with any name and address. That gets round the deliberate hard-coding in `src/lib/donations/issuer.ts` (Lutan: a receipt must not read a field anyone can edit), and the forged issuer is stored on the receipt. Fix: the RPC builds the issuer itself (a `receipt_issuers` lookup, or a SQL function mirroring `issuer.ts`) and ignores or drops the parameter. At multi-tenancy this becomes the per-shelter issuer anyway (`docs/decisions/2026-10-09-multi-tenancy-spike.md`, *What fought back* §6), so doing it now is the same work done once.
- [x] **`issue_donation_receipt` also takes what the receipt says (`p_content`: donor name, lines, total) from the caller, so the API can issue a receipt for an amount nobody gave (found by `receipt-issuer-server-side`, 2026-10-10).** **DONE 2026-10-10 (`claude/receipt-content-server-side`, migration `0177`):** the RPC now stores `receipt_content(donation)`, a SQL copy of `receiptContentFor()` beside `0176`'s `receipt_issuer()`, and ignores `p_content` (kept in the signature so the deploy order does not matter). `check-donation-receipts-schema.mjs` issues every receipt with forged content and compares the stored content, as text, with what `receiptContentFor()` builds, on seven probe donations and every real dev donation; it was 22 red before the migration and 64 green after. With `0176` and `0177` the issuer and the content no longer come from the caller, but **the date still does**: `p_issued_on` is stored as given, so the API can backdate a receipt (its own item, filed on the backlog branch the same day). `docs/decisions/2026-10-10-receipt-content-server-side.md`. Same shape as the issuer hole closed in `0176`: the RPC is `security definer` and stores `p_content` as given, and the app builds it with `receiptContentFor(donation.donor_name, lines)` (`src/app/management/donations/actions.ts`). Anyone holding `donation.receipt` can call `/rest/v1/rpc/issue_donation_receipt` directly and get a correctly numbered receipt saying 1,000,000 baht for a 100-baht gift, stored in the register as though printed from the donation. Smaller than the issuer hole because the same login can already edit the donation's lines before issuing, so the forged figure at least has to match nothing; but a receipt whose stored content disagrees with its donation is exactly what a tax check would find. Fix: the RPC builds `content` from `donations` and `donation_lines` itself, mirroring `receiptContentFor()`, keeps `p_content` accepted and ignored as `0176` did with `p_issuer`, and the receipts harness passes forged content. Needs a migration, so it is a schema slot.
- [x] **`issue_donation_receipt` still takes the receipt date (`p_issued_on`) from the caller, so the API can backdate a receipt into another tax year (found by `receipt-content-server-side`, 2026-10-10).** **DONE 2026-10-12 (`claude/receipt-backdate-rule`, migration `0186`):** the RPC now validates `received_on <= p_issued_on <= shelter_today()` (22023 otherwise, before the counter moves). `check-donation-receipts-schema.mjs` passes a date before the donation, a future date and null (all refused) and one receipt backdated three days (accepted). `docs/decisions/2026-10-12-receipt-date-rule.md`. The original text follows. Third of the same shape after `0176` (issuer) and `0177` (content): the RPC is `security definer` and stores `p_issued_on` as given, with no check against today, the donation’s `received_on`, or anything else. The app always sends `todayIso()`, so no screen does it, but anyone holding `donation.receipt` can call `/rest/v1/rpc/issue_donation_receipt` directly and get the next number dated, say, last December, which is the one field a tax check reads first. Numbers are gapless and in order, so a backdated receipt would sit out of date order in the register, which is how it would be spotted, not prevented. Fix: the RPC uses the shelter’s today (Asia/Bangkok) itself, keeps `p_issued_on` accepted and ignored as `0176`/`0177` did, and the receipts harness passes a forged date. ~~Decide first whether the Director ever needs to issue a receipt dated earlier than today (a gift recorded late); if so, the rule is `received_on <= issued_on <= today`, not today only.~~ **ANSWERED 2026-10-11 (Lutan, in the `/plan-day` chat): YES, a backdated receipt is fine for the Director to issue.** His reason, in his words: *"It is not uncommon for someone to donate and then ask for a receipt a week later."* **So the rule is `received_on <= issued_on <= today` — not today only.** Three things that follow, and none of them is a judgement left to the stream: (1) **a receipt may never be dated before the donation it is for**, because that is not a late receipt, it is a wrong one; (2) **it may never be dated in the future**, which is the whole point of the item — a receipt dated into next tax year is the thing a tax check reads first; (3) **"today" is the shelter's today, Asia/Bangkok** (`shelter_date()`, `0073`), not UTC, or a receipt issued in the Thai evening is refused as being in the future. Keep `p_issued_on` **accepted and validated**, not ignored — this differs from `0176` and `0177`, which accepted and ignored their parameters, because here the caller's value is now legitimate input rather than something only the server should decide. The receipts harness should pass a date before `received_on` and a date after today and expect both refused, plus one legitimately backdated receipt and expect it accepted. **Do not narrow this to today-only on the grounds that it is safer**: it would refuse the ordinary case Lutan has just described, and the Director would have no way to issue the receipt she was asked for. Needs a migration, so it is a schema slot.

- [x] **`worktree.mjs` defaults a portless worktree to 3000, the main checkout's port, and hands the same port out twice (scripts; found 2026-10-16 by `/plan-day`).** **STATUS 2026-10-16: DORMANT, NOT FIXED — Lutan put the Claude Code setting back to the original folder the same day, so `worktree.mjs new` writes `.port` again and no portless worktree should appear. It is one setting away from returning, and the second half below is a latent fault regardless.** Both `cmdDev` (`scripts/worktree.mjs:477`) and the `launch.json` writer (`:353`) read `readPort(dir) ?? MAIN_PORT`, where `MAIN_PORT` is **3000**. A worktree with no `.port` therefore gets a `launch.json` aimed at 3000, and `preview_start` attaches the session to whatever already serves there — the main checkout, or **another stream's dev server**. The failure is quiet and nasty: a stream verifies its change against someone else's build and sees it pass or fail for reasons unconnected to its work. **Second half, and the part that is NOT setting-dependent: `nextFreePort` reads `.port` files, so it cannot see a worktree that lacks one and allocates the same port twice.** Observed: `worktree.mjs new planner-handover-173` was handed **3008**, already assigned to the live `ledger-and-labels-schema` stream. Harmless there (a docs branch runs no dev server) but a second dev server on 3008 would have collided with a live one. **Context, so nobody re-derives it:** for part of 2026-10-15 and 2026-10-16 the desktop app cut its own worktree per session under `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/<slug>-<hash>`, and those have no `.port` — that is how both halves were found. **Do:** (a) make `nextFreePort` enumerate every worktree `git worktree list` knows, not only those with a `.port`, so a port is never issued twice; (b) refuse to write a `launch.json` aimed at `MAIN_PORT` from a worktree that is not the main checkout, or allocate and write `.port` instead. **(a) is worth doing whatever the setting**, because two worktrees can collide for other reasons. Also consider teaching `worktree.mjs list` to show worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/` — `git worktree list` sees them and `list` does not, and four stale ones are sitting there now that `worktree.mjs done` cannot remove (they need `git worktree remove`). → *Deployment* **DONE 2026-10-16 (a) and (b):** `nextFreePort` counts every worktree git knows, spares included; `writeLaunch` assigns and writes `.port` for a non-main worktree without one instead of falling back to 3000. NOT done: `list` still does not show `.claude/worktrees/` spares. `docs/decisions/2026-10-16-cards-count-in-ci-and-worktree-ports.md`.
