- [x] **A schema branch that adds a public view turns CI red on every OTHER stream, for as long as it stays unmerged.** Found 2026-10-16 by the `0.33.0` release, whose record PR went red having touched nothing but three Markdown files. **Mechanism:** `public-views` (`scripts/check-public-views.mjs`) runs against the **shared dev database**, while its `PUBLIC_VIEWS` allow-list is read from **the branch under test**. The schema-first rule (CLAUDE.md) requires a migration to be applied to dev *before* its PR merges. In that window the new view exists in dev and is absent from `PUBLIC_VIEWS` on `main`, so every branch cut from `main` fails with `FAIL public_<thing>: anon SELECT is refused - HTTP 200 (a new public view? add it to PUBLIC_VIEWS)`. **Observed:** `0210_appeals.sql` (#667) created `public_appeals` and `public_appeal_photos` and was applied to dev about a minute after #667's own CI had passed - so #667 was green and #668 (and anything else branched from `main`) was red, with no fault of their own and no fix available on their branch. **Why it matters beyond the nuisance:** the check is doing its job - an unlisted public view is exactly the silent-exposure risk it exists to catch - so it must not simply be softened. But a red that nobody can act on is the kind people learn to wave through, which is how a real one gets missed. It also stalls the merge train, since a red check is never merged past. **Options to weigh in the PR:** (a) have the check treat a view that exists in dev but is created by a migration **not on `origin/main`** as `skip` with a loud note naming the branch, rather than `FAIL` - it can tell, by reading `supabase/migrations` on `origin/main`; (b) run the check against a throwaway database built from the branch's own migrations instead of shared dev, which removes the coupling entirely but costs build time; (c) leave the behaviour and document it, which is what `0.33.0` did as a stopgap in `docs/release-handover.md`. (a) looks cheapest and keeps the signal. **Whichever is chosen, say explicitly what happens to a genuinely unlisted view on a branch that DOES own the migration** - that case must stay red. Needs a test plan that exercises both: a view from an unmerged foreign branch (should not fail you) and a view your own branch adds without listing it (must fail you). No schema. -> *Developer experience* **Done 2026-10-16 (`claude/ci-script-fixes-fold`): option (a). `check-public-views.mjs` skips an unlisted `public_*` view only with positive proof that another unmerged `origin/*` branch's migration creates it (loud WARN naming the branch), and fails every other case; proved by `scripts/check-public-view-owner.mjs`. See `docs/decisions/2026-10-16-public-views-foreign-branch-skip.md`.**

- [x] **System status says the Pi is "Not in use yet" while the Pi is serving the site: the check reads a setting the Pi never gets.** Lutan, 2026-10-11: the **Pi origin** tile on `/admin/status` shows *"Not in use yet: every page is served by the Cloudflare Worker, as before the Pi"*. **Why (read 2026-10-11 on `main`):** `checkOrigin()` (`src/lib/status/health.ts`, about line 240) returns `off` when `ORIGIN_HOST` is empty, reading it from the Worker's env or `process.env`. `ORIGIN_HOST` is set for the Worker in `wrangler.jsonc` (`pi.lannacare.org` production, `test-pi.lannacare.org` test), but when the Pi is up, **the Pi renders `/admin/status` itself**, and the Pi's `.env.production.local` is written by `scripts/pi/write-env.mjs`, whose `RUNTIME_VARS` copies only `PUBLIC_SITE` from `wrangler.jsonc`. So on a healthy system the page says "not in use", and it would only say something true while the Pi is *down* and the Worker is rendering. The tile is wrong exactly when everything is fine, and it hides nothing about an outage, but it makes System status untrustworthy at a glance. **Fix to choose in the PR:** (a) the page knows which machine drew it: no Worker env means this page came from the Pi, so say *"This page was drawn by the Pi at <host>"* as `ok`, and keep the tunnel probe for the Worker's view; and/or (b) add `ORIGIN_HOST` (and `ORIGIN_KEY` if the probe needs it; never print it) to `RUNTIME_VARS` so the Pi probes its own tunnel as the Worker would. (a) alone is the honest minimum; say which and why. **Also check:** the status **alert** emails (`src/lib/status/alerts.ts`, which alerts on origin `warn`) run from the Worker's cron and so do see `ORIGIN_HOST`; confirm, so the alert is not affected the same way. Both environments (test and production) have the same gap; a Pi redeploy (`deploy-pi.sh`) is needed for (b), which is Lutan's step for production. Releases line (the Director sees this tile as Admin).

- [x] **`apply-migrations.mjs --drift <env>` crashes every time, on every environment (found 2026-10-13, during the `0.28.0` release).** `ReferenceError: unapplied is not defined` at `scripts/apply-migrations.mjs:226`. Introduced by `e6df8b2b` — the `--upto` PR (#570), **in the `0.28.0` release itself**. `driftReport()` destructures `{ unapplied, missingFile }` into its own scope and returns a count; the new explanatory block at the call site then reads `unapplied` and `missingFile` as if they were in scope, and they are not. The condition is evaluated unconditionally, so **every** `--drift` run dies, whatever the state of the database. **What still works, and why this was not caught:** the crash happens *after* `driftReport()` has printed the whole comparison, so the substance — file count, applied-row count, and the two gap lists — is on screen and correct; only the `No drift: <env> matches origin/main` verdict line and the exit code are lost. It exits non-zero through the crash, so it fails loudly rather than silently, and a reader skimming the output sees a correct comparison. Nothing in CI runs `--drift`. **Why it matters:** the release runbook requires the named drift check on **both** databases and says to quote its verdict, precisely because that line is what reads as a drift check to whoever reads the record afterwards. `0.28.0`'s record therefore quotes the comparison (`192 file(s), 192 applied row(s)`, 0 on either side, both databases) and states that the verdict line could not be printed. **The fix is two lines:** have `driftReport()` return the two arrays rather than only their total, and read them from that at the call site. **While there:** add a case to whatever covers this — `check-release-guards.mjs` is the nearest harness — because a release gate that cannot run is worth one assertion. Also note `--drift dev` is not a thing: the dev database is `--env test`. *Done on `claude/release-tooling-fixes`: `driftReport()` returns the arrays; a case in `check-release-guards.mjs`; verified with `--drift --env test` printing the verdict and exiting 0.*

- [ ] **A USB SSD on the Pi as a bootable spare and a second backup copy.** **Status 2026-10-02 (PR #297 merged): script, timer and runbook are in (`scripts/pi/spare-clone.sh`, `docs/pi-hosting.md` "Spare boot drive"); NOT done until a clone has been booted from. The first drive tried was a counterfeit (2 TB label, 40-50 kB/s, USB 2, `048d:1234`) and was rejected. Needs a branded 500 GB-1 TB SSD, `f3probe`, then `spare-clone.sh init` and the boot test. Encryption decision is proposed (unencrypted clone, drive kept secure), awaiting Lutan: `docs/decisions/2026-10-02-spare-boot-drive-not-encrypted.md`.**  Lutan, 2026-10-02, who has a spare external USB SSD. **Worth doing, for fast recovery rather than for the code** (the code is already on GitHub and the laptop). **Main use, a bootable clone of the Pi's NVMe:** OS, packages, `/etc` and the things that are *not* in git (the two env files, the `cloudflared` tunnel credentials and config, the `lanna-care` systemd unit, Glances/monitoring config). Use `rpi-clone` again (`docs/pi-hosting.md` already uses it to copy SD → NVMe): `sudo rpi-clone sda` onto the USB drive, then on a timer (weekly, and before any OS upgrade), so the clone stays recent. The Pi's boot order `0xf146` tries NVMe first and USB next, so **verify** that with the NVMe removed or disabled the Pi boots from the USB clone and serves the site; that test is the point of the item. **Second use:** a copy of the weekly database dumps, which today sit on the NVMe beside everything else (plus Drive), e.g. `backup.mjs`'s planned `--local-copy` pointed at the USB mount. **Limits to write down:** same box, same house, so theft, fire, flood or a power surge take both drives; Drive and GitHub stay the off-site copies, this is the quick way back from a dead NVMe. Because the clone holds secrets and a USB drive is easy to walk off with, encrypt it (LUKS on the backup partition; a bootable clone needs either an unencrypted boot partition with the secrets on an encrypted one, or accept the risk and keep the drive physically secure; decide with Lutan). Check the Pi 5's power supply can drive the USB SSD alongside the NVMe HAT (the official 27 W supply), and that the drive shows up as the same device after a reboot (mount by UUID). Deliverable: the timer and script in `scripts/pi/`, a "Spare boot drive" section in `docs/pi-hosting.md` with the recovery steps, and a monitoring tile (clone age) in the Home Assistant item. **An SD card is an accepted interim spare, decided 2026-10-02, and it does only the bootable half.** Lutan has spare cards, and this closes the recovery gap without waiting for a purchase — which matters while the Pi is the single point of failure for every write on both environments and the last recovery was "Lutan restarted it". It genuinely works on this box: the Pi was first flashed to SD and `rpi-clone`d to the NVMe (`docs/pi-hosting.md:152-158`), and `BOOT_ORDER=0xf146` already reads 6 NVMe, 4 USB, 1 SD, so SD needs no eeprom change. **Three caveats.** (1) **Use a USB card reader, not the built-in slot.** `spare-clone.sh:102` tests `lsblk -dno TRAN` for `usb`, so `mmcblk0` is refused outright; a card in a reader reports `usb`, passes unchanged, and is tried earlier in the boot order too. No code change needed, and the check should stay as it is. (2) **Size.** `init` writes 512 MB boot plus `ROOT_SIZE`, default **64G**, so a 16-32 GB card needs `ROOT_SIZE` lowered to fit the NVMe’s *used* space — read `df -h /` on the Pi first. (3) **Still `f3probe` it.** SD is the most counterfeited storage there is and the drive tried on 2026-10-02 was a fake. Endurance is a moderate worry rather than a blocker, because `spare-clone.timer` runs `rpi-clone -u` incrementally and not a full weekly rewrite — but SD has no SMART and tends to fail silently or go read-only, on the one device you only reach for on the worst day. So **re-run the boot test periodically** and treat the card as interim, not as the answer. A branded SSD is still wanted: for the archive half (the item below) and for speed.

Today a deceased resident's whole record lives only in Google Drive, under `Residents/Deceased/<Name> (<ID>)/`: the summary PDF, the offline `index.html` and the photos and files beside them (`src/lib/archive/archive-deceased-resident.ts`). This is the record the shelter keeps for good, so a copy that does not depend on Google is worth having. **What "offsite" means here:** the copy is independent of Google (an account lockout, a deleted folder, a Drive outage), but it sits in Lutan's house next to the Pi, so it is not offsite from the Pi; Drive stays the primary and this is the second copy. **Shape:** a pull-only mirror run by a timer on the Pi (nightly is plenty): walk `Residents/Deceased/` through the Drive API with the Pi's existing credentials, download new or changed files (compare Drive file id and `modifiedTime`, so the regenerated PDF and index after a bio or photo edit, `refreshDeceasedArchiveIfNeeded()`, are picked up), and never write to Drive. The offline `index.html` was built to be opened without the app, so the mirror is browsable straight off the drive. **Deletions:** if a folder disappears from Drive, keep the local copy and log it rather than deleting it (the point is to survive a mistake in Drive); a death withdrawn in error (`undo_deceased_placement()` moves the folder back under `Residents/`) should be noted in the log too, not silently kept as if still deceased. **Sharing the drive with the spare boot clone:** give each its own partition (the clone needs the whole-disk layout `rpi-clone` writes; the archive needs a plain data partition mounted by UUID), or pick one job for this drive; decide alongside that item. **Privacy:** the archive holds medical history and may name carers and adopters, so encrypt the archive partition (LUKS) as the spare-drive item suggests for the clone. **Multi-shelter:** keep one folder per shelter on the drive, so it fits the per-shelter Drive item. **Done when:** the mirror script and timer are in `scripts/pi/`, a restore note in `docs/pi-hosting.md` (how to copy a folder back to Drive), a "last archive sync" tile in the Home Assistant item, and a test: mark a test resident deceased on dev, wait for the sync, edit its bio, sync again, and confirm the new PDF is on the drive. **This half needs the real SSD; the interim SD card does not cover it, decided 2026-10-02.** Capacity is the obvious reason — the clone takes the whole of a small card and leaves nothing over — but the stronger one is that the two jobs want opposite things from the drive. The clone is deliberately **unencrypted** (`docs/decisions/2026-10-02-spare-boot-drive-not-encrypted.md`: a Pi that must come back unattended after a power cut cannot wait for a LUKS passphrase), while this archive **must** be LUKS-encrypted, since it holds medical history and names carers and adopters. The clone is also rewritten weekly, so rot gets caught; an archive written once and then left on flash would quietly stop being a real copy, with no SMART to say so — the wrong medium for "the record the shelter keeps for good". Waiting costs little: Drive remains the primary copy, and the exposure this item addresses is an account lockout or a deleted folder, not a dead NVMe. This also settles the question the item raises above — *"give each its own partition ... or pick one job for this drive"* — as **two devices, one job each.**

The other two `0.20.0` refusals also did not recur: `gh pr merge` and `apply-migrations.mjs --drift production` both ran, which closed the two gaps `0.20.0`'s record had to leave open. Net effect: Lutan did **exactly one job** on `0.20.1` (the Worker production deploy), which is what `docs/release-procedure.md` has specified since 2026-10-02 and had not been true since. The standing instruction not to add a rule for the Worker production deploy is unchanged. → *Deployment*

- [x] **`apply-migrations.mjs` does not guard `--env test`, so a stale worktree can silently undo a merged migration's effect.** Found 2026-10-15 during the `0.32.1` release. `GUARDED` is `envName === "uat" || envName === "production"` (`scripts/apply-migrations.mjs:94`), so the check that a checkout's `supabase/migrations/` matches `origin/main` is skipped for dev. Consequence, observed rather than reasoned: `0203_clear_stale_ledger_row_0201_map_rooms.sql` deleted the phantom `0201_map_rooms_drop_map_id_shape.sql` ledger row from dev, is recorded as applied, **and the row is back** — dev reads `208 applied` against 207 files and `--drift test` is red, while production is clean because the row was never there. The cause is that three merged-but-not-cleared worktrees (`facility-map-with-enclosures`, `map-rooms-column-drop`, `mobile-44px-finish`) still hold the file under its **old** name, and an unguarded `--env test` run from any of them re-inserts it. The effect is quiet: the migration reports success, CI is green, and only the drift check notices. **Do:** (1) decide whether `GUARDED` should cover `test` too — the argument against is that dev is where schema-first work is applied *before* merge, which the guard would forbid, so the fix is probably a narrower check (refuse a file that is not on `origin/main` **and** not in the current branch's diff) rather than full guarding; (2) a new migration to delete the row again, since an applied file is never edited; (3) clear the three leftover worktrees, which removes today's source. Note (2) alone is not a fix — it is re-runnable by hand and will come back the next time an old worktree applies to dev. **Not a release blocker:** production is unaffected and dev's actual schema is correct, both columns being dropped under either filename. Recorded as a stated gap in `0.32.1`'s release record. **UPDATE later the same day: part (3) is DONE, which changes part (2).** A `/clean-streams` round cleared all three worktrees, and a sweep of every `Animal_Shelter_*` checkout now finds **no copy of `0201_map_rooms_drop_map_id_shape.sql` anywhere**, so nothing can re-insert the row. That removes the reason (2) was not a fix on its own: **a single new migration deleting the row would now close this permanently**, where before it would have come straight back. (1) is still the real question and is unchanged — the guard gap is a live hazard for the *next* renamed migration even though today's source is gone, so do not close this item on the strength of (2) alone. Dev still reads `208 applied` against 207 files and `--drift test` is still red. **PART (1) DONE 2026-10-16 (`claude/migration-test-guard`, `docs/decisions/2026-10-16-migration-guard-for-test.md`): `--env test` now refuses a file absent from `origin/main` but present in the merge-base. Part (2), the cleanup migration deleting the phantom `0201` row, is DONE 2026-10-16: `0208_clear_phantom_ledger_row_0201_again.sql` (`claude/ledger-labels-schema`, `docs/decisions/2026-10-16-ledger-row-and-resident-labels.md`); `--drift test` no longer lists the 0201 row, checked after two applies. Closes the `0.32.1` stated gap.** → *Deployment*

- [ ] **`setup.sh` adds the Pi's swapfile to `fstab` with no priority, so it comes back *below* zram — and on the live Pi it was not in `fstab` at all.** Found 2026-10-19. `/swapfile2` was created by hand during `0.36.0` and `/etc/fstab` had **no swap entry whatsoever**, so the swap fix that `0.36.1` depended on **would have vanished at the next reboot**, silently, taking the Pi back to the state where builds were killed three times running. Fixed on the live machine (`swapon -p 200`, plus `/swapfile2 none swap sw,pri=200 0 0`) and **proved by an actual reboot** — it came back at priority 200. Still to do in the repo: `scripts/pi/setup.sh` line 77 writes `sw` with no `pri=`, so a rebuilt Pi gets the file swap at a *lower* priority than zram, which is the wrong way round — zram is compressed RAM and spends RAM to save it. Add `pri=200` there and explain the ordering in `docs/pi-hosting.md`. Note the priority change was **not** what fixed the `0.37.0` build (see the Turbopack cache item) — it was a real misconfiguration found on the way past.
- [ ] **`eslint` walks into `.claude/worktrees/`, so `gates.mjs` reports a five-figure lint failure in the main checkout that CI never sees.** Found 2026-10-19 while running the gates for the `0.37.0` release. Two leftover app-cut worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/` held `.next` and `.open-next` build output; `eslint` linted all of it — **2,948 errors and 36,883 warnings, every one of them inside those folders** — and on the first run exhausted the V8 heap and aborted with exit 134 before reporting anything at all. CI is unaffected because it checks out clean. **The danger is the shape of the failure**: a release manager meets a red `lint` on `main` with an out-of-memory abort and a five-figure error count, which looks like a catastrophe in the code and is entirely a stale folder. Do: add `.claude/**` to the eslint config's ignores. Also note `worktree.mjs list` cannot see these folders (git does not track them) and an orphaned three-day-old `next dev` was still running inside one, regenerating `.next` as fast as it was deleted and squatting on port 3000 — `/clean-streams` covers app-cut worktrees, so the gap is that nothing notices them from the gates' side.

## Quick wins

- [x] **A gate script can print its verdict and then exit non-zero from a teardown crash, so its exit code contradicts its own answer — and for a gate, it contradicts it in the dangerous direction.** Found 2026-10-16 during the `0.34.0` release. `node scripts/facility-map-holders.mjs --env production` is the gate Lutan asked for before `0212_retire_facility_map_activity.sql` was applied to production: it exits 1 when a role would be stranded, so **non-zero means "DO NOT APPLY"**. It printed its table and `Without facility.enclosures at Read: 0 (safe to retire)`, then died with `Assertion failed: !(handle->flags & UV_HANDLE_CLOSING), file src\win\async.c, line 94` and exited **127** — reproduced twice before the apply and again after it. The script's own `process.exit(stranded.length ? 1 : 0)` had already decided `0`; the 127 is libuv tearing down with the `fetch` keep-alive socket still open on Windows, and says nothing about the check. **So a session reading only the exit code would conclude the gate had failed when it passed**, and would refuse to apply a migration that was provably safe — or, worse, would learn to wave away a non-zero exit from this family of scripts and one day wave away a real one. **The shape is not specific to this script:** any one-shot `scripts/*.mjs` that `fetch`es the Supabase Management API and then calls `process.exit()` can do it, which is most of the `check-*` and reporting scripts, including ones whose exit code CI reads. **Fix (small, one place):** add a shared exit helper in `scripts/lib/` beside `env.mjs` that flushes stdout and lets the event loop drain before exiting — `await new Promise(r => setImmediate(r))` after the last write, or close the keep-alive agent / pass `{ keepalive: false }` — and use it from the scripts that currently exit straight after a `fetch`. **Then prove it:** run the fixed `facility-map-holders.mjs` against test and read `echo $?` as `0`, twice. **While there, check whether CI is exposed:** any job whose step is a bare `node scripts/check-*.mjs` inherits the same ambiguity, and a flaky 127 there would read as a real failure and block a merge for nothing — `grep -n "node scripts/check-" .github/workflows/ci.yml`, and say in the PR which jobs were and were not affected. No schema and no user-visible surface, so `n/a` on the release-notes line. Worth doing because the cost is asymmetric: the bug makes a passing safety gate look like a failing one, and gates exist precisely for the moments when nobody has spare attention to debug them. Interim note for anyone who meets it before the fix: a non-zero exit **accompanied by an `async.c` assertion line** is noise; a non-zero exit **without** one is a real verdict. **Done 2026-10-16 (`claude/ci-script-fixes-fold`): `scripts/lib/exit.mjs` `exitWith()` replaces a bare `process.exit()` after `fetch` in 15 scripts (exit code now 0/1 as decided, reproduced 127 before and 0 twice after on `facility-map-holders.mjs`). CI runs on Linux where the libuv assertion is Windows-only, so no CI job was exposed. See `docs/decisions/2026-10-16-shared-exit-helper.md`.**

- [x] **The resident picker is empty for Admin and Management: `resident_who_and_where` returns rows only to who-and-where roles, when every role above them should see it too (schema, small).** Lutan, 2026-10-12: "Found it: resident_who_and_where only returns rows for logins with the volunteer role, so the picker is empty for Admin and Management (2IC, volunteers, and Head of Medical are unaffected). Volunteers have the lowest level of access so every role above that should also have that access." **Confirmed on `main` 2026-10-12:** the view (latest body `0180_perm_drop_enum_readers.sql`) ends `where public.on_volunteer_floor()`, and `on_volunteer_floor()` is true only for a role whose `roles.scope_residents = 'who_and_where'` (the volunteer, the 2IC, both Heads). A role with the **whole** resident record (`scope_residents` all: Admin, Management) gets **zero rows**, so every page that reads the view shows nothing to them: the resident picker (`src/app/medical/ResidentPicker.tsx`, `src/lib/medical/residents.ts`) on **Add Medical Photos** and **Record Weight** (and Feed Special Diets if it uses it), and anything else in `grep -rln resident_who_and_where src` (`src/lib/residents/who-and-where.ts`, `list-view.ts`, `export.ts`, `src/lib/enclosures/details.ts`, `src/app/r/[code]/page.tsx`, `src/app/residents/page.tsx`): check each, since some only read it when the caller is limited (`readsWhoAndWhereOnly()`) and are fine. **Fix (one re-runnable migration):** the view's filter becomes "any live role that may read residents at all": `on_volunteer_floor() or sees_all_residents()` (or the `has_permission('resident.record', 'read')` cell plus app access, whichever `0144`/`0180` make the honest test), so the who-and-where columns, which are a strict subset of what Admin and Management can already read in `residents`, are visible to everyone at or above the floor. Nothing new is exposed: the view has no column a full-record role cannot already see. Keep it refused to a doctor/clinic login unless that scope already reads those residents (`is_clinic_login()`, `0167`), and to public viewer and signed-out. **Add the case to a check** so it cannot regress: a probe in the permission parity or `check-medical-jobs.mjs` that Admin and Management each get the same row count from the view as the 2IC. **Also look for the same shape** in the other floor-only objects `0180` rewrote (any `where public.on_volunteer_floor()` with no "or above" branch) and fix those in the same file. Releases line (Admin and Management can now pick a resident on Add Medical Photos and Record Weight), [done 2026-10-13 (`claude/resident-picker-floor`, migration 0192): the view now passes `on_volunteer_floor() or sees_all_residents()`; no other floor-only positive filter existed, see `docs/decisions/2026-10-13-who-and-where-for-all-residents-readers.md`] test plan: as Admin and as Management on dev, the picker on both pages lists residents; the 2IC's and a volunteer's are unchanged; a doctor login and a signed-out request still get nothing they did not before.

- [x] **Two shell scripts are committed without the executable bit, and one of them is invoked by systemd.** Found 2026-10-02 setting test up on the Pi: `bash: ./scripts/pi/setup-test.sh: Permission denied`. `git ls-files -s '*.sh'` shows `deploy-pi.sh` and `setup.sh` as `100755` but **`setup-test.sh` and `spare-clone.sh` as `100644`**, in the index, so every clone gets them non-executable. `docs/pi-hosting.md:122` tells you to run `./scripts/pi/setup-test.sh`, which cannot work as committed; the workaround is `bash scripts/pi/setup-test.sh`. **`spare-clone.sh` is the one that matters more**, because `scripts/pi/spare-clone.service` has `ExecStart=__REPO__/scripts/pi/spare-clone.sh sync` — systemd invokes the file directly and requires the bit, so the timer would fail with the same error, silently, somewhere nobody is watching. It has not bitten yet only because that timer is not installed (see the spare-clone item). **Fix:** `git update-index --chmod=+x scripts/pi/setup-test.sh scripts/pi/spare-clone.sh` and commit; two mode changes, no content. **Worth pairing with a guard**, since this is the second thing this week to reach `main` because nothing checks `scripts/` — a syntax error in `deploy.mjs` did the same on 2026-10-02 and CI was green on it (see that item). One CI step would catch both classes: `node --check` over `scripts/**/*.mjs`, and a check that any `*.sh` named in a `.service` file's `ExecStart` is mode `100755`. **Done 2026-10-02** (`claude/script-exec-bits-guard`): both files are `100755`, and CI job `script-integrity` (`scripts/check-script-integrity.mjs`) now parses every `scripts/**/*.mjs` and fails on a `.service` `ExecStart` `.sh` that is not `100755` in the index, printing the `git update-index --chmod=+x` fix. It states what it does not cover. Decision: `docs/decisions/2026-10-02-script-integrity-reads-the-index.md`.

- [x] **Bug: on Record a donation, "Choose resident" finds nobody when you search.** Lutan, 2026-10-09: choosing "For a resident" and searching in the picker does not work. **Almost certainly the cause (read 2026-10-09, not yet reproduced):** `src/app/management/donations/new/page.tsx` loads the picker's list with `supabase.from("residents").select("id, name, thai_name, current_status")`, but **`residents` has no `current_status` column** (0001 keeps status out of the table on purpose; it is worked out in `resident_list_view` / `resident_current_state`). The query therefore errors, the page ignores the error (`residents.data ?? []`), and the picker opens on an **empty list**, so every search shows "no residents". **Fix:** load from `resident_list_view` as the other pickers do (`src/app/immunizations/new/page.tsx`: `resident_id, name, thai_name, current_status`, mapped to `id`), probably leaving out deceased residents (`NOT_DECEASED`) unless a gift in memory of one should be recordable; ask Lutan. And **stop the silence:** check `error` on this query and show a message on the form instead of an empty picker, since an empty list that looks like "no matches" is what hid this. Worth a quick grep for other `.from("residents").select(...current_status...)` reads, which would fail the same way. Check on the donation's page and receipt that the chosen resident shows (`residents:designation_resident_id(name)`). Small, no schema. A `releases.ts` line (the Director will notice it working) and a test: search by English name, Thai name, pick one, save, the donation page names the resident. **Done 2026-10-10 (`claude/donation-picker-and-map-zoom`):** reproduced first on dev (PostgREST 42703, *column residents.current_status does not exist*), so the read cause was the real one. The picker now loads from `resident_list_view`, **deceased included** (Lutan, 2026-10-10: a gift in memory of an animal must be recordable; the row shows Deceased). A failed load is logged and shown on the form. The donation's own page now throws on a failed read instead of showing *not found* or *no receipts yet*. Grep found no other `current_status` read off `residents`; the wider `?? []`-without-`error` pattern is filed separately. Tested: English search, Thai search, a deceased resident, save, and the donation page reads *A resident: Summer*. The receipt PDF carries no designation, by design.

- [x] **`check-phone-width.mjs --clean` sweeps other runs, not just its own (tooling; found by the `0.24.0` release, 2026-10-10).** The sweep matches everything a run makes by pattern — `name like 'ZZ Width %'` and `phonewidth-` logins (line 597) — so it deletes **another session's in-flight** seed rows and throwaway logins as readily as a killed run's. Seen on 2026-10-10: a `--clean` during the release removed `phonewidth-admin / management / second-in-command-d45ea577@example.invalid`, a role set this checkout's script could not even produce, so another stream was evidently mid-run; it also cleared a stale login from 2026-10-03. Dev data is disposable so nothing was lost that matters, but with three streams running the sweep is a trap for whoever is in the middle of a run. **Fix:** scope it to the current run id, or to rows older than an hour, and print what it removed. **Not closed by PR #509**, which fixed the Staff principal (the ticked item above) and did not touch the sweep.
- [x] **`ReleaseRole` is out of date, so a release note cannot be tagged for three live roles (found at the `0.25.0` cut, 2026-10-10).** `src/lib/releases.ts` declares `export type ReleaseRole = "admin" | "management" | "staff" | "doctor" | "volunteer"`. `staff` was retired by `0173` in `0.24.0` and is still listed; `second_in_command`, `head_of_maintenance` and `head_of_medical` have existed since then and are **not** listed, so a note meant for the 2IC or either Head cannot be tagged at all — the file would not typecheck. Today that shows up as notes being left untagged, which reads as "everyone" and is the safe direction, so nothing is broken; it is a gap that quietly removes an option. **Fix:** align the union with the roles the manual names (`src/lib/manual/types.ts`), drop `staff`, and check no existing entry tags `staff` before removing it (none did at `0.25.0`, checked). Previously released entries stay as they are — they are history, and untagged reads as everyone. Worth doing in the same PR as any future note that needs one of the three.

- [ ] **Videos of residents: keep them in the resident's Photos section, uploaded straight to Drive. STORAGE IS DECIDED — this is a BUILD, not a decision (schema then app).** Lutan, 2026-10-18: "Can we load videos into the residents photos? Or do we need a different section for videos?" **Answer today (read 2026-10-18 on `main`): no, videos cannot be loaded.** Every photo upload route accepts **images only** (JPEG, PNG, WebP, HEIC: `src/app/api/residents/[id]/photos/route.ts` ~25, `photos/shelter`, `photos/pending`), every upload is capped at **15 MB** (`src/lib/uploads/limits.ts`), and the photo route serves only images and PDFs (`src/app/api/photos/[fileId]/route.ts` ~101). A phone video is roughly 50 to 150 MB a minute, so even a short clip is far over the cap. **Recommendation: the same Photos section, not a separate one.** Staff think of "the pictures of Panda", videos sit in the same Drive folders (Shelter, Medical, Foster, Adoption) and need the same rules (Medical stays private, approval before publishing from the Add resident photos card, posted-on-social-media marks), so one section with a **Photos / Videos / All** filter and a play icon on video thumbnails is simpler than a second section that duplicates every rule. **What has to be built, and why it is not small:** (1) **Upload straight from the phone to Google Drive**, not through the app: the app asks Drive for a **resumable upload session** for the right folder and hands its address to the browser, which sends the file to Drive in chunks (surviving a dropped connection on site), then tells the app the new file id to record. That avoids the Worker's and the Pi's request-size limits and keeps the 15 MB cap for everything else. (2) **Playing it:** a video thumbnail from Drive, and playback either through Drive's own player in the lightbox or streamed through the photo route with range requests; pick the one that plays inline on an iPhone and Android, and test both. (3) Allowed types: MP4 and MOV (what phones record), with a **size cap per video** (e.g. 200 MB, about 2 minutes) and a clear message above it. **[SUPERSEDED 2026-10-18, and again 2026-10-19 — read the ANSWERED paragraph at the end of this item before acting on anything from here to it. The shelter’s account has 1 TB, not 15 GB, so there is nothing left to decide and the YouTube/Facebook options below are dropped.]** **Decide first, because of the zero-ongoing-cost rule:** the shelter's Google account has **15 GB free** for everything (photos, archive PDFs, backups). Video will use that up quickly (at 100 MB a clip, 150 clips is the lot), and more Drive space is a **paid** plan, which this project does not use. Options to put to Lutan: (a) store videos in Drive with a strict cap and a storage tile on System status showing space left; (b) **keep videos on YouTube (unlisted) or Facebook** and store only the **link** on the resident, which costs nothing and plays everywhere, at the price of the video living outside the shelter's Drive; (c) both, a short clip cap in Drive and links for anything longer. Recommended (c), or (b) if storage is tight. **Public site:** a video is public only if it is in a public folder and approved, the same as a photo, and never from Medical. Manual (Photos and videos), both dictionaries, releases line, decision file (videos: where they are stored and why), test plan on a phone: record a 30-second clip and add it to a resident; a weak connection resumes; it plays in the lightbox on iPhone and Android; a Medical video is not public; a clip over the cap is refused with the message; a linked YouTube video plays. **ANSWERED 2026-10-18 (Lutan): storage is not a major concern.** The shelter's own Google Drive, where the files will end up (the *Give production its own Drive tree* item), has **1 TB**, not the free 15 GB assumed above, and it is the shelter's existing account, so this costs the project nothing. **So: option (a), videos stored in Drive.** Keep a generous per-video cap only to protect uploads on a phone connection (e.g. 500 MB, about 5 minutes; say the figure in the PR), drop the YouTube/Facebook link route from this item (it can come back as its own item if wanted), and still add the **Drive space used / left** to System status so the 1 TB is watched. Until production moves to the shelter's Drive, dev and test write to the current `lannaanimalfoundationbwm` tree, so keep test clips short. **RECONFIRMED 2026-10-19 (Lutan): “Decision 5: already given twice, why are we losing these decisions. The customer has a 1TB account.” He is right, and the decision was never missing — it was buried under the superseded 15 GB text above while the title still said “decision on storage first”, so a checklist built from titles read it as open. Title and premise fixed in the same commit. DO NOT ASK HIM AGAIN: option (a), Drive, generous per-video cap, Drive space on System status.**

- [x] **BUG: Resident intake's Review step shows the intake date as "NaN undefined NaN" (small, app only; cause found).** Lutan, 2026-10-15, with a screenshot: he picked today's date on step 2, and step 6 (Review) showed *Intake date: NaN undefined NaN*. **Cause (read 2026-10-15 on `main`):** the review builds its rows with `display()` in `src/app/residents/new/IntakeForm.tsx` (~72), which reads each field by **id** (`form.querySelector('#intakeDate')`) and passes the intake date to `formatDate()` (~129). Since #603 (`470d2456`, 2026-10-13, *Date boxes read day first (DD/MM/YYYY) on every device*), `DateInput` (`src/components/DateInput.tsx`) gives the **id to the visible text box**, which holds `15/10/2026`, and puts the ISO date (`2026-10-15`) in a **hidden input carrying the name** (~78). So the review formats the day-first text as if it were ISO, and `formatDate()` turns it into NaN. **What is saved is right:** the form submits the hidden input's ISO value by name, so the resident gets the correct intake date; only the review line is wrong. Confirm that on dev before closing. **Fix:** read the date by its submitted value (the `name`, through `FormData` or the hidden input), not the visible box, or have `DateInput` expose the ISO value; then **sweep for the same pattern**: any other review or summary step that reads a `DateInput` by id (grep `querySelector` and `getElementById` against fields rendered with `DateInput`, and every `formatDate(` fed from a form element). Also make `formatDate()` return the input unchanged, or "—", rather than "NaN undefined NaN" when it cannot parse a value, so a future slip shows something readable. Releases line (the review shows the date again). Test plan: intake with today's date and with a past date, in English and Thai, shows the right date on Review and saves it; the other forms the sweep finds.

Each one shows on the assignee's My dashboard (the item above) for its day and is marked done or skipped, and only that result is kept (who, when, a note), so there is a record that the stocktake happened. Decide whether occurrences are generated ahead (a cron in `worker/`, or on first read of the day) or computed from the rule and stored only when acted on; the second avoids a job table filling with future rows. **Recurrence:** a small, explicit subset rather than full iCal RRULE: every N weeks on chosen weekday(s) (weekly, fortnightly with a start date as the anchor), monthly on day N, monthly on the Nth weekday ("first Monday"), with a start date and an optional end date. Dates are in Asia/Bangkok. **Order between jobs:** "after the stocktake" means an occurrence can depend on another template's occurrence the same day, and shows as "waiting for stocktake" until that one is done. **Missed jobs:** decide whether an undone occurrence stays overdue on the dashboard until done or skipped (suggest yes, with how many days late) or quietly expires. **Admin:** a Management page to create, edit, pause and reassign templates, with a preview of the next few dates, and reassignment when a login is archived. - [x] **Deceased residents: confirm what happens to the archive when photos or the bio change after death.** Customer question 2026-09-22 — check the business logic and close the gaps. *How it works today:* the three edits still allowed on a deceased resident (0052: bio via `/residents/[id]/edit`, photo upload via `src/app/api/residents/[id]/photos/route.ts`, set-profile-photo and delete-photo in `src/app/residents/[id]/photos/actions.ts`) each call `refreshDeceasedArchiveIfNeeded()` (`src/lib/archive/refresh-deceased-archive.ts`), which re-runs `archiveDeceasedResident()` — the folder move no-ops and the summary PDF and `index.html` in `Residents/Deceased/<Name> (<ID>)/` are replaced in place, so the archive follows the record. *Gaps to decide on:* (1) it is **best effort and silent** — every caller ignores the returned `{ error }`, so if Drive is down the edit saves but the PDF/index stay stale and nobody is told; either surface it (hub banner "Archive out of date — Retry", reusing the existing Retry button) or record a `deceased_archive_stale_at` on `residents` that the hub shows. (2) It only runs when `deceased_archived_at` is set: a resident whose first archive never completed does not get one from an edit — fine, but the hub should say so. (3) A multi-photo upload regenerates the PDF once **per file** (sequential uploads); cheap for a handful, but debounce or run once after the batch if it turns out slow. (4) A HEIC profile photo is never embedded in the PDF (`EMBEDDABLE_IMAGE_TYPES`), so choosing a phone photo as profile after death gives a PDF without a picture — convert on upload or note it in the manual. (5) Verify in dev end to end: mark a test resident deceased, add a photo, change the bio, set a different profile photo, delete a photo — open the PDF and `index.html` in Drive after each step and confirm the change is there; write the outcome into the manual's deceased topic. *Status 2026-10-02 (`claude/deceased-archive-followups`, decisions `2026-10-02-deceased-archive-followups`):* gaps 1, 2, 3 and 5 are closed or consciously declined (walked end to end in dev; a simulated Drive outage shows the warning; persistent flag and debouncing declined). **Still open: gap 4 — upload a real iPhone HEIC after death, choose it as profile, and confirm the PDF has the picture.** **GAP 4 IS CLOSED, and the "still open" note above was already wrong when it was written (corrected 2026-10-07).** `a1452515` (**2026-09-24**, *"Put the profile photo in the summary PDF even when it's HEIC or large"*) made `loadProfilePhoto()` try **Drive's JPEG thumbnail first** and fall back to the original — and Drive renders HEIC, so `EMBEDDABLE_IMAGE_TYPES` only ever gated the *fallback*. - [x] **Microchip number on a resident, searchable from a chip scanner.** Done 2026-09-30 across 0113, PR 221, 0116 and `claude/microchip-vet-feature` (0117); see the second-half item below and `docs/decisions/2026-09-30-microchip-second-half-vet-form-public-boolean.md`. "Microchipping" already exists as a procedure type (0031), so the act of chipping can already be logged, just not the number. **Schema PR first:** `residents.microchip_number text` (nullable), stored as digits only (strip spaces and dashes on save), **unique** across residents where set (a partial unique index, so a mistyped duplicate is caught), with a check that allows the ISO 11784/11785 standard 15 digits and, if the shelter has older chips, 9/10-digit ones too (ask Lutan whether any exist before tightening it). Optional `microchip_implanted_on date`. Locked with the rest of the record on death (the 0026 trigger's column list). **Where it is entered:** Edit resident and the intake wizard (Health step), and offered straight after a "Microchipping" procedure is logged ("Record the chip number?"). Show it on the hub's details card, in the deceased archive PDF and index, and on the vet-visit and procedure views where a vet needs it. **Scanner search:** handheld and USB/Bluetooth microchip readers act as a keyboard: they type the 15 digits and press Enter. So (1) the `/residents` search and the header search match `microchip_number` exactly (after stripping non-digits), alongside name and R-code; an exact chip match jumps straight to that resident's hub, whatever the place/zone filters or deceased toggle say; (2) a small **Scan a chip** box (autofocused input, e.g. on `/residents` and the intake wizard's first step) so a staff member can scan a stray at the gate: a known chip opens the resident, an unknown one offers "New resident with this chip" prefilled. Phones cannot read the common 134.2 kHz (FDX-B) chips over NFC, so do not promise phone scanning; test with a real reader Lutan has, or by typing into the box. **Privacy and public site:** the number stays staff-only. Do not add it to any `public_*` view; the public resident page may show "Microchipped: yes" (a boolean derived from the column), which is the flag 0060's "Desexed / Vaccinated" ticks were meant to have. Vets see it for residents in their scope. **Encouraging chipping:** a count on the management dashboard (residents without a chip), a filter on `/residents` ("No microchip"), and a gentle prompt on the hub for a resident marked ready for adoption with no chip. - [x] **Residents: replace the "Status" zone chip with "Unallocated", and add Fostered and Hospitalised chips beside Adopted.** [done 2026-10-08, `claude/residents-and-nav-polish`: diagnosis confirmed on dev (all four statuses sit in the Lifecycle zone). `?unallocated=1` filters `current_status = 'Unassigned'` and adds to picked zones; an old link to the Lifecycle zone means Unallocated. `?status=adopted|fostered|hospitalised`, `?adopted=1` still honoured; the hidden-match notice and the download cover all three. `/enclosures`' Lifecycle cards were already Hospital, Unassigned and Fostered only, so it never showed the adopted and is unchanged.] Lutan, 2026-10-08: picking the Status zone lists adopted animals as well as unallocated ones. **Decided by Lutan the same day:** that chip shows **only unallocated** residents and is renamed **Unallocated**; Fostered and Hospitalised get their **own chips next to Adopted**. **Why it happens today (read 2026-10-08, confirm on dev):** "Status" is the **Lifecycle pseudo-zone** (`SYSTEM_ZONE = "Lifecycle"`, `src/lib/enclosures/options.ts`), whose pseudo-enclosures hold Unassigned, Hospitalised, Fostered and Adopted residents. A zone pick filters `zone_id in (…)` (`applyFilters`, `src/lib/residents/list-view.ts` ~line 73), and the list's only default status filter is "not deceased" (`listQuery` ~182), so all four come through; that contradicts the file's own comments (~37, ~140) and the page's `adoptedHidden` count (`residents/page.tsx` ~137), which assume a zone pick leaves the adopted out. **Build:** (1) on `/residents`, the Lifecycle zone is no longer offered as a zone; in its place an **Unallocated** chip filters `current_status = 'Unassigned'` (status, not zone, per the existing "by status rather than zone" rule in `applyFilters`); it can sit with the zone chips since unallocated animals are on site. Each card is encoded with the resident's link, **`/r/<R-code>`** (`src/lib/tags/links.ts`, from 2026-09-22's "Copyable links for enclosure QR codes and resident RFID cards"), which normally opens the resident's page. Phone-only by definition (no PCs on site). - [ ] **Prescription schedule: three round ticks instead of a frequency list (design to settle first).** Lutan, 2026-10-04, from the whiteboard form (*Amoxicillin, 2 tablets, Morning / Lunch / Evening ticks, start, end*): perhaps the `frequency` table is not needed. Agreed shape: a prescription's pattern is one of three kinds. **Daily:** the ticks are the truth and `doses_per_day` is their count. **Every N days / weeks / months:** the interval lives on the prescription (a weekly tablet or monthly flea treatment has no honest tick pattern); it still holds a round (0138 defaults it to morning) and `doseDueState()` and `prescription_doses_between()` (0044) already work from interval plus start date. **As needed:** an explicit choice with no ticks, so an empty set is never confused with a mistake (the `none` vs `ok` status views). Edge cases to settle before building: (1) **more than three doses a day** (four- or six-hourly) cannot fit three rounds, so forbid it or add a fourth round (one `insert` into `rounds`); (2) **different amounts per round** (2 in the morning, 1 in the evening) cannot be expressed by one `dose_quantity`, and is likelier to come up than the others; (3) **stock forecast and usage-versus-plan** read `doses_per_day`, so they would read the tick count; (4) **existing prescriptions** all carry `frequency_id` and Management edits the frequency list today, so the migration needs a back-fill and that screen needs a replacement. Dropping `frequency_id` is a schema stream of its own (migration PR first, per CLAUDE.md). Not part of `medical-round-screens`, which reads `prescription_rounds` and `frequency` as separate sources and so is not blocked by this either way. Also decides where the add-prescription ticks live (Management, not the Head of Medical's screens). **ANSWERED by Lutan, 2026-10-04 — edge case (2): yes, a prescription can give different amounts per round.** Two in the morning and one in the evening is a real prescription, and the item already flagged this as *"likelier to come up than the others"*. **So `dose_quantity` moves from the prescription to the round**: the amount belongs on `prescription_rounds`, not on `prescriptions`. That is a schema change on top of `0138`, with a back-fill copying each prescription’s single amount onto every round it holds, and it reshapes the add-prescription form from one amount box to one per ticked round. **It also changes three readers:** the medication list and the pick list sum per round rather than dividing a daily figure, and edge case (3)’s stock forecast reads the per-round amounts summed rather than `doses_per_day` × one quantity. **None of this blocks what is already built** — `medical-round-screens` (#357) reads `prescription_rounds` and `frequency` as separate sources, so it keeps working until the amount moves. **Still to settle: (1)** more than three doses a day (four- or six-hourly) cannot fit three rounds — forbid it, or add a fourth round, which is one `insert` into `rounds`; and **(4)** the back-fill and the replacement for the frequency screen, since dropping `frequency_id` is *"a schema stream of its own"*.

Lutan, 2026-10-03: "We seem to have a disconnect between Clinic, vets and Doctors." **The model, decided by Lutan the same day:** (1) **A Clinic is what the system used to call a Vet.** It is the place a resident is taken to and a visit is booked with. **"Vet" goes from the system entirely** (data, screens, menus, both languages, manual) so the word cannot mean two things. views (`vet_contacts` from 0126 and anything else with `vet` in it). **The `vet` role becomes `doctor`** (confirmed by Lutan, 2026-10-03: the vet login is the doctor's login): `alter type app_role rename value 'vet' to 'doctor'` keeps existing policies working, because they store the enum value, not the text, but every literal `'vet'` in `src/`, `worker/` and the check scripts has to change in the same release. (b) alone hides residents seen by a colleague at the same clinic, and a visit with no doctor recorded (optional, always) is then seen by no doctor login at all, so (c) is the likely answer. The 2-decimal cost column refuses sub-1% precision, e.g. per-gram prices: follow-up on the backlog branch] From the backlog page's suggestion box (2026-09-26), confirmed by Lutan 2026-09-29. Dry kibble is bought in 20 kg bags but given to dogs by the cup; medicines arrive by the box or bottle but are given by the tablet or ml. **Today each item has exactly one unit**, used for everything: `diet_types.unit` (0051: "daily_qty_* and cost_per_unit are in this unit") and `medication.dose_unit` (0027). Stock on hand (0083), stock counts (0093) and deliveries (`stock_receipts`, 0096, which records the unit at receipt and expects "2 boxes of 50" to be converted by hand before saving) all use that same unit. So staff either count kibble in cups or feed in kilograms, and the forecast, stock and cost figures are only as right as that mental arithmetic. **Shape:** keep the item's existing unit as its **base unit** (the one feeding or dosing is recorded in, and what the forecasts already compute), and add a small per-item **conversion table**: other units it is bought, received or counted in, each with how many base units one of it holds (e.g. kibble: base `cup`; `kg` = 10 cups, `bag (20 kg)` = 200 cups; a tablet medicine: `box` = 50 tablets, `strip` = 10). Per item, not global, because a cup of one kibble weighs differently from another. Mark one conversion as the **purchase unit** and one as the **count unit** (can be the same) so forms default sensibly. **Where it is used:** "Record a delivery" takes a quantity in any of the item's units and stores both what was entered (quantity + unit) and the base-unit equivalent. The stocktake sheet (and the phone cards in the item above) counts in the count unit, e.g. "3 bags and 4 kg" if mixed entry is worth it, and saves base units through `record_stocktake()`. Stock on hand and days-of-stock can be shown in the purchase unit ("2.4 bags, about 11 days"). Cost moves to a **price per purchase unit** (what the receipt says: 850 baht a bag), with cost per base unit derived for the diet and medication forecasts and Cashflow. Doses, prescriptions, diets and forecasts stay in the base unit, so nothing there changes. **History must not shift:** existing counts and receipts are in today's single unit, which becomes the base unit, so they need no rewrite. Editing a conversion factor later must not silently re-value past rows, so each row keeps the base-unit amount it was saved with (0096 already snapshots the unit for the same reason). **Schema PR first** (a conversions table keyed on medication or diet type, like `stock_counts`' item-kind pair, plus the entered quantity/unit columns on `stock_receipts` and `stock_counts`); admin and management edit conversions on Management → Medications / Diets. Decide while building: whether a conversion factor can be approximate (a cup of kibble) and whether the page should say so; mixed-unit entry on the stocktake or one unit per line; and whether this settles the related open item "A single-cell stock edit writes no history". Check Stock between counts and Cashflow arithmetic end to end with a real kibble example. Manual (Medications, Diets, Stocktake, Deliveries topics), both dictionaries, a releases line and a `docs/decisions.md` entry for the base-unit rule. **Schema half done 2026-09-30 as `claude/schema-units-of-measure` (0118; see `docs/decisions/2026-09-30-units-of-measure-schema.md`) — the feature half builds against this:** table `item_unit_conversions` (`item_kind` + `medication_id` / `diet_type_id` as in `stock_counts`; `unit`, `base_units_per` > 0, `is_purchase_unit`, `is_count_unit` with at most one of each per item, `note`; unique per item by lower-cased unit; admin and management write, admin / management / staff / volunteer read). The base unit is the item's existing `dose_unit` / `unit`, unchanged. **The point-in-time factor** is `entered jsonb` on both `stock_receipts` and `stock_counts`: `[{"quantity","unit","factor"}]`, a copy of the factors in force when the row was saved, so editing a conversion never re-values history; `quantity` / `counted_quantity` stay the base-unit total and a CHECK requires sum(quantity × factor) to equal it. Null `entered` = entered in the base unit (all existing rows). `record_stocktake(jsonb, jsonb)` keeps its signature and now accepts an optional `entered` per element beside `id` and `count` (count in base units). Deliveries are written straight to `stock_receipts`: set `quantity` (base) and `entered` together. No cost column: price per purchase unit ÷ `base_units_per`. Still to do in the feature half: the forms and pages, refusing a conversion named like the base unit, stamping `factor` from the live conversion at save time, and the open decisions above.
- [x] **Stock on hand and days-of-stock.** Neither medications nor diets record what's actually in the cupboard, so the forecasts say what will be used but not when it runs out. Split out of the medication requirement page item when that closed (2026-09-21).

- [x] **Doctors belong to a vet: investigate a managed list rather than free text.** Lutan, 2026-09-27, during Pass 0 of the role walkthrough. A clinic has many doctors — Novel has around 20 on staff — and the concern raised was that the relationship is modelled the wrong way round. It is not: `doctor_name` sits on `vet_appointments`, not on `vets`, so one vet already has many doctors. What is missing is anywhere to **manage** them. The column is free text by Lutan's own call on 2026-09-24 (`0074`, `docs/decisions.md`), with the cost written down at the time — "Dr Somchai" and "Somchai" stay two strings, so counting visits per doctor means grouping by hand — and that migration closed with "Promoting it to a lookup is its own item if that is ever wanted". This is that item. Today the only affordance is `loadDoctorNamesByVet` (`src/lib/vets/doctors.ts`), which harvests the distinct names already typed against each vet and offers them as a `datalist` on the vet-visit form. That stops a name being typed three ways, but a doctor nobody has recorded yet is not suggested, a typo becomes a permanent suggestion, and there is no screen where a clinic's roster can be seen or corrected. **To investigate:** whether a `vet_doctors` table (vet_id, name, active) with a nullable `vet_appointments.doctor_id` beside the existing text column earns its keep; how the names already recorded would be reconciled into it; and whether the shelter will actually maintain a 20-name roster per clinic or would rather keep typing with better suggestions. Schema-first as its own PR if it goes ahead, and the free-text column stays for historical rows either way. Note for whoever picks this up: the walkthrough's Pass 0 line "Management → Vets has at least one vet, and at least one has a doctor name" was wrong — the vet record has no doctor field — and has been corrected in `docs/role-walkthrough.md`. **Decided 2026-09-27 (Lutan): build both.** Schema half is #176 (`0102_vet_doctors_and_vet_accounts.sql`, applied to dev): a `vet_doctors` list per clinic that fills itself from typed names by trigger, `doctor_name` kept and following the list, `merge_vet_doctors`, `p_doctor_name` on `schedule_bulk_appointments`, and `user_roles.vet_id` + `current_user_vet_id()` for the vet-account→clinic link items 4 and 8 need. **Feature half still to do:** the list on the clinic hub (view, rename, deactivate, merge), the booking form passing `p_doctor_name` instead of its second write, suggestions from the list instead of `loadDoctorNamesByVet`, choosing a vet account's clinic in `/admin/security`, manual and release-notes line; tick this item then. **Done 2026-09-28** (`claude/vet-doctors-roster-screen`): Management → Vets → Doctors lists each clinic's doctors with their visit counts, and renames (saying how many visits the new spelling reaches), merges (pointing out look-alike spellings such as "Somchai" / "Dr Somchai"), marks a doctor as left, and adds or deletes an unused one; the clinic hub shows the list read-only; booking passes `p_doctor_name` in the one RPC call; the visit forms suggest the clinic's active doctors. The `/admin/security` clinic choice had already shipped with the vet-scope work.

- [x] **A single-cell stock edit writes no history, but the `0093` back-fill treated past ones as counts.** [done 2026-09-29 as `claude/stock-edit-history`, migration `0112`: Lutan chose one way in — `record_stock_correction()` writes a `source = correction` row, kept out of usage intervals; see docs/decisions.md 2026-09-29] Found 2026-09-27 while clearing UAT's stock figures. `record_stocktake()` writes a `stock_counts` row per item (`0093`), and the stocktake sheet goes through it. `updateMedicationStock` and its diet twin (`src/app/management/medications/actions.ts`) do not: they `update` the column directly, so `0083`'s trigger stamps `stock_counted_at` and nothing lands in the history. The result is that **Stock between counts cannot see a figure typed on the Management page** — four such edits on UAT this morning left no trace in `stock_counts` at all. What makes it more than a design choice is that `0093`'s back-fill *did* capture exactly those edits, one synthetic stocktake each, because all it had to go on was `stock_on_hand` and `stock_counted_at`. So a cell edit made before `0093` is history and the same edit made after it is not, which is the kind of split nobody will reconstruct later from the data. **To decide:** either route the single-cell edit through `record_stocktake()` so there is one way in, or leave it out of history on purpose and say so on the page — and either way `0093`'s comment should stop implying the two agree. Worth settling before the first real count, since that is when the history starts being worth something. **The display half is now done too (2026-10-01, `claude/stock-count-source`):** Lutan chose Stock between counts only, so a row there says when a figure was typed by hand during the dates being compared, in the table and in the CSV. No figure changes — a correction is still never paired into an interval. Labelling back-fill rows so they stop passing as real stocktakes was considered and declined for now, and is noted as still open in `docs/decisions/2026-10-01-corrections-on-stock-between-counts.md`.

- [x] **A vet's photo upload should be limited to the Medical folder.** Lutan, 2026-09-27, Pass 1 (Vet) of the role walkthrough. **Done 2026-09-27** (`claude/medical-photos-profile`): no picker for a vet, and the upload route answers 403 to any other folder. Confirmed a vet can add photos from the resident hub, which is intended (`assertPhotoWriteAccess` allows every app role), but the folder picker offers all of them. A vet has no reason to file into the shelter's general or project folders, and a misfiled clinical photo is awkward to find later. Restrict the choice to **Medical** for the vet role — ideally by not showing the picker at all when there is only one valid destination, so it reads as "this goes in Medical" rather than a one-item dropdown. Enforce it on the server too, not only in the form: the upload route is the thing that has to refuse.
- [x] **Five more places take a UTC day for a shelter day.** Found 2026-09-28 by `claude/utc-visit-date`, grepping `slice(0, 10)` across `src/` after fixing the three visit forms. Each takes the leading date of a stored UTC timestamp as a shelter day, so it is a day early between 00:00 and 07:00 Bangkok. (1) `residents/[id]/ResidentHub.tsx` builds `today` from `now.slice(0, 10)` (`now` is `new Date().toISOString()` from the page), so a prescription that ended yesterday still counts as active on the hub until 07:00. (2)–(4) `hospital/return/ReturnFromHospitalForm.tsx`, `rehome/RehomeForm.tsx` and `rehome/return/ReturnToShelterForm.tsx` set the date input's `min` from `placement_history.start_date.slice(0, 10)`. That column is `timestamptz`, and `placementStartDate()` stores `now` for a same-day move, so a placement made at 03:00 has a `min` one day too early. The server still refuses the date, but with an error rather than a greyed-out day. (5, minor) `maintenance/MaintenanceBoard.tsx` falls back to `updated_at.slice(0, 10)` against a shelter-day cutoff. Fix with `todayIso(new Date(x))`, as `visitDate()` does. Checked and fine: `immunizations/new/actions.ts` (date arithmetic on a date), `lib/management/cashflow.ts` (a `date` month), `lib/status/usage.ts` (Cloudflare analytics days are UTC by design).

- [x] **One weight per vet visit: hide visits that already have one.** Lutan, 2026-09-27, Pass 1 (Vet) of the role walkthrough. Today a person belongs to exactly one clinic in two places, and both need to allow several. **(1) The doctor roster:** `vet_doctors` (0102) has a single `vet_id`, so a doctor who also works at a second clinic has to be entered twice, as two unrelated rows, and nothing shows they are the same person. Make the doctor the person and add a link table, e.g. `vet_doctor_clinics (doctor_id, vet_id)`, keeping the name-key uniqueness per clinic. **Careful:** `vet_appointments` has a composite foreign key `(vet_id, doctor_id) → vet_doctors (vet_id, id)` that guarantees a visit's doctor works at the visit's clinic; that guarantee must move to the link table, not be dropped. Existing duplicate rows for the same person at two clinics can be merged afterwards from the clinic page (a "same person as…" merge), not guessed by name in the migration. **(2) Vet logins:** a vet account has one clinic, `user_roles.vet_id`, read through `current_user_vet_id()` by 18 places across `0102`, `0108` (which residents a vet sees) and `0110` (which clinic a vet may write for), plus `src/lib/vets/scope.ts`. Several clinics means a set: e.g. `user_vet_clinics (user_id, vet_id)` and a `current_user_vet_ids()` returning an array, with every policy changed from `= current_user_vet_id()` to `= any(current_user_vet_ids())`. A vet then sees the union of the residents their clinics treat; the vet-visit form's clinic, today fixed to their one clinic, becomes a choice among theirs (preselected when there is only one); Settings → Security gets a multi-select for a vet's clinics. Keep `current_user_vet_id()` working until nothing calls it, or replace all callers in the same PR. **Decided by Lutan, 2026-10-01: both,** the roster doctor and the vet login, **and a vet login is linked to its own doctor entry.** So: (3) a nullable, unique `user_id` on the doctor (one login is one doctor, and one doctor has at most one login), set in Settings → Security beside the vet's clinics (pick an existing doctor, or create one from the user's name). A linked vet's clinics should come from their doctor's clinics rather than be kept twice: decide while building whether `user_vet_clinics` is needed at all, or whether a vet's clinic set is simply the clinics of the doctor their login is linked to (simpler, one source of truth; an unlinked vet login then has no clinics and sees nothing, as today's login with no clinic does). When a linked vet records a visit, the Doctor field is themselves, prefilled and locked to their own entry; staff and admins still choose any doctor at the visit's clinic. A doctor removed from a clinic keeps their past visits there. **Most doctors will have no login (Lutan, 2026-10-01):** many of the vets residents are taken to never use the system, so adding a doctor must need only a name and their clinic(s), with **no email, account or invitation**. That stays possible from the clinic page and from the vet-visit form (typing a new name, as today). A login is linked to a doctor afterwards, only if that doctor is ever given one, and unlinking or archiving the login leaves the doctor and their visits untouched. **Schema PR first,** then the feature; test with a vet login on two clinics that it sees both clinics' residents and no others, can record for either, and is refused for a third (`scripts/` check like the 0108 / 0110 harnesses). Manual (Vets, Security), both dictionaries, a releases line and a decision file in `docs/decisions/`. **Schema half done on `claude/schema-doctor-multi-clinic` (migration 0125, 2026-10-02); the feature half remains. Build against this:** `vet_doctors` is now the person (`vet_id` kept, nullable and deprecated = first-listed clinic, so current pages still work; new `user_id` unique, set only by an admin at aal2, by trigger). `vet_doctor_clinics (vet_id, doctor_id, active, name_key)`, PK `(vet_id, doctor_id)`, is the link; "removed from a clinic" is `active = false` (a link a visit uses cannot be deleted); unique `(vet_id, name_key)` is the per-clinic spelling rule. The visit guarantee is the composite FK `vet_appointments (vet_id, doctor_id)` -> `vet_doctor_clinics (vet_id, doctor_id)`; moving a visit to another clinic re-resolves the typed name to that clinic's own doctor. No `user_vet_clinics`: a vet login's clinics = its linked doctor's active clinics, `current_user_vet_ids()` (uuid[]), UNION `user_roles.vet_id` until you move Settings -> Security onto the doctor link, backfill a doctor per login that has only `vet_id`, and drop that column. `current_user_vet_id()` still exists with no SQL callers; `src/lib/vets/scope.ts` still reads `user_roles.vet_id`, so switch it to the set and remove the function. Staff and management cannot edit the links of a doctor who has a login (admin only), and a vet writes links only for their own clinics, so the clinic page needs to handle those refusals. `merge_vet_doctors(from, into)` now merges across clinics (clinics, visits and login move; admin only if a login is involved; two logins refuse): call it for the "same person as..." merge. Not merged by name anywhere. Test with `scripts/check-doctor-multi-clinic.mjs`.

- [x] **Upcoming vet visits for the Director: one page (list and calendar) with each resident and clinic; stretch goal, booked visits appear in her Google Calendar.** Lutan, 2026-10-08, for the Director. **What exists:** visits are `vet_appointments` (date and time, clinic `vet_id`, optional doctor, status, reason), booked from the resident hub, `/vet-visits/new` and the bulk booking (`schedule_bulk_appointments`). The only all-visits page is `/appointments` (`src/app/appointments/page.tsx`), and it is **a vet's page by design**: it refuses anyone not on the `own_clinic` scope, so the Director, who books, has no view of everything coming up. Each visit: the resident's **name and photo**, **clinic**, doctor if set, date and time, reason, a link to the resident and to the visit's Edit. Reuse `loadClinicAppointments()` (`src/lib/vets/appointments.ts`) without the clinic filter rather than writing a second query. (2) **Two views:** a **list grouped by day** (Today, Tomorrow, then each date; overdue Scheduled visits at the top in their own group, since "a past visit still Scheduled" is how the app shows overdue). **A Hide overdue switch (Lutan, 2026-10-08):** overdue visits are usually done and only waiting for test results before someone marks them finished, so the Director wants them out of her way; one tap hides the overdue group on both views, the choice is remembered on her device (a per-viewer convenience, not a setting), and the page says how many are hidden ("3 overdue hidden, show") so none is lost from sight. Worth raising while building, not deciding here: if "done, waiting for results" is the normal state, a status of its own (e.g. **Awaiting results**) would say so honestly and let overdue mean genuinely missed; that is a status change on `vet_appointments` (schema PR, and the vet visit form's Status options), so ask Lutan first as the default on a phone, and a **week / month calendar** for the PC, each visit a short chip (resident · clinic), tapping opens it. Build the calendar as a plain CSS grid, no library, unless the build shows otherwise. Filter by clinic; hide Cancelled and Completed by default. Dates day-first and in the shelter's time zone (`todayIso()`, `formatDate`), and Thai in Buddhist Era like the rest of the app. (3) **Stretch: her Google Calendar.** Three ways, cheapest first, and the item should ship (a) and settle (b) or (c) with Lutan: **(a) "Add to Google Calendar" link** on each visit and straight after booking — a `calendar.google.com/calendar/render?action=TEMPLATE&…` URL pre-filled with title ("Vet: Panda · Novel Clinic"), time and a link back to the visit. No setup, no tokens; she taps once per visit. Does not follow later changes. **(b) A calendar feed (iCal / `.ics` subscription):** a route such as `/api/calendar/<secret>.ics` listing upcoming visits, which she adds once in Google Calendar ("From URL"). Every visit appears and updates on its own, no Google API. Limits to say out loud: Google refreshes subscribed calendars only every few hours to a day, it is read-only, and the URL is a secret anyone holding it can read, so it carries only resident name, clinic and time (no medical detail), uses a long random token per person that can be revoked and reissued (stored hashed), and is refused once the person is archived. **(c) Write events with the Google Calendar API:** each booking, change and cancellation creates, moves or deletes an event in her calendar, immediately. Needs her own Google consent (a Calendar scope; the shelter's existing OAuth client is the Drive one, and adding a scope means re-consent, possibly verification, see the Google Cloud stocktake item), a stored refresh token per person and its expiry risk (the 2026-09-25 Drive outage), and an event id kept on the visit. Most work and most fragile; only if (b)'s delay is not acceptable. **Recommendation:** list + calendar page, (a) on every visit, then (b). (c) only on her explicit ask. Schema only if (b) needs a token table or (c) an event-id column: then a schema PR first. Manual (a "Vet visits" topic, and how to subscribe in Google Calendar), both dictionaries, a `releases.ts` line, and a test plan: a visit at 03:00 Bangkok (the UTC-day trap), a cancelled visit, a Thai reader, the feed refused for an archived login. **Shipped (2026-10-13, `claude/vet-visits-director`):** `/upcoming-visits` (not `/vet-visits`, which redirects to `/clinic-visits`), under Shelter Operations, for `medical.visits` read at the shelter-wide scope; list by day with an Overdue group, Hide overdue (per device) with its hidden count, clinic filter, Completed and Cancelled off by default, and a week/month CSS-grid calendar from md up. No migration. The Awaiting results status question was put to Lutan, not built. **Stretch (3), the Google Calendar link / feed, is filed as its own item below.**

- [ ] **Two-way calendar: moving or deleting a vet visit in Google Calendar changes it in the app (phase 2 of the calendar item above; build that first).** Lutan, 2026-10-15, for the Director: once a visit is in her calendar, she would like to "move it in her calendar and push the change back to the system so she can manage her calendar as normal and the system polls for changes made to the calendar item in Google. This would also work for cancellations where a deletion from the calendar cancels the appointment in the system." **Possible, and free.** **How:** (1) every event the app creates carries the visit's id in the event's private properties (`extendedProperties.private.visitId`), so the app only ever looks at its own events and ignores everything else in her calendar (her other appointments, her hand-made entries); (2) the Worker's existing 15-minute cron asks Google for **only what changed since last time** (`events.list` with a `syncToken`, stored per calendar), so it is one small call per run; Google's push notifications (a `watch` channel) would be faster but need renewing about weekly and a public endpoint, so poll first and add push only if 15 minutes proves too slow; (3) **a moved event** sets the visit's date and time to the event's new start (in Asia/Bangkok); a change to the end time, title or description is ignored and put back on the next app-side sync, since the visit has no end and the title is generated; (4) **a deleted event** cancels the visit. **Safeguards to agree with Lutan, because a calendar delete is easy to do by accident on a phone:** the visit is marked cancelled with the reason *"Cancelled from Google Calendar"*, never deleted, so it can be restored; System status or the Upcoming visits page lists anything changed from the calendar in the last week; and (recommended) an email or in-app note to the Director saying "Novel - Blackie on 20 Oct was cancelled in your calendar; it is cancelled in Lanna Care too", so a mistaken delete is noticed. **Loops and conflicts:** the app records the event's `updated` time and etag after each write and ignores a change that is its own; if a visit was changed in the app **and** in the calendar since the last sync, the **app wins** and the calendar is put back, and the clash is listed for someone to look at (rare: one person, two places). A visit already completed is not changed by a calendar edit. **Who did it:** Google does not reliably say which person moved an event, so the audit row records the change as made *via Google Calendar* (the calendar's owner), not a named login. **Scope:** the same `calendar.events` token as the calendar item already reads as well as writes, so no new consent. **Limits to tell her:** a change shows in the app within about 15 minutes, not instantly; only entries the app created are synced back (if she drags a hand-made entry, nothing happens); a new entry she types in the calendar does **not** create a visit (booking stays in the app, where the resident and clinic are chosen). Schema: a `calendar_sync_state` row (calendar id, sync token, last run) and the visit's `calendar_etag`; one schema PR, or fold into the calendar item's if both are built together. Manual (moving and cancelling from your calendar), releases line, decision file, test plan: drag an event to another time and see the visit move within 15 minutes; delete one and see the visit cancelled with the reason and the note sent; change it in both places and see the app's version win and the clash listed; edit an unrelated event and see nothing change.
