## Admin

- [x] **A separate "Add resident photos" card, so volunteers can take a photo first and tag it to a resident, into the Shelter folder only (small schema PR, then app).** Lutan, 2026-10-17: "separate access card needed for add resident photo. I want volunteers to be able to add resident photos by taking photo first then tagging to a resident", then **"but only Shelter folder."** **Today (read 2026-10-17 on `main`):** the photo-first flow already exists, `/photos/add` (`src/app/photos/add/`, take or pick photos, then choose the resident, uploaded through the same routes as the hub), guarded by the activity `photos.resident_add` (`catalogue.ts:69`, `routes.ts` ~259). But **only the Residents card gives that activity** (`cards.ts` ~81), together with editing the record, moves, rehoming and deaths, so a volunteer cannot have it without far more than they need. And the folders offered come from `photoCategoriesFor()` (`src/lib/google/drive-client.ts` ~66): **all four folders for a login that may publish (`photos.resident_publish`), and Medical only for anyone else**, so a volunteer given the activity today would be offered **Medical** and nothing else, the opposite of what is wanted. **Build:** (1) **A new card, "Add resident photos"** (`cards.ts`, label in both dictionaries), opening `/photos/add`, whose bundle is the add-photos right plus the **who-and-where** read of residents the picker needs (`resident_who_and_where`, which volunteers already read). Give it to the **Volunteer** role on Settings → Who does what (a setting once the card exists). (2) **Shelter folder only, enforced, not just offered:** recommended, a **new activity** `photos.shelter_add` (yes/no) in the catalogue (**schema PR**: the `permission_activities` row, and the upload routes' and `record_attachment`'s folder checks taught it), granted by this card, under which the flow offers **only Shelter** (no folder choice shown at all) and the upload route and database **refuse any other folder** for that login, so a direct call cannot file into Medical, Foster or Adoption. `photoCategoriesFor()` returns `["Shelter"]` for such a login. The Residents card and the Head of Medical's jobs keep what they have today. (3) **Decide with Lutan before building, because Shelter photos are public:** non-Medical photos show on the resident's **public page** (`public_resident_photos`, `0101`), so a volunteer's photo would go **straight onto the website** once the site is unlocked. Options: (a) accept that (simple; staff can remove one); or (b) a volunteer's photo is held as **"waiting for approval"** and appears publicly only after someone with `photos.resident_publish` approves it. Recommended (b) if volunteers are many or new, (a) if they are a few trusted people; ask. (4) Volunteers cannot delete, move or set a profile photo from this (those stay with the Residents card). Manual (Adding photos as a volunteer), releases line, decision file, test plan on a phone signed in as a volunteer: take a photo, pick a resident by name or R-code, it lands in the Shelter folder; no folder choice is shown; a direct upload to Medical is refused; they cannot delete or move a photo; the photo shows on the resident's page (and publicly, or after approval, per the decision). **ADDED 2026-10-17 (Lutan): the card is for Volunteers, Management and the 2IC**, not volunteers alone, so name and describe it for everyone ("Add resident photos: take a photo, then choose the resident"), and give it to all three roles. **How it combines with other cards:** the Shelter-only rule is what **this card alone** gives. A role that also holds a card with wider photo rights keeps them: **Management** holds the **Residents** card (all folders, publish, move, delete), so for Management this card adds the photo-first tile on the home screen and changes nothing about which folders it may use; rights are the union of a role's cards, as everywhere else. **The 2IC** holds no photo card today, so with this card she gets Shelter only, like a volunteer. The approval question in (3) then applies only to logins whose photos come in through this card alone (volunteers and the 2IC), not to Management. - [x] **Bug: Settings → Security shows "Minified React error #441" instead of saying what went wrong.** Reported by Lutan 2026-09-26 with a screenshot on the dev-coloured site: an action on the archived `manager@gmail.com` row (Restore or Delete) failed and the row showed only "Minified React error #441; visit https://react.dev/errors/441…". **What #441 is:** React's production stand-in for *any* error thrown from a Server Action (`resolveErrorProd` in `react-server-dom-*-client.browser.production.js`). In a production build the real message is stripped before it reaches the browser, so `throw new Error(...)` in a `"use server"` file never shows its text to the user, **not even the friendly translated ones** (`t.admin.security.errors.cantDeleteOwnAccount` and the like). **So it is two fixes. (1) This page:** `src/app/admin/security/actions.ts` throws in every action (create, approve, change role, temporary password, archive, restore, delete). Make each return a result (`{ ok: true } | { ok: false, error: string }`) and have `UsersTable.tsx` / `AccessRequests.tsx` / `CreateUserForm.tsx` show `error`. Map known failures to plain words in both languages. Log the raw error server-side. **The failure in the screenshot is confirmed** (Lutan, 2026-09-26): it was **Delete** on a login with records against it. About 20 foreign keys to `auth.users` have no delete rule, so a delete is refused as soon as the person created anything: `created_by` on ten tables (from 0001 on), `uploaded_by`, `updated_by`, `user_id` on `assistant_actions` (0070), and others. **Don't fix it by changing them to `on delete set null`:** that would erase who recorded what, and that history is the point. Archive (0063) is the right tool for someone who has left. Instead, Delete is for accounts with no history (a typo, a test login). Before deleting, check the references (a small `security definer` function that counts them, or catch the error), and either hide Delete for such users or answer "This person has records in the system, so they can't be deleted. Archive them instead." **(2) The same pattern across the app:** at planning time 13 `"use server"` files under `src/app` held 98 `throw new Error` lines. Every one that can happen in normal use (validation, "not allowed", a clash) shows #441 in production. Sweep them to the return-a-result shape (the `upload-worker-error` fix already did this for uploads). Keep `throw` only for genuinely unexpected failures, and give those a generic "Something went wrong, please try again" plus the error's digest so it can be looked up in the Worker logs. Do the Security page first as its own small PR, then the sweep. The manual needs no change. Add a releases line (people will see real messages).

The other `"use server"` files under `src/app` still `throw new Error(...)` for ordinary refusals (validation, not allowed, a clash), and every one of those shows "Minified React error #441" in production — including `assertAdminRole()` on the other `/admin` pages. Sweep them to the same type (and fold the existing near-duplicates, `FriendActionResult`, `ProjectActionResult`, `MaintenanceActionResult`, `TranslationActionResult`, into it). Verify against a production build (`next build` + `next start`); dev mode shows the real message and proves nothing. Probably one PR per area so they can run alongside other streams. - [x] **A logo or photo upload that exhausts the Worker shows the user a minified React error.** Done 2026-09-25: it was not the Worker. Next caps a Server Action body at 1 MB and rejects a larger one before the action runs, so every logo or Website photo between 1 and 15 MB failed where no app code could catch it (reproduced on dev: HTTP 500, `E394 Body exceeded 1 MB limit`). `next.config.ts` now lets the app's one limit through (`src/lib/uploads/limits.ts`, 15 MB, also used by every upload route), the clients pre-check the size and turn any thrown failure into words (`runUploadAction`), and `proxy.ts`'s 10 MB body cap was raised with it. What a Worker can really process is still unmeasured — see the follow-up item. Found 2026-09-24 on production, uploading a Shelter Friend logo: the page printed `Minified React error #441` and a link to react.dev, which decodes to "An error occurred in the Server Components render" — the message itself is stripped in production builds. The same image failed twice and a smaller one succeeded, so it is size- or format-dependent. It is **not** the app's own validation: `MAX_FILE_BYTES` (15 MB) and `ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES` both `return { error }` with readable text before Drive is touched, and the Drive calls themselves sit in a `try/catch` that returns a friendly message. So a file that passes validation is breaking *during* the upload, where nothing catches it. The likely mechanism: `drive.uploadFile` (`src/lib/google/drive.ts`) builds a multipart `Blob` holding the whole file in memory inside the Worker, and on the free plan that can exhaust memory or the 10 ms CPU budget — the same `1102` family as the render pressure the Pi origin is meant to fix. **Two things to do, and they are independent.** (a) Catch it: wrap the action so a resource failure reaches the user as "that image is too large to process — try one under about 2 MB" rather than a React error code. A user cannot act on `#441`, and it reads as the app being broken. (b) Decide the real limit: 15 MB is inherited from `admin/website/actions.ts` and is almost certainly higher than a Worker can actually process, so the number should reflect what works rather than what the form accepts. **The same limits and upload path are used by `/admin/website` photos and blood-test attachments** (`src/app/api/blood-tests/[id]/attachments/route.ts`), so whatever is wrong is wrong in three places. Worth re-testing after the Pi origin lands, since rendering and uploads move to real CPU and memory then and the failure may simply go away — but the error message should be fixed regardless, because the next resource limit will produce the same unreadable page.

Let each user choose the app's look and feel from a small set of colour themes (e.g. the current dark orange, a light theme, a high-contrast one, and one or two alternative accents), saved per user so it follows them between devices — a `user_preferences` row or `user_metadata` (preferences, not permissions, so user-editable metadata is fine here), with `localStorage` only as a no-flash cache. (1) A near-duplicate check in `load-residents.mjs`'s dry run — warn, do not refuse.** List each row matching an existing resident (**including archived and Lifecycle/Unassigned ones**) after stripping a bracket tag (`Noon` ~ `Noon (Daeng)`), by identical Thai name, or by close spelling; show the existing code, current enclosure and created date so a human can rule same-dog / different-dog. **Keep the exact-name refusal as it is.** **(2) `scripts/correct-resident.mjs`** — dry run by default, `--apply` to write, `--env` like the other scripts. `--remove R-nnnn` removes a resident with **no real history**, refusing if it has vet appointments, blood tests, prescriptions, weights beyond intake, immunizations, procedures, attachments/photos, adoption updates or a Drive folder; its seed placement and diet rows go with it inside one `begin…commit` (**the FKs have no cascade, and `0119` guards placement history — so check how the 2026-10-05 R-0240 delete got past it**, which is a finding in its own right). Print exactly what will be touched plus a before/after of the survivor; write the removed rows to `--receipt <path>` as JSON **before** deleting; refuse unless both codes exist and the names are similar, or `--force-names`. `--merge-into` only if it is clean to do, otherwise leave it out. **Constraints the brief recorded:** Lutan is non-technical here, so **output must be plain and the commands copy-paste**; **the script is the deliverable — no session runs it with `--apply` against any database**, dry runs against dev only, Lutan runs the apply; **no `process.exit()` after a `fetch`** (libuv assertion on Windows, see `load-residents.mjs`). No schema expected — if one is needed, stop and say so. Needs a decision file, the README scripts list, a `Bash(node scripts/correct-resident.mjs *)` permission rule for the main checkout, and `docs/test-plans/resident-corrections.md`. → *Admin* **SUPERSEDED IN PART 2026-10-06 (Lutan): the duplicate residents themselves were already sorted out by another session, so the incident half is closed.** What is left is only the *prevention*: the near-duplicate warning in the loader so the next bulk upload does not pass `Noon` against `Noon (Daeng)`, and a reviewable script so a correction does not depend on finding a session willing to do it. **Lutan noted the inconsistency plainly — one chat deleted R-0240 and another refused the same request for R-0220.** The inconsistency is the real complaint, and a fixed script anyone can run is the answer to it. **Low priority now; drop it if the loader is not used again.**
  - **2026-10-07 (`resident-view-grants-0160`): the R-0240 question is answered; the rest of the item is untouched.** `0119` never guarded a delete: its triggers fire on `placement_history` UPDATE and INSERT, and only the deceased lock fires on DELETE. A session reaches the database as `postgres` or with the service key, both of which bypass RLS, so no policy was the path either. The delete was simply allowed. Production's `audit_log` (residents audited since `0121`) should hold it, and the script's `--remove` checks remain the only guard. `docs/decisions/2026-10-07-view-write-grants.md`.

Stock is held and counted in base units, and **Counted in** picks the stocktake's default. **What is really single:** (a) **Bought in** is one unit per item, enforced by a unique index (`item_unit_conversions_*_purchase_key`), and it is what the **price** hangs on (Price per pack: one price per purchase unit, saved as a cost per base unit) and what **Purchasing** suggests buying in; so the 14 kg bag on special cannot carry its own price, and a cheaper 20 kg bag changes the per-kg cost only if someone re-enters the price. (b) A delivery records **one size per entry**: 2 × 20 kg plus 1 × 10 kg is two deliveries (`entered` is already an array for mixed lines, "still undecided" in `0118`). **Build:** (1) **Schema PR:** drop the one-purchase-unit index (keep one *default*, `is_default_purchase`, for forms); a price per purchase size, with a date (or take it from deliveries: `stock_receipts.cost` ÷ base quantity is the real price paid, which is better than a typed one when it exists); decide which wins and say so. (2) **Settings → Medications / Diets units:** tick **Bought in** on as many sizes as apply; the badge reads per size. (3) **Record a delivery:** several lines in one delivery (size, how many, cost), summed into base units with each line kept in `entered`; the phone steps get "Add another size". (4) **Price per pack:** a price per size; the per-base-unit cost the forecasts and Cashflow use comes from the most recent delivery's actual cost per base unit, else the default size's typed price; show which. (5) **Purchasing:** the need stays in base units; suggest it in the default size and show what it is in the others ("about 3 × 20 kg or 4 × 14 kg"), cheapest per base unit first when prices are known. (6) **Count in packs, several sizes at once (CHANGED 2026-10-12, Lutan, superseding "one counted-in unit"):** *"there might be 10 20KG bags, 4 x 10KG bags, 3 x 14KG bags and 1 x 5 KG bags in the store room. Given the level of education of the users it would not be practical for them to have to try to figure out the math of how many cups or kgs we have and it certainly wouldn't be good having to get them to calculate decimal places based on kg lots."* So the stocktake card (phone) and the sheet (desk) show **one row per size** the item has (each pack size, plus the base unit for loose stock), each a whole-number box with big + / − buttons, and the system adds them up and shows the total in plain words ("= 287 kg"); **nobody types a decimal or converts anything.** Saved through `record_stocktake()`'s existing `entered` array (one line per size, factor copied, `0118`), so no new function is needed; the base-unit total stays what every reader uses. **Open packs:** a half-used bag or a cut sleeve cannot be a whole number of packs, so offer the base unit row for loose stock where it is countable (tablets: count the loose tablets), and for feed a simple choice for an **open bag** (about full / about half / about a quarter / nearly empty) that the system turns into kg from the bag size; say plainly that it is an estimate. **Counted in** becomes the order the rows appear in (most common size first), not the only unit. Same rows on **Same as last time** (it repeats last count's lines, not just its total). Medicine works the same way: boxes, sleeves and loose tablets, totalled in tablets. **Check:** existing deliveries and counts keep their amounts (the factor is copied into each row, `0118`), and the forecasts' numbers do not move unless a price does. The only thing that works is typing a street address, and **in Thailand Google often places a typed address at the wrong spot, or on a different business**. **Reproduce first, with real rows** (dev, and read-only on production when Lutan asks): note the exact address text and the URL the tap opens, for each failing contact and friend. **How it works today:** the address field holds either typed text or a pasted maps link, sometimes with text after it. The typed address stays as the written address, for reading and for post. (4) **Fix the existing rows:** a script that lists every contact and friend with an address that is a dead `goo.gl/maps` link, a link that does not resolve, or plain text, so Lutan or the Director can re-share the right link for each; the map is hidden for those (not a 404) until fixed. (b) is weaker than written: Google kept active `goo.gl` links working after August 2025, so a `goo.gl/maps` link must be followed to be judged, not refused by its shape. A Management page listing, per medication, a **recommended purchase quantity** so whoever does the ordering does not have to work it out. **The sum, per item, in its own unit:** *expected stock now* = last counted quantity (`stock_counts` / `medication.stock_on_hand`, 0093) − scheduled usage since that count (the prescription forecast, `doses_per_day` × `dose_quantity`) + receipts since that count (`stock_receipts`, 0096); *needed* = scheduled usage over the chosen period (from today) + **safety stock**; *recommended purchase* = needed − expected stock now, **never below 0**, rounded up to a whole pack if a pack size is known. **Period picker:** 1 week / 2 weeks (and perhaps 1 month / custom), reusing `src/lib/management/forecast-window.ts` as the forecasts already do. **Safety stock:** a new optional `medication.safety_stock` (numeric, the item's unit, null = none), set on the add/edit form in Management → Medications when an item is created or later, for items that are always in use whatever is prescribed today — IV/sub-Q fluids and the common antibiotics are Lutan's examples. It is a floor kept on the shelf, so it is added to *needed* on every period. Consider also adding the supplier lead time already stored (`reorder_lead_days`, 0083) to the period, so stock ordered today still covers the period once it arrives — say which in decisions.md. **Build on what exists, do not fork it:** `src/lib/management/stock.ts` already takes forecast usage off the last count to give days of stock; move the "expected stock now" part into one helper both pages call (and check whether it adds receipts since the count yet — if not, fix it there, so Medications' days-of-stock and this page agree). **Show the working** in each row (counted X on <date>, used ~Y since, received Z, need W for the period + S safety) so nobody has to trust a bare number, flag items **never counted** rather than guessing, and flag a count older than a few weeks as unreliable. A CSV / printable list of just the items to buy, grouped by supplier (the receipts' `supplier_contact_id` gives the usual supplier), is the thing someone takes to the vet wholesaler. **Cover food too (Lutan, 2026-09-28):** `diet_types` carry the same stock columns, counts and receipts, so the page covers every diet as well as every medicine — a Medicines / Food switch or two sections. **Special diets matter most**, so list them before the standard diet (the standard-diet flag from the Facility diet item tells them apart) and make the safety stock available on `diet_types` too. Diet usage comes from the residents on each diet (the diet forecast the Diets page already shows), not prescriptions. **Schema first:** `safety_stock` on both `medication` and `diet_types` (and pack size, if wanted) as a small `-schema` PR. Home: Management (or Shelter Operations if the Settings/Management review moves stock there). Manual topic en/th; a releases line. **Schema half done 2026-10-02 as `claude/schema-purchasing` (0128; see `docs/decisions/2026-10-02-safety-stock-schema.md`) — the feature half builds against this:** `safety_stock numeric` (nullable, `>= 0`, null = none; zero is a real value, distinct from null) on **both** `medication` and `diet_types`, stored in the item's **base unit** (`dose_unit` / `unit`) like `stock_on_hand`, counts and receipts. The form may take it in the purchase unit but must convert to base on save, as deliveries do. **No unit column and no pack-size column:** the pack is the item's purchase unit in `item_unit_conversions` (0118), so round up to its `base_units_per`. Nothing reads the column yet; write access is whoever already edits those tables. The item stays open for the page, the forms and the shared expected-stock helper.

- [x] **Saving a Shelter Friend does not publish it, and nothing says so.** Found 2026-09-24 on production, and it cost a round of "the release did not deploy properly" before the cause was clear. Making a Shelter Friend is two steps — **Save** the details, then **Publish** — implemented as two separate actions (`updateFriend` and `setFriendPublished` in `src/app/management/shelter-friends/actions.ts`). After Save the profile is a draft: `published` stays `false`, `public_shelter_friends` correctly filters it out (the view is `where sf.published and c.archived_at is null`, 0076), and so the public `/friends` page shows its empty state, the nav entry stays hidden and the home-page thank-you strip does not appear. All of that is correct behaviour, and from the outside it is indistinguishable from the feature being broken or not deployed. The card gives no indication after saving that the profile is still a draft. Options, cheapest first: a line on the card after Save — "Saved as a draft. Publish to show this on the website." — or a visible Draft badge on an unpublished profile, or a prompt on Save offering to publish straight away. Worth doing before anyone other than Lutan uses the feature, because the failure mode is silent: nothing errors, nothing is missing, the page simply looks empty. Related: the public page's empty state ("We're just getting started on thanking the businesses that help us") is written for a visitor and reads as intentional, which is right for the public but gives staff no hint that their own unpublished draft is the reason they cannot see it.

- [x] **Base the vet forecast on recent visit frequency, not a flat per-visit estimate.** Asked for by Lutan 2026-09-23 while testing PR #60: "can we set it to look at an average rolling number of visits recorded per week in the last quarter x the cost per vet visit, or number booked for that week if it's more." Today the vet line is a flat typical-visit estimate edited on `/admin/website` — it does not know how often the shelter actually goes. The proposed rule is, per week, `max(rolling average visits/week over the last quarter, visits actually booked that week) x cost per visit`, so a quiet week still carries the historical rate and a busy one is not understated. Decisions to make before building: (a) the page forecasts by **month**, so either the weekly figure is aggregated up or the rule is restated monthly; (b) whether "cost per vet visit" stays the flat estimate or becomes the mean of actual `vet_appointments.cost` over the same quarter, which would make the whole line self-maintaining; (c) what a booked visit with a **known** cost does — it should surely use its own cost rather than the estimate, which means the rule is really `max(estimated visits, booked visits)` for the *count* and actual cost where known; (d) the empty case, where a shelter with no history gets an average of zero and the line silently reads nothing rather than "unknown". Note this interacts with the defect PR #60 already fixed, where `coalesce(va.cost, estimate)` over a LEFT JOIN charged the estimate to months with no visits at all — any frequency-based rule needs the same care about distinguishing "no visits" from "no data". **Looked at 2026-09-24 and left as the flat figure on Lutan's call:** dev held 71 completed visits, none with a `cost`, and 20 in the last quarter (about 1.5 a week) — so the frequency half has data but the cost half does not, and the change needs a migration while 0073 was in flight. See `docs/decisions.md` (2026-09-24). The dev query and the proposed rule are recorded there, so this is ready to pick up once invoices are being recorded.

(2) **Cumulative view, a line chart over the same 12 months:** **adoptions** and **deaths** as running totals from the first month shown (month 1's figure, then month 1 + 2, and so on); **intakes** the same, unless Lutan says to leave intakes out of this view; and a **residents in care** line. (3) **Residents in care, a new figure, and the one thing to confirm with Lutan before building:** his words are "total residents being average of the residents for the period". Recommended reading: **each month's point is the average number of residents in care during that month** (count on site each day from `placement_history`, shelter dates, then the month's mean; a resident in foster or hospital counts as in care, adopted and deceased do not; say which in the chart's note), which is honest about a month where many arrived and left. The other reading, **a running average from the start of the 12 months to each month**, would be a flatter line; ask which he means and say which was built. Either way the residents line sits on its own scale, as it is in the tens or hundreds while monthly adoptions are single figures: a second axis on the right, clearly labelled, or a small separate panel above, whichever reads better at 375 px; do not plot it on the adoptions scale. (4) Same colours as the bars (intakes primary, adoptions success, deaths danger) and a neutral for residents, a legend, the value on tap or hover, a text table underneath for screen readers, and a plain note under the chart saying what each line means. Hand-drawn SVG like today's chart, no new chart library; light and dark themes; Thai. Releases line (Management), test plan: toggle both ways; cumulative adoptions in the last month equal the sum of the 12 bars; residents in care checked by hand for one month against the placements; a month with no events keeps the running totals flat; 375 px, Thai, dark mode. **ANSWERED 2026-10-17 (Lutan), replacing point (3)'s average: the residents line is a DAILY running count, not a monthly average.** *"Run cumulative numbers based on start number + intake - fostered - adopted - deceased + returned, on a daily plot."* So: take the number of residents **at the shelter** on the first day of the 12 months (counted from `placement_history`), then step **one point per shelter day**: **+ intakes, - fostered out, - adopted, - deceased, + returned** (from foster or adoption) that day. This means **fostered residents are NOT counted as at the shelter** while away (a change from the recommendation above), and returns bring them back. **Decide and say in the PR:** whether a resident in **hospital** counts as at the shelter (recommended yes: still the shelter's responsibility and coming back), and **cross-check** the daily figure against a straight count of residents on site on a few dates; if they differ, a placement is missing a type, which is worth knowing. The x-axis becomes days across the 12 months (month labels on the axis); the adoptions and deaths lines stay running totals, drawn as steps on the same days. The residents line keeps its own scale, as before. *Done on claude/dashboard-cumulative-chart: hospital counts, intakes are in the view, cross-check found one Foster placement filed under the Unassigned enclosure (docs/decisions/2026-10-18-cumulative-trend-chart.md).*

The job was impossible from the moment it was assigned, and nothing said so at the point where it could have been prevented. **Filter the assignee list by what the job's target screen needs**: a stocktake job offers only the roles `canStocktake` allows (admin, management, staff, volunteer); a maintenance job only those who can write maintenance; and so on. The server action in `src/app/assistant/actions.ts` calls `loadAssistantContext()` for whoever asks, so a vet — who has no Assistant button and whose `/assistant` page shows only "can't use the assistant" — can still call it directly and get the resident list, vets and enclosure options, limited only by RLS. Writes and lookups each re-check the role; this one does not. Return an empty context with `notAuthorized` unless `canUseAssistant(role)`, the way `lookups.ts` does, and check whether `page.tsx` should skip loading for the same roles.
- [ ] **In-app chat assistant that does things, not just answers.** Raised 2026-09-22: the Director's biggest pain point is time, and the ask is an experience like working with Claude here — type "move Panda from A3 to B1" or "Bella died last night, lung problems" and the system makes the changes, popping a modal only when it needs something it can't infer. **Hosting (user's direction 2026-09-22):** the production assistant should run on an LLM the shelter hosts itself — on the Raspberry Pi 5 at home or a cloud box — not on a metered Claude subscription. Claude is for the prototype and for teaching: build against the Claude API first because it gets tool use right with the least effort, and while doing so record every real exchange (request, tool calls, corrections) into an eval set that the self-hosted model is then measured against and, if needed, fine-tuned on. To keep that swap possible the model layer must be **provider-neutral from the first commit**: one `src/lib/assistant/llm.ts` adapter that takes messages + tool definitions and returns text / tool calls, with a Claude implementation (`@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `claude-opus-5`, streaming, adaptive thinking; `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` as a Cloudflare secret) and an OpenAI-compatible implementation for whatever the shelter hosts (Ollama / llama.cpp / vLLM all speak that shape), selected by env var. Nothing outside the adapter may import a vendor SDK. **Honest sizing note for the Pi:** a Pi 5 with 8–16 GB runs a 3–8B quantised model at a few tokens/second; that is workable for a short reply but tool-calling accuracy in mixed Thai/English at that size is marginal and each turn will take tens of seconds. Expect the self-hosted target to be a small cloud GPU (or a hosted open-weight endpoint) and treat the Pi as the stretch goal — measure both against the eval set before deciding. **Shape:** a chat panel (slide-over from a header button, also a full page `/assistant`; works on the phone) that sends the conversation to a route handler which calls the adapter with a **fixed toolset that wraps the app's existing server-side operations** — never raw SQL. First tools: find resident (by name/Thai name/code, returning candidates), find enclosure, move resident (`src/lib/placements/move.ts`), send to / return from hospital (`hospital.ts`), record death (`deceased.ts`, with cause), foster/adopt/return (`rehome.ts`), log weight, log vet visit, log immunization, add prescription, and read-only lookups (resident hub summary, who is in an enclosure, what's due). Each tool runs under the caller's own Supabase session, so RLS and the role checks apply exactly as in the UI and the assistant can never do more than the person could by clicking. **Confirmation:** every write is a two-step — the model calls the tool with `dryRun: true`, the UI shows a preview card ("Move Panda (R-0042) from A3 → B1 today, no notes") with Confirm / Change / Cancel, and only a Confirm re-invokes the tool for real; irreversible ones (death) use the existing `ConfirmDialog` wording. This matters doubly for a smaller self-hosted model: the confirm step is what makes a mis-parsed request harmless. **Missing information:** a `request_details` tool the model calls when a required field is unknown (which of two residents named Panda; date of death when "last night" is ambiguous across midnight; the enclosure when only a zone was named) that renders a small modal form built from the tool's field spec; the answers go back as the tool result. **Ambiguity:** resident lookup always returns candidates with code, enclosure and photo so the model can ask "the Panda in A3 or the one in Foster?" instead of guessing. **Audit:** log each assistant conversation and every executed tool call (who, when, input, result, which model served it) to a new `assistant_actions` table, and stamp the resulting rows' notes with "via assistant" so the hub history shows it — this table doubles as the eval/training corpus. **Scope of first cut:** the placement and medical tools above, English + Thai input, admin/management/staff only (volunteers get read-only tools), no memory across conversations, Claude behind the adapter. **Second cut:** stand up the self-hosted model, run the eval set, switch the env var when it clears the bar. **Later:** voice input on the phone, "what happened this week" summaries from the management dashboard queries, drafting the Facebook post for a project. **Decide with the user before building:** whether low-risk logs (weight, immunization) may skip the confirm to keep it fast; the accuracy bar the self-hosted model must reach on the eval set before it replaces Claude; whether conversations are retained beyond the audit rows.

## Auth

- [x] **Name card taps under the new permissions: a signed-in person must never see less than a visitor, and what they see beyond that follows their role.** Lutan, 2026-10-07: with permissions now set per role (the roles build), does tapping a resident's name card still work? The intended rule: **signed in → the resident's page with medical; anonymous → the resident with general information only.** **What happens today (checked in the code, 2026-10-07):** `/r/<code>` (`src/app/r/[code]/page.tsx`) shows the **public card** to anyone signed out or signed in without app access (`public_viewer`), which is right. Anyone with app access is sent to `/residents/<id>`, and that page now depends on the role: (a) **Admin, Management, Staff:** the full page with medical. Right. (b) **The 2IC, Head of Medical, Head of Maintenance and volunteers:** these roles borrow `volunteer` underneath (`legacy_role`, `0136`, `0141`, `0143`), and a role without `resident.record` gets **`ResidentWhoAndWhere`** (`0134`): who the resident is and where it lives, **no medical, and less than the public card shows a stranger** (no bio, temperament, age or adoption details). So for them a tap is *worse* than not being signed in. (c) **A vet or doctor login:** the page is limited to residents their clinics treat (`0108`), so a card for any other resident gives **404**, where a visitor would have seen the public card. **The fix:** (1) **Never less than the public card.** When a signed-in person may not open the full record, `/r/<code>` shows them the public card's information (the same `public_resident_cards` view anyone could read) plus whatever their role adds, instead of the who-and-where page or a 404. The same rule on `/residents/<id>` itself. (2) **Medical follows permissions, not just being signed in.** Lutan's "signed in sees medical" is right for every role that can read medical records, but it is now a per-role choice: in the Director's draft (in Next up), the two Heads and volunteers have no "view residents and their records" tick, so they would **not** see medical; the Head of Medical's job is the medication list, not the record. **Ask Lutan whether that is what he and the Director want**, or whether everyone signed in should read a resident's medical history from a card, in which case it becomes a tick for those roles in her matrix, not a special case in the code. Record the answer in `docs/decisions/`. (3) **Keep the jobs landing** from the name card item (Medical records): a tap with a job waiting goes to that job, and a plain tap shows the resident with buttons for the person's own jobs. (4) **Make it provable:** add the card to the permissions parity check or a `scripts/check-*.mjs`: for each role (signed out, `public_viewer`, Admin, Management, Staff, 2IC, both Heads, volunteer, vet inside and outside their clinic), tap a card and assert it lands on the public card, the public card plus extras, or the full record, and never on no-access or 404. Both dictionaries, Manual ("Scanning a name card"), a releases line.

- [x] **Settings → Security requires 2-step verification.** Done 2026-09-27 (see `docs/decisions.md`): `/admin/security/verify` sets up an authenticator app and asks for the code once per sign-in; all eight Security actions check `aal2` themselves; Reset in the new 2-step column and `bootstrap-admin.mjs --reset-2step` are the recovery routes; no recovery codes. Everything else stays as it is: the rest of the app changes shelter data, which can be corrected or reversed, so it keeps today's sign-in (password or Google). **Why 2-step and not "Google only":** the admins use personal Gmail accounts, so nothing enforces or reveals whether Google's own 2-step verification is on, and Google-only adds a lock-out if that sign-in ever breaks. Supabase Auth's built-in authenticator-app (TOTP) factor is free on the current plan, and a session that has passed it carries `aal2` in its JWT, so the rule can be checked in code and in the database. **Build:** (1) **Step-up, not a new login:** opening Security with an `aal1` session (`supabase.auth.mfa.getAuthenticatorAssuranceLevel()`) goes to a small page. The first time, it enrols an authenticator app (QR code + a manual key, verify one code, then show a few one-time recovery codes if Supabase supports them, otherwise explain the recovery route below). After that it asks for the 6-digit code and returns to Security. The same step-up works whether the admin signed in with a password or with Google. (2) **Enforce it where the power is, not just on the page:** every server action in `src/app/admin/security/` checks `aal2` itself before doing anything, since the service-role calls there bypass RLS. Add an RLS check (`auth.jwt()->>'aal' = 'aal2'`) on writes to `user_roles` too, so no path can change a role without it; that part is a small schema PR first. (3) **Settings landing page:** the Security tile says it needs your authenticator app. **Recovery:** a lost phone must not lock the shelter out. Another admin who has passed 2-step can reset a colleague's factor from Security, and `scripts/bootstrap-admin.mjs` (service role, run by Lutan) can remove a factor as the last resort. Write both down in README and `docs/decisions.md`. **Test on dev first:** confirm the `aal` claim after TOTP verification, what a Google session reports, how long `aal2` lasts in a session, and that a step-up survives the proxy's refresh. Manual (Security topic: set up the app, what to do if the phone is lost), both dictionaries, a releases line, a test plan covering each refused path, and the security review item should note it. **Not in scope:** requiring 2-step for management pages or for sign-in generally. Revisit if salaries (Management) land, since those figures cannot be "undone" once seen.

## Architecture

- [x] **Fable review of the database structure, ending in a report.** Lutan, 2026-10-13: "Fable review of database structure and report." **Who and how:** a session on the Fable model (`claude-fable-5-1`), **read-only**: it reads `supabase/migrations/` (about 180 files, latest `0181`), the decision files that explain them (`docs/decisions/`, `docs/roles-and-permissions.md`), and queries the **dev** database's catalogue through the same Management API the scripts use (`pg_catalog`, `information_schema`, `pg_stat_user_tables`, `pg_stat_user_indexes`, `pg_stat_statements` if enabled, `EXPLAIN` on the app's heaviest reads). **Never production**, no writes, no migrations; the report is the deliverable. Narrower and deeper than *Top-to-bottom architectural review by Fable* (done 2026-10-11, `docs/architecture-review-2026-09-22.md`), which covered the whole system: read its database and security findings first, and the fifteen items it filed, and build on them rather than repeating them; say which of its findings this review confirms, deepens or disagrees with. **Ask for:** (a) **a plain description of the database as it is**: the main areas (residents and placements, medical, stock, maintenance, people and roles, website, donations), how they connect, a diagram, checked against the README; (b) **structure:** tables and columns no code reads any more (left behind by renames such as `0172` and the enum drop `0180`/`0181`), duplicated data that can drift apart, missing foreign keys, `not null` and `check` constraints the app relies on but the database does not enforce, money and date types (`numeric`, `date` vs `timestamptz` and the Bangkok-day handling), naming consistency; (c) **security:** every table's RLS against the permissions model (`has_permission()`, scope helpers), every `security definer` function and owner-run view (the multi-tenancy spike counted 58 and 38), grants to `anon` and `authenticated`, anything readable more or less widely than the app intends (the `resident_who_and_where` finding of 2026-10-12, empty for Admin and Management, is the kind of thing to look for, in both directions); (d) **speed:** missing or unused indexes, policies that call a function once per row, the slowest queries the app actually runs, table and index sizes against the free plan's 500 MB; (e) **change history:** migrations that are not re-runnable, harnesses that replay old definitions, anything that would make rebuilding production from zero fail (the cutover item does exactly that); (f) **readiness for several shelters**, briefly, pointing at the spike rather than redoing it; (g) **what is good and should be left alone.** **The report:** `docs/database-review-<date>.md` in the repo (it must name **no real people or donors**, the repo is public; use counts and table names, never row data), and a PDF copy on Lutan's Desktop (`OneDrive\Desktop`). It opens with a **five-minute summary in plain English** for Lutan, then the findings **ranked** (data loss or security first, then wrong results, then speed, then tidiness), each with the tables or files, why it matters for the shelter, a suggested fix, whether it needs a migration, and a rough size, **written as a ready-to-paste backlog item**. Lutan picks which become items; the review raises none itself and changes nothing. **Done when** the report is on `main` (its own small PR, with a test plan that is `n/a` for UI and says which queries were run) and on the Desktop, and Lutan has been walked through the summary. **DONE 2026-10-13 (`claude/fable-db-review`): the report is `docs/database-review-2026-10-13.md`, with a PDF on the Desktop; sixteen ranked findings, each written as a ready-to-paste item in its §2, none raised here. STATUS: the walkthrough of the five-minute summary with Lutan is still outstanding, and which findings become work is his call after it.**

- [ ] **DECIDED 2026-10-10 — move only the public website to `lannacareforanimals.org`; the staff app stays on `lannacare.org` for now, and later moves to a Cooper `.org`. Build it so both moves are easy.** **Lutan's decision, 2026-10-10:** *"We will just move the public website to lannacareforanimals and keep the system on lannacare.org for now. Eventually we will migrate the system from lannacare to a cooper….org so please ensure we can move it easily and repoint the public website with minimal effort when the time comes to move it."* **So the discussion below is settled in favour of the split**, and what remains is a build with one hard requirement: **neither address may be written into the code.** **What "easy to move" means, concretely:** (a) **two settings, one per address** — the staff app's address and the public website's address — each set per environment in one place (the Worker's settings, `wrangler.jsonc`), and every link, redirect, sign-in return address, email link, QR/tag link, canonical URL and Open Graph tag built from them, never typed out; a grep for `lannacare.org` and `lannacareforanimals.org` in `src/` and `worker/` should find nothing but those settings and comments; (b) **the app decides what to serve from the address it was reached on** (public pages on the public address, staff pages on the app address, each sending the visitor to the other where needed), so adding the Cooper address later is a new hostname and a changed setting, not a code change; (c) **the old staff address keeps working after a move**, forwarding to the new one, so printed name cards and QR codes (which carry `lannacare.org`) never break; (d) **a written checklist** in `docs/` (or the README) of every place outside the code that holds an address — Supabase sign-in redirect URLs, Google sign-in client and consent screen, Cloudflare DNS, routes and WAF rule, the Pi tunnel hostnames, email sender, Search Console — so the Cooper move is a list to work through, not a hunt; this item's build writes it while doing the public-site move, because that move touches the same places. **Follow-on decided by this:** the cutover item (Deployment) assumed `lannacare.org` would become the UAT test site; it stays the live staff app instead, so **UAT needs a new address** (e.g. `uat.lannacare.org`). **Owed:** a `docs/decisions/` file recording this decision, written in the first PR that builds any of it. **ALSO DECIDED 2026-10-10 (Lutan): printing name cards and QR codes waits until both sites are on their final addresses** (the public site on `lannacareforanimals.org`, the staff app on its Cooper `.org`). So new cards are printed once, with the final address, and never reprinted for a move. Until then, cards and links already out there keep working because the old address forwards (point (c) above). **Same day, Lutan asked whether splitting makes the system harder to manage; answered:** not meaningfully, because it stays **one system** (one code base, one database, one deploy, one Pi), answering on two addresses. The ongoing extra is small: two address settings, the rule for which pages show on which address, and links between them (the public site's Staff login, a tag scanned by a member of the public going to the public page). Splitting it into two separately deployed apps would be the version that is harder to run, and is not proposed. Original text follows. **Discuss: keep the staff app on `lannacare.org` (later a Cooper `.org`) and move only the public website to `lannacareforanimals.org`.** Lutan, 2026-10-02. **The deliverable is a decision, not a build:** a `docs/decisions/` file agreed with Lutan, then a rewrite of the cutover item (Deployment) to match. **The idea:** instead of moving the whole of production to `lannacareforanimals.org`, the staff app (sign-in, residents, medical, Settings, everything behind a login) stays on `lannacare.org`, moving to a Cooper-named `.org` once the product has its name, and `lannacareforanimals.org` serves only the shelter's public pages (`/`, `/adopt`, `/our-work`, `/friends`, `/donate`, `/foster`, `/volunteer`, the public photo route). With several shelters that becomes one app domain for every shelter's staff, and one public domain per shelter. **What it buys:** (a) Google sign-in, the consent screen, Supabase redirect URLs, the 2-step setup and auth mail all live on one domain and never need re-reviewing per shelter, which is most of the cutover item's step 5; (b) a new shelter is a DNS record plus a public domain, not a new sign-in setup; (c) the QR and RFID tags already printed (`/r/`, `/e/` on `lannacare.org`) keep working; (d) the public site's cutover shrinks to DNS, a route and the public-page checks. **Things to settle, honestly:** (1) **It is still one app and one database.** "Front end and back end" here means one Next.js app answering on two hostnames and choosing what to serve by host (in `src/proxy.ts`): public routes on the public domain, app routes on the app domain, each redirecting to the other. Splitting into two deployments is possible later but not needed. (2) **The production database still has to be decided separately:** the cutover item's new Supabase project, and keeping today's one as UAT, are unaffected by which domain the app answers on. (3) **UAT needs a new home,** because the cutover item makes `lannacare.org` UAT: e.g. `uat.lannacare.org`, or `test.lannacare.org` doubling as it. (4) **Moving the app twice** (`lannacare.org` now, Cooper `.org` later) repeats the sign-in setup once; consider waiting and going straight to the Cooper domain at cutover if the name is close, and keep `lannacare.org` redirecting either way so tags never break. (5) **Printed tags for visitors:** a `/r/` tag scanned by a member of the public lands on the app domain today and shows the public profile there; it should redirect to that shelter's public domain instead, which needs a shelter → public-domain mapping (it is the same lookup the multi-shelter spike needs to pick a shelter from a hostname). (6) **Search engines and the lock:** the app domain is `noindex` everywhere; the public domain is indexable once the `PUBLIC_SITE` lock comes off for it; canonical URLs and Open Graph tags must use the public domain. (7) **Staff link from the public site** ("Staff login" in the footer) points at the app domain; a signed-in admin editing the website on the app domain previews it on the public domain. (8) **Photos:** public pages request images from their own domain (`/api/photos/` on the public host, edge and Pi cache as in the photo item), so the photo route must answer on both. (9) **Email:** sender domains (see "Send all auth mail from one sender domain") fit this naturally: auth mail from the app domain, any public mail from the shelter's. (10) **The Pi tunnel and Worker routes** gain a hostname each. **Read with:** the cutover item (Deployment), the multi-shelter spike and the per-shelter Drive item (Architecture), and the Chiang Mai regional-listing question, since a regional listing is one more public domain over several shelters. Lutan's view, to test in the paper: it should simplify going multi-tenant and make the move to `lannacareforanimals.org` easier because the public site needs little back-end setup. Both look right; the paper should confirm it against the cutover item's steps one by one. **Architecture review, 2026-10-11 (`docs/architecture-review-2026-09-22.md`):** when the staff app eventually moves host, `src/lib/auth/same-origin.ts` and `next.config.ts`'s `serverActions.allowedOrigins` must move with it (and `httpHostHeader` in `scripts/pi/cloudflared-config.yml`); the Deployment item *The public hostnames are hard-coded in two places the cutover list does not name* makes them one list so this cannot be missed. Review §2.1 S5.

- [x] **A release note shipped for a feature whose own decision file said a manual step was outstanding — decide whether §7 may be ticked in that case (process; found 2026-10-10).** **What happened.** #518 (`claude/pi-visitor-count`, `f08b62aa`) fixed a real drift bug — two hand-kept optional-secret lists, so `CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID` reached the Worker but not the Pi, which serves the pages — and added this note, tagged `roles: ["admin"]`: *"Settings → System status: the Website visitors tile now shows how many people visited the website, instead of saying Not set up."* **It did not.** The same PR's decision file (`docs/decisions/2026-10-10-one-optional-secrets-list.md`, "Not changed") closes by saying the Pi's copy of `.env.deploy.production` still needs the two lines by hand, and the backlog item still read *"the query has still never run against the live API"*. `0.25.0` was cut the same day, so **the note went out to admins in release mail for a feature that does not work.** Lutan reported it as an urgent bug; being fixed as `visitor-count-live`. **The bug itself is the BUG item in `## Admin`** (*the Website visitors tile still says Not set up…*, `4ed3d331`), being fixed as `visitor-count-live`; **this item is only the process question**, and it exists separately because that item carries its release-time lesson as prose and **that prose is lost the moment the bug is ticked.** **Why the gates did not catch it:** `check-test-plan.mjs` validates that §7 has a **new `unreleased` line**, not that the line is **true** — it cannot read a tile. So the checker is not at fault and **this is not a request to change it**; `continue-on-error` must not come back and the script must not start failing on unsigned plans (CLAUDE.md). **The decision to make:** may §7 be ticked when the same PR's decision file, README or backlog note records a manual step still outstanding? **Recommendation:** no — a note describes what a shelter user can now see, so if a step between the merge and the user seeing it is known to be outstanding, the honest answer is `n/a: <the step that is outstanding>` and the note goes in the PR that closes that step. A one-line rule in CLAUDE.md's testing section would carry it; whether it also becomes a check (grep the decision file for an outstanding-step phrase?) is a second question and probably not worth it. **The wider version, worth considering separately:** every one of the last three releases has had at least one note whose truth depended on a deploy step. → *Architecture*
- [ ] **Promote the `test-plan` check from a red flag to a required check.** Requested 2026-09-23 by Lutan, alongside enlisting a test manager: every feature gets a test plan checklist, filled in during verification and signed off before the feature reaches production. The mechanism is built — `docs/test-plan-template.md`, copied per feature to `docs/test-plans/<feature>.md`, plus `scripts/check-test-plan.mjs` and a `test-plan` CI job that fails a PR which does not add or update a *completed* checklist (every line ticked or `n/a: <reason>`, no placeholders left, `Result:` one of three values, `fail` blocks). That is PR #55 — open, CI green, carrying its own completed checklist as the first one through the gate. **The part deliberately not enabled yet:** `test-plan` is not a required check in branch protection on `main`, so it reports red and the PR merges anyway. That is a GitHub settings change on the repo (Settings → Branches → `main` → require `CI` *and* `test-plan`). **No exemptions, including schema-only PRs** — ruled 2026-09-23: an exemption was granted and then reversed within minutes, on the grounds that a checklist which is mostly `n/a: no UI surface, no code reads these columns yet` costs about a minute and is exactly the record you want when that migration later turns out to matter. If it is ever revisited, derive the exemption from the diff (the PR touches nothing outside `supabase/migrations/`) rather than from a label: a label is a manual click that can land on a PR which is not schema-only, so it has to be verified against the file list anyway, at which point the file list is doing the work and the label only adds a way to get it wrong. Note also that the gate sits before merge, not before deploy — `main` moves several times a day (four merges on 2026-09-23 alone), so untested work accumulating on `main` would make every release all-or-nothing. Keep a thin release-time smoke list as well (sign in, residents list, one resident hub, `/adopt` signed out), because a per-feature gate cannot catch two features interacting badly. Everything merged up to `f32f2c1` (#51–#54) is the agreed baseline and is exempt; testing starts from the next feature. **Staged deliberately, 2026-09-23:** Lutan's call is to run `test-plan` as a red flag first and promote it to a required check once the process has visibly bedded in — "see how we go, and if it is working smoothly then we can change to a hard block". So red-without-blocking is a planned first stage, not an oversight, and this item is the scheduled revisit rather than a defect. The reasoning (a soft gate people follow beats a hard gate they resent, and nothing is live until the Pi lands) is recorded in `docs/decisions.md` on PR #55.

- [x] **`check-test-plan.mjs` can't tell a post-merge sign-off PR from a feature PR that forgot its release line.** Raised 2026-09-24 on PR #80. #77 (intake capacity warning) merged with its plan complete apart from a real-phone check; the phone pass was then recorded in a follow-up PR from the same branch that touched only `docs/test-plans/intake-capacity-warning.md`. The checker reads the plan's **Release notes.** line against *that PR's* diff, and a ticked line with no new `unreleased` entry fails ("gained no line in this PR"), even though #77 had added it. The workaround was to reword the line as `n/a: in this follow-up PR … went into unreleased with #77` — honest, but it rewrites the feature's permanent record to suit a later PR, and every sign-off recorded after merge will hit the same thing. This will be common: section 8's deployed smoke test can only happen after merge, so a manual check moved there (as the phone pass was) is always recorded post-merge. Fix options: (a) when a PR changes only files under `docs/test-plans/`, check the release-notes line against the diff that introduced the plan (`git log --diff-filter=A` on the file, or the first PR that touched it) rather than the current diff; (b) accept a ticked line when `unreleased` — or a cut release — already contains a line the plan quotes; (c) an explicit marker such as `release line: #77` that the checker verifies by looking at that PR's diff. (a) needs no new syntax and is probably the right default. Afterwards, restore #80's line to its ticked wording. Soft gate, so nothing is blocked meanwhile — but a false red on every sign-off PR is exactly what teaches people to ignore a red `test-plan`.
