Lutan, 2026-10-10: take this off hold and into the build. **Order of work:** (1) a short scope, `docs/merch-shop.md`, with the Director's answers to the questions below and a recommendation on build vs. link; (2) Lutan picks the option; (3) build it in the same stream (schema PR first if the app holds products or orders). The scope is now step one of the build, not the end of the item. **DECIDED 2026-10-10 (Lutan): build it into the website, option (b) below — not a link out to LINE MyShop, Facebook or Shopify.** His reason: the website is meant to be a one-stop shop, and sending supporters off to another site loses them. So step (2) is settled. The scope still needs the Director's answers (what is sold, prices, who packs and posts, domestic or overseas, orders a month, who answers "where is my order"), and should now spend its effort on the build's own choices instead of build vs. link: **which payment company takes the money** (PromptPay QR and cards; choose it together with the per-donation QR item under Fundraising, so donations and the shop share one checkout and one record of the supporter), print-on-demand vs. holding stock, and the staff side (an orders list to pack, post and mark sent). **Consequence to accept:** the checkout runs on the shelter's own servers, so the Pi failover work (Next up) matters more: a Pi outage would be lost sales, not just a staff member waiting. Payment is taken on the payment company's own hosted page, so no card details ever touch the app or the Pi. Record the decision as its own `docs/decisions/` file in the build PR. **ANSWERS, Lutan 2026-10-10:** (1) **What is sold:** mainly clothes with Lanna Care logos, mugs and other small items. (2) **Who ships:** mostly **drop-shipped from suppliers** — the system **gathers the orders and sends each supplier one combined order** (a batch per supplier, not one email per customer order). The shelter **may also hold a small stock** and post some items itself. So one customer order can be split across several suppliers and the shelter's own shelf, and each part needs its own status (sent to supplier, shipped, tracking number). (3) **Where to:** **Thailand and international.** (4) **Volume:** about **50 orders a month** to start, growing. **What this means for the build:** a product catalogue with sizes and colours, each variant linked to the supplier that makes it (or to shelter stock, with a count); a checkout with shipping prices for Thailand and abroad; an order record split into supplier parts; a batching step that gathers unsent parts per supplier on a schedule or at the press of a button and sends the combined order (email, file or the supplier's own ordering system, whichever each supplier accepts); a staff screen for orders, batches, tracking and the items the shelter posts itself; and order and shipping emails to the customer. 50 a month is light work for the system. **Still open, for the scope:** prices and margins; **which suppliers** (Thai or international print-on-demand printers that put a logo on clothes and mugs and ship abroad — compare cost, quality, delivery times and how they accept orders); shipping prices per country, and whether overseas buyers pay in baht or their own currency; customs and import duty for overseas buyers (say so at checkout); returns and wrong sizes; who answers "where is my order"; and the tax question (trading income, not donations), for the accountant. The payment company (above) must take overseas cards as well as PromptPay. Original text follows. Customer request 2026-09-23. The ask is selling shelter merchandise online (t-shirts, calendars, tote bags and the like); this item ends with `docs/merch-shop.md` plus a `docs/decisions.md` entry and a recommendation the customer can say yes or no to — no schema and no routes until they have. **Questions to answer with them:** what is actually for sale and at what price; who packs and posts a parcel (shelter staff in Suphan Buri? Thailand Post / Kerry / J&T, who pays the postage, domestic only or overseas too?), or whether print-on-demand removes stock entirely; whether collection at the shelter is the common case; how many orders a month realistically — that number decides everything below; who answers "where is my order"; stock counts, sizes and variants, and what a sold-out item does; receipts, refunds, and whether the shelter's tax position cares that this is trading income rather than donations. **The real decision is build vs. link:** (a) point the public site at a hosted storefront — LINE MyShop or a Facebook/Instagram Shop, which is where their supporters already are, or Shopify — so the app adds a nav link and nothing else, and the shelter gets payments, stock and shipping labels for free; (b) build `/shop` into this app, reusing the Drive photo plumbing, the `site_pages` copy pattern, the translation queue and the Worker, with `products` / `orders` tables and a hosted checkout; (c) a middle path — a catalogue in the app that hands off to (a) for payment. Weigh it honestly: (b) is only worth the work if an order needs to tie back to something the system already knows (a resident, an appeal, a supporter record shared with donations), and it puts payments, stock and customer support on infrastructure that is about to move onto a Raspberry Pi in Suphan Buri (`docs/pi-hosting.md`), where an hour of downtime is a lost sale rather than a staff member waiting. Read it next to the Fundraising section (*Make `/donate` ask for money*): if both happen, a buyer and a donor are usually the same person and should not end up as two unrelated tables.

- [ ] **Investigate options for a drop-shipment B2B offering on the system — the deliverable is an options paper, not a build.** Requested 2026-09-24 by Lutan. The idea: sell goods through the system without the shelter holding stock or posting parcels, a supplier shipping direct to the buyer, with businesses as the buyers or the partners. **Blocked: do not start until the Director has answered the prerequisites below** (Lutan is taking them to the Director); record the answers here, dated, before the work begins. **Prerequisites (answers from the Director):** (1) **What "B2B" means here**, because the options differ completely. Is it (i) the shelter *sourcing* from a B2B drop-ship supplier (print-on-demand merch, or pet food and supplies from a Thai wholesaler) and selling on to supporters; (ii) the shelter *selling to businesses* (vets, pet shops, cafés, the companies on the "Shelter Friends" list) buying branded or bulk goods shipped direct by the supplier; (iii) businesses selling *through* the shelter's site with a cut going to the shelter (affiliate or marketplace); or (iv) something else, e.g. offering this system itself to other shelters? (2) **What would be sold**, roughly at what price, and to whom: supporters in Thailand only, or overseas too? (3) **Suppliers already in mind**: any wholesaler, printer or partner business the Director has spoken to, and any known margins or minimum orders. (4) **Who handles the customer side**: payment, VAT invoices / tax receipts for business buyers, returns and "where is my order". Shelter staff, the supplier, or nobody yet? (5) **Tax and legal position**: whether trading income (rather than donations) changes the shelter's status, and who can confirm that (their accountant?). (6) **Expected volume**: realistic orders a month, which decides whether anything is worth building. (7) **How it relates to the merch shop and donations**: one effort or separate ones? **Once answered, the work:** research which suppliers actually drop-ship inside Thailand (and overseas, if it matters), their integration (API, CSV feed, email order, or a manual order form), margins and minimums; work out what the system would have to hold for the chosen model (products, business accounts, orders, supplier routing); and **weigh build vs. link honestly**, as the merch item does: a hosted storefront or the supplier's own white-label shop may give most of the value for none of the payments, support and Pi-uptime risk (`docs/pi-hosting.md`). The deliverable is `docs/drop-shipping-b2b.md` plus a `docs/decisions.md` entry and a recommendation Lutan and the customer can say yes or no to. No schema and no routes until they have. Read it next to **Scope an online merchandise shop** and **Make `/donate` ask for money** above, and **"Shelter Friends"** on the public site: if more than one happens they should share one catalogue, one checkout and one record of who the buyer, donor or business is. Folding this into the merch scope as one of its options is a fine outcome. **PARTLY ANSWERED 2026-10-10 (Lutan, through the shop):** option (i), the shelter sourcing from drop-ship suppliers and selling on to supporters, is now part of the **Online merchandise shop** (Fundraising, waiting on the Director), which gathers orders and sends each supplier a combined order. What is still open here is only (ii) selling to businesses and (iii) businesses selling through the site; do not research drop-ship suppliers separately for this item.

- [ ] **Affiliate links: earn the shelter a small cut when supporters buy through its links — either on Shelter Friends or as their own list. Decide the shape first, then build.** Lutan, 2026-10-08. An affiliate link is a tracked link to a shop (Shopee, Lazada, Amazon, a local pet-food or vet-supply store) that pays the shelter a commission on whatever the visitor buys, at no extra cost to them. **Two places it could live, the first decision:** (a) **on Shelter Friends** — a Friend that runs an affiliate or referral scheme gets an optional affiliate link (and a line such as "buy through this link and the shelter gets 5%") on its card on `/friends` and the contact hub's Preview; small, because the public profile, translation of prose, the per-field opt-ins and the `public_shelter_friends` view already exist (0076, 0099, `docs/decisions/2026-09-24-shelter-friends-the-feature-half.md`); but a Friend is a business that *helps* the shelter, and a big marketplace is not one, so (b) **a separate list** — e.g. "Shop for the shelter" on `/donate` or under Get involved: a curated set of products or shops (the food the residents actually eat, a wish-list of supplies) each with an affiliate link, a photo, a price hint and a short translated note. Possibly both: Friends carry their own link, marketplaces go on the list. **Questions for Lutan / the Director before any schema:** which schemes the shelter is (or could be) signed up to (Shopee and Lazada affiliate programmes, Amazon Associates for overseas supporters, a local shop's own referral code); whether any Friend already offers one; whether a wish-list ("buy this and have it delivered to the shelter") is the real wish, which is a different and possibly better thing than commission; who checks that links still work and products still exist; and whether commission income has any tax or status implication (same question the merch and drop-ship items ask). **Build notes once decided:** links must stay `https://` only through `src/lib/links/validate.ts` and a database check, as Friends' links do; mark them `rel="sponsored noopener"` and say plainly on the page that the shelter earns from them (Thai and overseas disclosure rules, and supporters' trust); record clicks only if a scheme does not already report them, and never put visitor data in the link; schema first, its own PR, per the migration rules. Read next to the merch shop and drop-shipment items above — option (iii) of the drop-ship prerequisites ("businesses selling *through* the shelter's site with a cut") is this idea, so if the Director's answer there settles it, note it in both. ### Security

- [x] **Pin `search_path` on every `security definer` function (architecture review S7, 2026-10-11; verify first).** Across the migrations there are 171 `security definer` declarations and 164 `set search_path` lines, and a rough scan finds about forty definer declarations with no `search_path` within four lines (some will be false positives, and later files replace earlier bodies). Supabase's linter flags this because a definer function resolves unqualified names on the caller's path; on this project `authenticated` cannot create objects in `public`, so the risk is low, but it is the standard hardening and the newer migrations already do it. Do: on dev, `select n.nspname, p.proname from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid = p.pronamespace where p.prosecdef and (p.proconfig is null or not p.proconfig::text like '%search_path%') and n.nspname in ('public','private')` for the real list, then one migration of `alter function … set search_path = ''` (or `public`, matching each body) per function, and a line in `check-migration-grants.mjs` or a sibling that refuses a new definer function without one. Small. `docs/architecture-review-2026-09-22.md` §2.1 S7. **ALREADY TRUE — measured on dev 2026-10-12, nothing to build.** The item asked to verify first, and verifying closed it. A read-only `pg_proc` query against dev (`qxkmhwybjggxvsfxsxbd`) returns **57 `security definer` functions, 57 of them pinned, 0 unpinned** — 40 with `search_path=public` and 17 with `search_path=""`, so the per-function choice between the two was already made. **The gate the item asked for already exists:** `scripts/check-migration-grants.mjs:261` refuses a new `security definer` function that does not pin `set search_path`, and it runs inside `npm run lint`, so it has been on every PR all along. **Where "about forty" came from:** the review grepped the migration *files* — 173 `security definer` declarations against 165 `set search_path` lines across 110 files — but files are not the live state, because `create or replace` means a later file supersedes an earlier body; 173 declarations resolve to 57 live functions. The item predicted exactly this ("later files replace earlier bodies"). **Not verified on production**, which these sessions cannot read: if production is behind on migrations it could still hold an older unpinned body, so that stays a release-manager check before a deploy, not a workstream. `docs/decisions/2026-10-12-search-path-already-pinned.md`.

- [x] **A high-severity advisory has been red in CI all day and nothing said so.** Found 2026-10-06 while cutting `0.19.3`: `npm run audit:prod` reports `source-map-js 1.0.0 - 1.2.1`, **high**, [GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q) — event-loop denial of service through indexed source-map section offsets. It arrives as `next@16.3.5 → postcss@8.5.23 → source-map-js@1.2.1`, so it is in the production tree (`--omit=dev`). **Two separate things to decide.** (a) *The advisory:* `npm audit fix` claims a fix, but `npm ls` also reports `next@16.3.5 invalid: "16.3.8" from the root project`, so the installed Next does not match what `package.json` asks for and the fix may not be a one-liner; the practical risk here looks low, since the DoS needs the app to parse untrusted source maps at runtime, which is not an obvious path. (b) *The reporting*, which is the bigger problem: the `audit` job is `continue-on-error: true`, so the run concludes `success` while the job shows `fail`. It had been red on **every PR run of 2026-10-06**, back to at least 11:48 — more than ten PRs, all merged — and nothing surfaced it. This is exactly what `CLAUDE.md` records about `test-plan`: suppressing a job to stop it being noisy also stops anyone seeing it. The fix shape that worked there was to put the distinction inside the script — exit 0 for the states that are expected, non-zero only for the ones that are someone's mistake — rather than `continue-on-error` on the job. Consider the same for `audit:prod`: a known, accepted advisory passes with a printed note; a new one fails. **CORRECTED 2026-10-06 (`/plan-day`, verified): the reporting was NOT suppressed, and (b) should not be actioned as written.** The two audit paths **deliberately disagree** and there is a decision file saying so (`docs/decisions/2026-10-02-scheduled-audit-fails-on-purpose.md`); `ci.yml` says in terms **"Do not 'tidy' the two to match"**. On a PR the job is `continue-on-error` because red there *"would stand on a change that did not cause it"*; the backstop is **`advisories.yml`, a daily scheduled run that is allowed to FAIL on purpose** so GitHub emails a human where there is no PR to turn red. **It fired:** run `37470137258`, scheduled **2026-10-06T13:21Z, conclusion `failure`** — the first failure after four consecutive successes (2026-10-02 to 10-05). So the machinery did what it was designed to do. The real gap is only that the email reaches *whoever last edited the cron line* and nobody acted for some hours, which is a notification-routing question, not a CI design fault. **Also: `npm audit` was clean of highs on this tree earlier the same day**, so GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q looks newly published rather than long-missed; a green audit going red is the normal way a new advisory arrives. **And the `next@16.3.5 invalid` line is local staleness, not a repo problem:** `package-lock.json` holds **`next 16.3.8`** and `package.json` pins 16.3.8; only the main checkout's `node_modules` was still on 16.3.5 (no `npm ci` since the bump). `npm audit --omit=dev` reports **no critical**, so the Next RCE remains fixed. **So what is left is (a) alone:** one **high** in the production tree — `next → postcss@8.5.23 → source-map-js@1.2.1` — with `npm audit fix` offering a fix, and the practical risk low because the DoS needs the app to parse untrusted source maps at runtime. **Treat it as an ordinary dependency bump and leave both workflows alone.** Filed under `## Completed` by mistake and moved to Security on 2026-10-06. **DONE 2026-10-06 (`advisory-bump`): part (a) only.** `source-map-js` 1.2.1 → 1.2.2 in `package-lock.json` alone (`npm update source-map-js`); `postcss` already allows it, so no `package.json` change, no `overrides`, no Next bump. `npm run audit:prod` went from 1 high to 0 vulnerabilities. **Part (b) was deliberately NOT done and must not be re-opened:** the PR `audit` job is `continue-on-error` and `advisories.yml` is allowed to fail on purpose, and the backstop worked (see the correction above and `docs/decisions/2026-10-02-scheduled-audit-fails-on-purpose.md`). No workflow was changed. The notification-routing question (the email goes to whoever last edited the cron line) is not built here.

- [x] **Builds no longer type-check the dev server's `.next/dev/types`.** Done 2026-09-22: `tsconfig.build.json` (`tsconfig.json` minus `.next/dev`) is what `next build` type-checks with (`typescript.tsconfigPath` in `next.config.ts`, keyed on NODE_ENV so `next dev` and the editor keep `tsconfig.json`) and what `npm run typecheck` runs `tsc` against. Reproduced with truncated `routes.d.ts` / `validator.ts` under a running dev server: `next build` failed before, and `npm run opennext:build` (the deploy script's build step) completed after with the same files in place. Root cause is Next 16's `experimental.useTypeScriptCli` default, which hands the tsconfig straight to `tsc --project`; Next's own checker filters `.next/dev/types` out and the CLI path doesn't. Original brief: **A production build can fail type-checking on half-written `.next/dev/types/*.ts`.** Seen 2026-09-22: `tsconfig.json` includes `.next/dev/types/**/*.ts`, which a running `next dev` rewrites; when `next build` type-checks while that is mid-write (or after an interrupted build wiped `.next`), it fails with a wall of `TS1005 ';' expected` in `routes.d.ts` / `validator.ts` and the deploy stops. Workaround: delete `.next/dev/types/*` and rerun. Fix: have `scripts/deploy.mjs` build in a scratch copy of `.next` (or stop the dev server first / exclude `.next/dev/types` from the build-time `tsc`), so a deploy never depends on what the dev server is doing.

- [x] **Fix mobile row click on residents list.** In `src/app/residents/ResidentsTable.tsx` the name link's `after:absolute after:inset-0` overlay relies on `relative` on the `<tr>`, which mobile WebKit ignores, so tapping anywhere opens the last row. Anchor it to the cell or make the row properly clickable.

- [x] **Strategy for free-text fields across languages.** Decided and built 2026-09-21 (see `docs/decisions.md`): public-facing prose (resident bio / temperament / past story, project story, photo captions) gets one row in a `translations` side table (`0056_translations.sql`) — the text in the other language, a status, and a snapshot of the source it was written against, so an edit to the original re-queues it as *Out of date* rather than leaving the Thai silently wrong. Source language is detected from the script of the text. Managers write and approve at `/management/translations` (stale first, editor open on every row) or in the same `TranslationPanel` under the field on the resident hub / project folder; approved text is what a visitor reading that language sees, else the original. `summary_th` / `caption_th` moved into the table and were dropped; `thai_name` / `name_th` stay as labels. Maintenance job title and description joined the same day (`0057_translations_maintenance.sql`: tiers renamed to `reviewed` / `machine`, board and job page show the reader's language) — the user's first question was whether tasks were covered. Internal notes are untouched until the machine phase (Management item above); zone and enclosure names are the Facility item below. Original brief: The UI is fully bilingual, but staff-typed text (weight and vet-visit notes, bio and behaviour notes, cause of death, prescription notes, intake notes) shows in whatever language it was typed — a Thai user sees English notes and vice versa (noticed 2026-09-20 on the Weight tab). Options to weigh: leave as-is with a house rule on which language notes are written in; paired `_th` columns where a field is public-facing (the bio already has precedent in `thai_name`); or on-demand machine translation shown as a hint under the original, never replacing it. Decide before the public site or foster portal shows free text to a different audience than the one that wrote it.
- [x] **Contact hub tidy-up (four customer requests, 2026-09-22).** Done 2026-09-22 — Donor/Other removed from the enum outright (migration 0067, see `docs/decisions.md`); the address line and a map preview replace the duplicated detail rows; shared `maps.app.goo.gl` links are resolved server-side. Original item: All in `src/app/contacts/[id]/ContactHub.tsx` unless noted; one branch, one PR. (a) **Drop the Donor and Other contact types.** `CONTACT_TYPES` in `src/lib/contacts/contacts.ts` and the `contact_type` enum (`0001`) both carry `Donor` and `Other`; remove them from the constant, the Management → Contacts form and the `t.contacts.types` labels (`en.ts` ~2550 and `th.ts`). Check the dev and production `contacts` tables for rows of those types first (`select type, count(*) from contacts group by 1`) and decide with the user what they become (Volunteer? Vendor?) before writing the migration — Postgres can't drop an enum value, so either leave the values in the enum and stop offering them (simplest) or recreate the type; say which in `docs/decisions.md`. `scripts/import-appsheet.mjs` maps AppSheet's Donor too. (b) **Phone and WhatsApp appear twice on the card**: `ContactActions size="lg"` already renders each channel as an orange tile with its value, and the `<dl>` beneath repeats the same values as text. Remove the duplicated text rows — keep the `<dl>` only for details that have no action tile (today that's none, since every detail has a matching action), or fold the value into the tile and drop the list; whichever, the address must stay readable in full (long Thai addresses are truncated in a tile). (c) **Map preview for the address.** `mapHref()` treats an `http(s)` address as a pasted maps link and everything else as a search query. When the address is a link (or, cheaper, always), show a small embedded map under the address: a keyless `<iframe src="https://www.google.com/maps?q=<query>&output=embed">` works without an API key for a search query; a shared `maps.app.goo.gl` short link can't be embedded directly (it redirects, and iframes don't follow it into a usable embed) — either resolve it server-side once and store the coordinates, or fall back to the search embed on the text after the link. (d) **Alignment between Residents in care and Past placements.** The two sections sit in a `lg:grid-cols-2`; the left one has the `residentsInCareDetail` helper paragraph under its heading and the right one doesn't, so the two lists start at different heights. Either give both sections a helper line (e.g. "Residents who used to live with this carer.") or move the helper below the list next to `assignFromResident`, so the headings and the first card line up.

Scrolling ~200px clears them; one group expanded never overlaps. The proper fix is to bound the sidebar to the window and give it its own scrollbar (`md:sticky md:top-14 md:h-[calc(100dvh-3.5rem)] md:overflow-y-auto`), which needs `AppHeader` pinned at a fixed height and made sticky — a visible change on every page, so decide with the user first. ### Resident operations

- [x] **Summary PDF: a stray hyphen where a long name wraps before a Thai word.** Done 2026-09-24: textkit hands the hyphenation callback one *run* at a time and starts a new run where the script changes, so `Valley (เจ้าหญิง…)` arrived as `(` and `เจ้าหญิง…)`; with no space between them the line breaker counted the join as a hyphenation point and printed `(-` when it broke there. Every `Text` in `src/lib/archive/resident-summary-pdf.tsx` now carries `hyphenationPenalty` of textkit's infinity (10000), which makes such points unbreakable, so lines break only at spaces. Verified by rendering long Thai and long Latin names before and after (`docs/test-plans/summary-pdf-hyphen.md`).
- [x] **Intake warns when the chosen enclosure is nearly full or full.** Done 2026-09-24: the wizard's Arrival step uses `EnclosurePicker` (idPrefix `intake`, with placeholders that keep "blank means Unassigned"), fed by `loadEnclosureOptions()` — the same loader as Move — so the headcount and thresholds cannot disagree between screens. Register opens `CapacityWarningDialog` (intake wording via a new `copy` prop) and, as everywhere else, only warns: Register anyway still registers. The warning is on Register rather than on Arrival's Next (see `docs/decisions.md`). Correction to the brief: `record_intake` never rejected a full enclosure, so before this a volunteer got no warning at all rather than a late error. Original brief: Noticed 2026-09-22 while turning `/residents/new` into a wizard. Every other placement screen — move, return from hospital, return to shelter, the edit form's housing section, maintenance — uses `EnclosurePicker` (`src/components/EnclosurePicker.tsx`), which shows the chosen enclosure's occupancy underneath and, with `CapacityWarningDialog`, asks before putting one more resident into a full or nearly-full one. Intake is the exception: it has its own plain Zone and Enclosure selects, so a volunteer registering an arrival at the gate — the person least likely to know which kennels are full — gets no warning, and the first they hear of it is an error from `record_intake`. Swap the two selects on the wizard's Arrival step for `EnclosurePicker`. It needs `residentCount` and `capacity` per enclosure (`src/lib/enclosures/options.ts`), which `/residents/new`'s page query doesn't select yet — copy the query the move page uses. Note the picker names its own controls (`idPrefix`), so the wizard's Review step, which reads answers back out of the form by control id, needs its zone/enclosure lookups updated to match.
- [x] **Deceased Resident Summary PDF: the name overlaps the subtitle, and the footer never renders.** Done 2026-09-24: one cause for both — the page style's unitless `lineHeight: 1.4`, which @react-pdf resolves to an absolute 12.6pt and hands down to every child (see `docs/decisions.md`). The 20pt name got a 12.6pt line box; the footer's page-number text, re-laid-out after its render prop runs, read the inherited 12.6 as a multiplier on each pass and came out ~5,300pt tall, so the bottom-anchored footer sat thousands of points above the page. Line height is now set per text style in `src/lib/archive/resident-summary-pdf.tsx`. Checked by rendering the real component against stub records (Latin, Thai, Thai-only, a name that wraps, a four-page DEV render) and reading every page. The six archives already in production keep the broken layout until each is regenerated — a separate backlog item. Original brief: Noticed 2026-09-23 while rendering the PDF for the UAT watermark. The 20pt name and the `R-0042 · Dog · …` subtitle print on top of each other, and the fixed footer (name, code, generated date, page N / M) is missing from every page. Production output shows both, so they predate the watermark. A render of the component against a stub record is enough to check a fix; no Drive or database needed.
- [x] **Hide deceased residents from the residents list by default, with a "Show all" toggle.** Done 2026-09-23: `/residents` filters `resident_list_view` with the shared `NOT_DECEASED` expression (`src/lib/residents/status.ts`, now also used by the vet-visit and immunization pickers), and `?all=1` — the Show all / Hide deceased chip beside the filters, on phones too — brings them back, dimmed, with Deceased in the Status column. The line under the heading counts the mode: "212 residents · 38 deceased hidden", or "including 38 deceased" with the toggle on. A name search that matches a deceased animal says so rather than switching the list out from under you — "1 deceased resident matches — show" (see `docs/decisions.md`). The deceased count respects the name / zone / enclosure filters, so it always counts the animals that list would have shown. `/enclosures/[id]` is unchanged by design.
- [x] **Step-by-step intake instead of one long form.** Done 2026-09-22: `/residents/new` now asks the same questions over five steps (Who, Arrival, Health, For adopters, Story) and a Review that lists every answer with an Edit link back to its step. The write is untouched — one `recordIntake` call to the `record_intake` RPC on the single Register press (see `docs/decisions.md`). Steps are hidden rather than unmounted so values and `required` survive; every forward move runs `checkValidity()` over the steps it passes so the browser's own message lands on the field at fault, and Register validates before `requestSubmit()`. `?step=` keeps the place across a refresh, never the answers. The adoption recommendation fields got a step of their own (the brief named four field groups but five steps); `EditResidentForm` stays flat. Manual's intake topic rewritten. *Still to do:* re-capture `public/manual/resident-intake.png` — it needs a signed-in browser against a dev database, so it is a run of `node scripts/manual-screenshots.mjs` rather than a code change. Original brief: Customer request 2026-09-22: `/residents/new` is intimidating — `src/app/residents/new/IntakeForm.tsx` shows all four fieldsets (identity with name / species / sex / size / age / weight / blood-test interval / diet; adoption profile; arrival with date / origin / zone + enclosure / notes / ready-for-adoption; bio with temperament / past story / behaviour) on one page, ~25 fields before the Register button. Turn it into a wizard: one section per step, a progress header ("Step 2 of 4 · Arrival", steps clickable once visited), Back / Next, and a final **Review** step that lists every answer with an Edit link back to its step before the single Register press. **Keep the write exactly as it is:** one `recordIntake` call to the `record_intake` RPC at the end (`actions.ts`), so nothing half-registered is ever created — the steps are a client-side view over one `<form>`, not separate submissions. Implementation shape: keep everything in the one `<form action={formAction}>` and hide the inactive steps with `hidden` (not unmounted, so their values and the `required` attributes survive), and run `checkValidity()` on the visible step's fields on Next so a step can't be left with its required fields empty — the browser's own validation messages then point at the right control. Order the steps so the required things come first and the optional prose last: 1 *Who* (name, Thai name, other names, species, breed, sex, size), 2 *Arrival* (date, origin incl. the add-origin toggle, zone → enclosure with the existing capacity note, ready for adoption), 3 *Health* (age, weight, blood-test interval, diet), 4 *Story* (bio, temperament, past story, behaviour — all optional, say so, and note they can be filled later from Edit resident), 5 *Review*. Keep the URL at `/residents/new` (a `?step=` param is fine so a refresh doesn't lose the place; the values themselves live in the form, not the URL). Phone first — this is the form a volunteer fills at the gate — so one column, big Next button pinned at the bottom, and check it in the phone drawer's width. The `IntakeState` error from the server (name taken, enclosure full, RPC failure) should land the user on the Review step with the message, not on step 1. Reuse `AdoptionProfileFields` unchanged. Leave `EditResidentForm` as the flat form it is — editing one field on a wizard is worse, and the two forms already share the field components. Update the manual's intake topic (`src/lib/manual/en.ts` `id: "intake"`, and `th.ts`) and re-capture `resident-intake.png` (or whatever the screenshot script names it) since the page looks different. Record in `docs/decisions.md` that the wizard is presentation only and the RPC is unchanged.
- [x] **Decide which fields stay editable after death.** Decided 2026-09-21: the bio group (bio, temperament, past story, behaviour notes) and photos (add, remove, choose the profile photo) — nothing else. `0052_deceased_editable_fields.sql` relaxes `enforce_deceased_lock()` for a `residents` UPDATE that changes only those columns and `enforce_deceased_lock_attachment()` for `'resident'` attachments; blood test and procedure files stay locked. The edit page shows only the photo and bio sections for a deceased resident, the Photos tab keeps its uploader, and `refreshDeceasedArchiveIfNeeded()` regenerates the summary PDF and offline index after each such change (best effort — the hub's Retry still covers a Drive failure). Original brief: The deceased lock in `0026_deceased_workflow.sql` currently allows nothing, pending that decision. Once the list exists, relax `enforce_deceased_lock()` for those columns (and re-generate the archive when one of them changes).
- [x] **Edit resident details.** Add `/residents/[id]/edit` with a form + server action to update identity/bio fields (name, Thai name, other names, animal code, species, breed, sex, age, notes, adoption/public flags). Housing is not edited here.
- [x] **Move resident between enclosures.** `/residents/[id]/move` (linked from the hub's Housing card and the housing section) and a Housing section on the edit form both insert a `ChangeEnclosure` row into `placement_history` via `src/lib/placements/move.ts` (zone → enclosure picker, date, notes; Lifecycle pseudo-enclosures excluded; capacity warning before moving into a nearly-full/full/over-capacity enclosure). Existing trigger closes the prior placement (0024 makes it `BEFORE INSERT` — it never could have fired past the one-active-placement index as `AFTER` — and `security definer` so volunteers' moves work).
- [x] **Send to hospital.** `/residents/[id]/hospital` (from the hub's Housing card, the housing section, and each vet visit record via `?vetAppointmentId=` which pre-fills date and notes) inserts a `SendToHospital` placement into the Lifecycle/Hospital enclosure via `src/lib/placements/hospital.ts`, storing `previous_enclosure_id` so the resident can return later. Admin/staff only. The Housing card reads "In hospital · Off-site in medical care · Returns to X" while they're there.
- [x] **Return from hospital.** `/residents/[id]/hospital/return` (from the hub's Housing card and the housing section while hospitalised — it and "Send to hospital" are opposites, only one is ever shown) inserts a `ReturnFromHospital` placement via `returnResidentFromHospital()` in `src/lib/placements/hospital.ts`. The zone → enclosure picker defaults to the stored `previous_enclosure_id` but any physical enclosure can be chosen (e.g. isolation first), with a notice when the previous one is gone or wasn't physical. Admin/staff only. "Move enclosure" is hidden (and rejected server-side) while in hospital.
- [x] **Foster and adopt.** `/residents/[id]/rehome` (from the hub's Housing card and the housing section; `?type=foster|adopt` picks the tab) inserts a `Foster` or `Adopt` placement into the Lifecycle/Fostered or /Adopted enclosure with `carer_id` via `rehomeResident()` in `src/lib/placements/rehome.ts`. The carer is picked from contacts of type Carer, or added inline (name, phone, email, LINE ID — saved as a Carer contact) until Contacts management exists. A fostered resident can be adopted, moved to another carer, or sent to hospital; an adopted one can only be returned. `/residents/[id]/rehome/return` inserts a `ReturnToShelter` placement into a physical enclosure (`returnResidentToShelter()`), defaulting to the enclosure they left from. Admin/staff only. Which actions show for each status lives in `src/lib/placements/available.ts`.
- [x] **Hide adopted residents from the public adoption pages.** `0025_public_views_exclude_adopted.sql` filters `public_resident_profiles` and `public_resident_photos` on `current_status not in ('Deceased', 'Adopted')`; fostered residents stay listed (foster-to-adopt is common). Same migration revokes everything but SELECT on both views from `anon` / `authenticated` — Supabase's default privileges had granted INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, and `public_resident_profiles` is auto-updatable, so anonymous writes through it were being accepted.
- [x] **Undo a death recorded by mistake.** Done 2026-09-21 (see `docs/decisions.md`): the deceased banner offers an admin **Withdraw this death** → `/residents/[id]/deceased/undo` (reason required, confirmation dialog). `undo_deceased_placement()` (0049) appends a `DeceasedInError` placement (0048) back into whatever the death closed — the resident's history keeps both the death and the reversal, dated when it was made — and restores exactly what the cascade did from the snapshot the Deceased row now records in `placement_history.deceased_cascade`: the appointments it cancelled, the prescriptions it ended (with the end dates they had) and `ready_for_adoption`. The lock lifts on its own. The Drive folder moves back under `Residents/` and the generated summary PDF and index page are deleted (`src/lib/archive/restore-deceased-resident.ts`), with a retry on the hub if Drive failed. The dashboard no longer counts a withdrawn death. Original brief: Today a `Deceased` placement can only be reversed in SQL: the record is locked database-side and the cascade (cancelled appointments, ended prescriptions) isn't reversible row by row. Decide whether admins get a proper "recorded in error" path, and what it should restore.
- [x] **Record deceased.** `/residents/[id]/deceased` (from the icon beside the edit pencil on the hub's details card, admin/staff only) records the death (date, cause, notes) behind a confirmation dialog via `src/lib/placements/deceased.ts`. The resident becomes Deceased, drops off the public pages, and their whole record turns read-only — enforced by triggers in `0026_deceased_workflow.sql`, not just hidden buttons. The same migration fixes `current_status` never having returned `'Deceased'` (it tested the zone name, so `0025`'s public-view filter wasn't actually hiding deceased residents) and makes the 7.2 cascade `security definer` so staff's appointment/prescription cleanup isn't silently filtered out by RLS. Afterwards the Drive folder moves to `Residents/Deceased/`, and a summary PDF plus an offline `index.html` index are written into it (`src/lib/archive/`); the hub shows the archive state with a retry when Drive was down.

### Medical records

- [x] **Optional doctor name on a vet appointment.** Done 2026-09-24 in two PRs. #76 added `vet_appointments.doctor_name` (0074: free text; a trigger trims it and stores blank as NULL, and a check constraint states the same). The feature PR adds an optional **Doctor** field to `/vet-visits/new` and `/vet-visits/[id]/edit`. As decided 2026-09-23 it is free text with a `<datalist>` of the names already recorded against the chosen vet, loaded once with the page and following the vet select. The name shows after the vet on the resident's Vet Appointments tab and in the deceased archive (summary PDF and offline index), and after the reason on the vet hub's visit list. A visit with no doctor renders exactly as before. `schedule_bulk_appointments` did not gain the `p_doctor_name` parameter this item planned; the booking action sets the name on the rows the RPC returns instead (see `docs/decisions.md`). The assistant's vet booking neither asks for nor accepts a doctor yet. ### Admin

- [x] **`worktree.mjs list` should say WHY a folder is HELD, so `/clean-streams` can clear the common case.** [done 2026-10-07, see `docs/decisions/2026-10-07-worktree-held-reason.md`: the column reads `HELD by a dev server on port N` when a next dev server is the only holder, a named session still wins, and `done` stays opt-in via `--stop-servers`.] Lutan, 2026-10-06, after asking what could possibly have `volunteer-read-only` open when nothing — not even he — goes into those folders. **The answer was a `next dev` server nobody stopped**, pid 15544, running since **2026-10-04 13:19**, serving a worktree whose PR had merged long before. It held `.next/` inside the folder, so `list` could not rename it and reported `HELD`, and **three cleanup rounds in a row could not touch it**. It was not alone: **all nine HELD folders had exactly one such server each** (ports 3004, 3006, 3011, 3015, 3017, 3018, 3019, 3020, 3023), **3.2 GB of working set between them**, out of 46 `node.exe` on the machine. **Why it accumulates:** in ordinary work you run one dev server from a terminal and closing the terminal ends it. Here a server is started **per worktree** by a session, it **detaches and outlives that session**, and the folder it serves is **meant to be deleted** afterwards. None of those is true of normal work, so it is a cost of the worktree-per-stream design rather than anything anyone is doing wrong. **The capability already exists and is well built:** `done <slug> --stop-servers` ends them and retries, and its `holders()` matches only a process *running from* the folder (an executable inside it, or `node.exe` running a script under its `node_modules`), **deliberately not one that merely mentions the path**, because *"a shell whose command line merely names the folder is somebody's session … and --stop-servers must never end one"*. It also found a **child process** a hand-written `Stop-Process` had missed. **So this item is not about building the ability — it is about surfacing the reason.** **Build:** `list`'s `held` column should read **`HELD by a dev server on port 3006`** (or the process name it found) instead of a bare `HELD` — **`holders()` already computes exactly this and throws it away**. Then `/clean-streams`, which is currently told *"do not propose `--stop-servers` unless the user says so for that slug"*, can safely offer it for folders held **only** by a dev server, while keeping that caution for anything else. **Worth considering alongside:** whether `done` should stop a dev server on the worktree's own `.port` without the flag at all, since by then the branch is merged and the folder is being deleted. **Why it matters beyond tidiness:** a bare `HELD` was read for three weeks as "someone is still working in there", including by `/plan-day`, which repeatedly told Lutan not to tear those folders down on that basis. A reason in the column answers the question without anyone investigating. No schema. → *Admin*
- [x] **Release notes register, with an email to admins on each major release.** Done 2026-09-23 (see `docs/decisions.md`, "Release notes register"): `src/lib/releases.ts` seeded with `0.0.1` "Current Baseline Build", `/releases` for every signed-in role (nav footer, manual topic), `package.json` at `0.0.1`; `scripts/deploy.mjs` refuses a production deploy with unreleased notes or a version mismatch, tags the Worker version, and mails a major release new to the site to that environment’s admins through the Worker’s free Cloudflare `send_email` binding (`worker/release-mail.mjs`, verified addresses only, `[UAT]`/`[Production]` in the subject, dev never sends). One-off Cloudflare setup in `docs/email-sending.md` §1; Resend SMTP for password reset stays under the Deployment item (§2). Original brief: Requested 2026-09-23 by Lutan. A page in the app (admin-visible; readable by everyone is worth asking) listing each release — version, date, **environment (UAT or Production)**, and short plain-language notes of what changed for users. Today nothing records a release: `package.json` is still `0.1.0` and deploys go through `scripts/deploy.mjs --env`, so the design needs to settle (a) **where notes live** — a checked-in file (e.g. `docs/releases.md` or a typed `src/lib/releases.ts`, written as part of the PR) is simplest and reviewable; a DB table (needs a schema PR first) allows editing in the app; (b) **how a release is recorded** — most naturally by `scripts/deploy.mjs`, which already knows the target env, stamping the version + env + date at deploy time; (c) **major vs minor** — a flag per release; only major releases send email. **Email:** on a major release, send the notes to every user with the `admin` role in that environment's database, with the environment named in the subject (`[UAT]` / `[Production]`) so a UAT test release is never mistaken for a live one. There is no app mailer yet — the only email today is Supabase Auth's (and production SMTP is still an open Deployment item), so pick a sender (a transactional API such as Resend, or the SMTP account set up for Auth) and note that `lannacare.org` Email Routing is receive-only. Depends on the `uat` environment item in Deployment for the UAT/Production distinction; until it lands, "dev" stands in for UAT. Record the choices in `docs/decisions.md`.

Every level below that is user-defined through the UI: staff create nested folders to any depth, and any folder can hold photos *and* its own info card. **Migration:** add to `project_folders` `title_th`, `summary` / `summary_th` (short story, markdown), `project_date`, `location`, `is_public` (default false), `cover_photo_id` (FK to `project_photos`, nullable); add `caption` / `caption_th` and `sort_order` to `project_photos`; tighten RLS so volunteers can add photos to an existing folder but not create, rename, move or publish folders. **Drive:** mirror the tree exactly — `Projects/<Category>/<user folders…>/` — via `ensureProjectFolder()` in `src/lib/google/drive.ts` (create on demand, rename/move folder with the record), uploads through `/api/projects/[id]/photos` following the resident-photo route, registered in the photo-proxy lookup (0015/0019 pattern) so `driveImageUrl` serves them. **Pages:** `/projects` shows the category level; `/projects/[id]` shows a folder — breadcrumb path, subfolders first then a photo grid with captions, plus an info panel (title, date, location, story, cover-photo picker, "Show on website" toggle) and actions to new-subfolder / rename / move / upload. ### Auth

- [x] **A Senior Staff role: staff with elevated control over some parts of the system — decide what it can do, then schema PR, then build.** Lutan, 2026-10-03. Some staff members should be able to do more than a normal staff member can, without being made Management or Admin. **Today's roles** are the `app_role` enum: `admin`, `management`, `staff`, `vet`, `volunteer`, `public_viewer` (0001, 0038, 0085). Management already sits above staff, but it also gets the Management section (cashflow, contacts admin, recurring jobs and so on), which is more than "a trusted staff member" needs. **First, a decision with Lutan (the deliverable before any code):** a table of what Senior Staff can do that Staff cannot, and anything Management can do that Senior Staff still cannot. Candidates to put to him, drawn from what is gated above `staff` today (check each against the code before the table is final): withdraw a death recorded in error (admin only today); hand over or reassign a recurring job for a sick week; approve stocktake and delivery corrections; edit the reference lists (medications, diets, frequencies, types); publish residents and projects to the website; create or delete maintenance jobs for others; approve access requests (probably not: that is Settings → Security and needs 2-step). Also settle: **is Senior Staff "staff plus a list", or a rung between staff and management?** The first is easier to reason about and keeps Management's financial pages out of reach; the second means every `in ('admin','management')` check gains it. **How it is built matters more than the list:** role checks are scattered. In the app they are named predicates (`isShelterRole`, `canManage`, `canWriteMaintenance`, `canStocktake`, `canRecordDelivery`, `canArchiveMedical`, `canWriteProjects`, `canReadRecurringJobs`, `canDoJob`, `canUseAssistant`, among others), and in the database about 26 migrations name `'management'` in RLS policies and `security definer` guards. Every existing `staff` check must also let `senior_staff` through, or a Senior Staff member could do *less* than staff, so sweep for `'staff'` in both before choosing where to add the new rights. Prefer a single "role includes" helper in SQL and TypeScript (e.g. `role_at_least('staff')` or a capability function) over adding the new value to dozens of lists by hand, and decide whether this is the moment to introduce it. **Schema PR first, and it is two files:** `alter type app_role add value 'senior_staff'` alone in its own migration (an added enum value cannot be used in the same transaction, as 0085 records), then the policy and function changes in the next. Read `0085_public_viewer_role.sql` and the "enum migrations need two files" note in CLAUDE.md before numbering. **Then the feature:** the role in the Settings → Security picker and the `/admin/security` actions; the nav and route guards; `roleSummary` and per-topic `roles` in the manual (`src/lib/manual/en.ts`), both dictionaries, `/releases` role filtering (`isForRole`), the recurring-job eligibility rules, the assistant's role checks, the README roles table, and the role walkthrough (`docs/role-walkthrough.md`) gains a Senior Staff pass with its "must not" lines. A decision file in `docs/decisions/` and a releases line. **Test:** a Senior Staff login can do each thing in the agreed table, and is refused everything Management has that was not granted (pages and a direct Data API call with its own JWT), and a plain staff login is unchanged. **Note 2026-10-09 (`remove-staff-role`):** Staff itself is retired (`0173`, `docs/decisions/2026-10-09-staff-role-removed.md`), so "staff plus a list" has no Staff to start from, and every `'staff'` check this item says to sweep now lets nobody through. The need it describes, a trusted person with more than a volunteer and less than Management, is what configured roles now do (the 2IC is one, `0143`). Whether to close this is still Lutan's call (`2026-10-03-configured-roles-not-enum-values.md`); if it is kept, it is a configured role, not an enum value. **Note 2026-10-11 (`perm-drop-enum`, `0181`):** the `app_role` enum no longer exists, so nothing in this item's mechanism (adding an enum value, sweeping `'staff'` in policies) can be done as written. A Senior Staff is a row in `roles` with its own cells and scopes, made in Settings → Who does what. Still Lutan's call whether to close it.
  **Status 2026-10-03: the roles paper recommends closing this as answered** (`docs/roles-and-permissions.md` §16, question L5). Under the matrix every role is "staff plus a list" and there are no rungs; each candidate power above is already a cell in the catalogue; and the 2IC, Maintenance and Medical are the Director's actual roles with more control over some elements. Not closed here: that is Lutan's call. If someone still fits none of the roles once the Director has answered, Senior Staff becomes the first role Lanna adds itself, not an enum value.
  **CLOSED 2026-10-19 by Lutan, not built and never to be:** *"Senior staff is not a thing, I don’t know where it has come from but we now have a different structure with us assigning cards to roles so any question about what a role should be able to do is not applicable as it’s configurable in the system."* So the whole premise is gone: the deliverable this item asked for — a table of what Senior Staff may do that Staff may not — **cannot exist**, because what a role may do is now data, set by giving it cards on Settings → Who does what, not a property of a role name in code. **The roles paper recommended exactly this closure on 2026-10-03** (`docs/roles-and-permissions.md` §16, question L5) and it sat open for sixteen days, during which it was carried as a decision waiting on Lutan and briefed to him twice. **Do not reopen it.** If a person ever fits none of the roles, the answer is to give an existing role another card, or to add a role — never a new rung in code.

The account carries `app_metadata.must_change_password`; the request proxy sends such a user to `/account/password` and nowhere else while their session was opened with a password (the JWT `amr` claim) — a Google sign-in carries on. `/account/password` (also in the nav as Change password, for anyone) sets the new password as the user and then clears the flag via the service role. Google-only accounts just never use the temporary password. Original brief: Instead of the admin typing a password on Admin → Security, the app generates a temporary one (shown once to the admin to pass on), and the user must set their own password on first email/password login before reaching the app (flag on the account, e.g. `user_metadata.must_change_password`, checked in the session proxy / a `/account/password` page). Google sign-in bypasses the forced change since no password is used. Pairs with the Forgot-password item below so people manage their own passwords end-to-end and admins stop being in the password loop; the admin "reset password" action on the Security page then becomes "issue new temporary password". Consider making the password optional at creation for Google-only accounts.

### Architecture

- [x] **`worktree.mjs done` refuses to remove free worktrees, blaming "a process that cannot be identified".** Done 2026-09-26 (see `docs/decisions.md`, "A failed rename is not a session"). `held()` now retries the rename probe (four tries over ~450 ms) and only a folder that refuses every time counts as held; `done` samples it immediately before removal and gives an unnamed refusal one longer wait (six tries over ~2 s). When nobody can be named, `done` no longer asserts an unidentifiable process: it says Windows refused the rename but no session or dev server was found, that this is usually transient and `list` may show the folder free, to re-run rather than `--force`, and what to look for if it persists. A named holder is refused exactly as before. The rename back is retried too, so a transient handle can never strand a worktree under its probe name. The false-positive case is now in `docs/test-plans/worktree-tooling.md` and `docs/test-plans/worktree-done-fix.md`: under a holder that flickers on and off, the old script refused 3/3 with the "cannot be identified" message and the new one got past the probe 3/3.
- [x] **Security-definer read helpers answer anon for any row: review function EXECUTE.** Done 2026-09-25 on dev (see `docs/decisions.md`, "Anon loses the functions"); **production apply awaits Lutan's go**. Reproduced first, and it was worse than the item said: besides `approved_translations` returning the approved Thai bio of residents who are not public (3 of the 4 on dev), four `security definer` writers let anon through because `current_user_role() not in (...)` is NULL, not true, for a NULL role. As anon, in a rolled-back transaction, `delete_resident_photo` deleted a public resident photo (its id is readable from `public_resident_photos`) and `record_attachment` added an attachment to a hidden resident and made it the profile photo. `0082_anon_function_execute.sql`: guards made null-safe (`is null or … not in`), which also covers a signed-in user with no role; the unused 5-argument `record_attachment` overload dropped; `approved_translations` moved to a new `private` schema the Data API does not expose (the views follow it by oid and keep working signed out); EXECUTE revoked from PUBLIC and anon on every function in `public`, then granted back to anon on `current_user_role`, `is_known_drive_file` and the three `shelter_*` date helpers only; `postgres`'s default privileges closed so a new function starts unexecutable by anon. `scripts/check-public-views.mjs` now calls every RPC the schema root lists as anon and fails unless the allow-listed five answer and every other one is refused as a function (42501 naming it): 23 FAIL before, 0 after.
- [x] **Anon can read four internal views that bypass RLS. Revoke it.** Done 2026-09-25 on dev (see `docs/decisions.md`, "Anon loses the internal views"); **production apply awaits Lutan's go**. Reproduced first: with only the anon key, `current_placement` (81 rows), `resident_current_state` (81) and `immunization_compliance` (220) answered, `immunization_duplicate_check` 200 empty. `0081_anon_view_grants.sql` goes further than the four: it revokes everything `anon` holds on every table, view and sequence in `public`, grants back SELECT on the ten `public_*` views and `site_content` / `site_content_photos` / `site_pages`, and closes the `postgres` role's default privileges for anon so a future object does not start out readable. All four views now return 401 `permission denied`; so do the other 38 internal objects, `schema_migrations` included. TRUNCATE: PostgREST has no verb that issues it and no `public` function contains it, so it was never reachable; anon now holds it on nothing. `security_invoker` deliberately not turned on (a signed-in behaviour change, not needed to close the anon hole). `scripts/check-public-views.mjs` now lists every Data API table and view with the service-role key and fails if anon can read any that is not on its public list, so a new object is covered without anyone adding it.
- [x] **`prescriptions` and `resident_diets` have no `updated_at`, so a wrong `end_date` is permanently undetectable.** Done 2026-09-24 (see `docs/decisions.md`). `0078_prescriptions_diets_updated_at.sql` adds `updated_at timestamptz not null default now()` to both, kept current by a generic `touch_updated_at()` BEFORE trigger: `now()` on insert and on any real change, kept on a no-op update, never settable by hand. Existing rows were back-filled with the apply time, so the audit value starts at 0078 (the column comments say so). Asserted on dev by `scripts/check-prescriptions-updated-at.mjs`. Original brief: Raised 2026-09-23 by the `utc-date-audit` stream. The audit could check `date` columns against `created_at` — a timestamptz, and therefore correct whatever the session timezone was — and that is how it established what the UTC "today" bug actually touched. `end_date` cannot be audited the same way: it is written days or weeks after the row is created, so `created_at` says nothing about when it was set, and neither table records when a row was last changed. Any `end_date` corrupted by the seven-hour window (from "End today", or from the deceased cascade above) is therefore unrecoverable after the fact — there is no reference timestamp to compare against. Add `updated_at timestamptz not null default now()` to both tables with a touch trigger, so the same audit is possible going forward. Additive and harmless to existing code; goes in the same migration PR as the `current_date` item above if that one is done first, since both are small.
- [x] **Nothing catches a user-visible PR that forgot its `unreleased` line.** Done 2026-09-24 (see `docs/decisions.md`, "What counts as user-visible"). `docs/test-plan-template.md` §7 has a release-notes line, ticked or `n/a: <reason>`, and `scripts/check-test-plan.mjs` holds it to the diff: a tick with no new `unreleased` line fails, and a PR touching `src/app/`, `src/components/`, `src/lib/manual/`, `src/lib/i18n/` or `worker/` with no new line fails unless a plan answers the line; an `n/a` reason is printed in the CI output for the reviewer. Red flag, not a hard block, like the rest of `test-plan`. Original brief: Found 2026-09-24 while cutting `0.1.0`: `unreleased` in `src/lib/releases.ts` was **empty**, so the release notes for ten merged PRs had to be reconstructed from PR titles and diffs rather than written by the people who made the changes — which is the guesswork the register exists to prevent. #60 (cashflow forecast) and #67 (nav rework) both merged *after* the register landed in #62 and neither added a line, and both are plainly user-visible. `scripts/deploy.mjs` cannot catch it: it refuses production while `unreleased` is **non-empty** (so nothing ships undescribed), but an empty list is indistinguishable from "nothing user-visible shipped in this batch". The gap is one-directional and silent, and it gets worse the longer a release goes uncut, because the reconstruction is done by whoever cuts it from titles rather than intent. Fix: a line in `docs/test-plan-template.md` under Documentation — *"does this change something a shelter user would notice? if so, `src/lib/releases.ts`'s `unreleased` has a line for it, written for a user and not as a commit message"* — ticked or `n/a: <reason>` like everything else, so a PR that genuinely changes nothing visible says so out loud. Worth pairing with a check in `scripts/check-test-plan.mjs`: when a PR touches `src/app/` or `src/components/` and `unreleased` is unchanged, require that line to carry a reason rather than a bare tick, since that is exactly the combination that produced this. Not a hard gate on the diff — plenty of `src/app/` changes are genuinely invisible — but a prompt at the moment the author still remembers what they changed.
- [x] **Postgres has its own copy of the UTC "today" bug — `current_date` in a UTC session.** Done 2026-09-24 (see `docs/decisions.md`). `0073_shelter_today.sql` adds `shelter_time_zone()` / `shelter_today()` / `shelter_date(timestamptz)` and moves eight sites onto them: the `maintenance.date_created` default, the `date_completed` stamp, both lines of the death cascade, `public_shelter_stats` (`in_treatment` and both "this year" counts) and `public_recent_adoptions.adopted_on`. A death at 01:26 Bangkok now closes open courses on its own day, asserted in a rollback harness on dev. `medication_daily_requirement` had already been dropped by 0044; existing rows not repaired (dev: 0 affected). Cashflow month boundaries stay with Dashboard follow-ups (e).
- [x] **One command to run the three gates, printing each exit code.** Done 2026-09-24. `node scripts/gates.mjs` runs `npm run typecheck`, `lint` and `build` — the same three as CI's `check` job — every one of them even after a failure, and ends with `gates: typecheck=0 lint=0 build=0`, exiting 1 if any failed. It refuses to start (exit 2, nothing run) when `node_modules/.bin` lacks `next`, `tsc` or `eslint`. `--plan` adds `check-test-plan.mjs` as a fourth, opt-in because a correct plan is red until someone signs. Section 2 of the test-plan template now asks for its output pasted as-is.
- [x] **`docs/decisions.md` merges by union locally but not on GitHub, so parallel PRs read CONFLICTING.** Done 2026-09-29. Split by decision: from 2026-09-24 on, each decision is its own file, `docs/decisions/<date>-<slug>.md`, so two streams add different paths and GitHub has nothing to conflict on. `docs/decisions.md` is a frozen baseline and the `merge=union` line is gone from `.gitattributes`. CLAUDE.md, README and the test-plan template say to add a file. Old citations by path still resolve, since the date names the file. `docs/decisions/2026-09-29-decisions-one-file-per-decision.md`.
- [x] **`worktree.mjs done` reports success when it has not removed the folder.** Done 2026-09-23 (see `docs/decisions.md`). `done` now checks, before touching anything, whether any process has the folder open (rename it to a sibling name and back: Windows refuses exactly when something holds it) and refuses, naming the holder. It removes the folder, prunes git's registry and deletes the branches, then verifies all four and prints `not done:` with what survived rather than `done`. `--stop-servers` ends dev servers running from the folder's `node_modules` and retries. `list` survives a stale or broken worktree (a `STALE` row instead of `fatal: not a git repository`) and names husks, which `done <name>` clears (build output only unless `--force`).
- [x] **`worktree.mjs list` should show which worktrees have a live session, and `done` should refuse one that does.** Done 2026-09-23. `list` has a `held` column (`HELD`/`free`, plus the Claude session's name from `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json`, checked against the live process's start time) and an `unpushed` column. `done` hard-refuses a branch with commits no origin ref has, with no override. It also *refuses*, rather than warns about, a held folder. The item asked for a warning because the check races. But Windows cannot delete a held folder anyway, so carrying on would only pull git out from under the session and leave a husk. The race (a session attaching in the milliseconds after the check) is the one case left.
- [x] **`sync` leaves the branch unpushed — the post-commit hook does not fire for merges.** Done 2026-09-23. `sync` pushes as its last step, and `.githooks/post-merge` pushes after every other merge or pull (including the daily `backlog` fast-forward). CLAUDE.md's "always matches" sentence is corrected and points at `list`'s `unpushed` column.
- [x] **`.claude/launch.json` hardcodes port 3000, so the browser pane is unusable from any worktree.** Done 2026-09-23. The file is gitignored and generated per checkout from `.port` (`dev` runs `npm run dev -- --port <port>`) by `new`, `dev`, `sync`, the post-merge hook and `node scripts/worktree.mjs launch`. Verified: `preview_start` with `name: "dev"` in the worktree-tooling worktree started `next dev --port 3002` and rendered the home page.

- [x] **The app should answer "what version am I?" without a sign-in, from the origin rather than the Worker.** Raised 2026-10-02 by `apply-migrations-consumer-warning`: `/api/releases/current` is answered by `worker/index.mjs` before the origin is consulted, so nothing can ask what the Pi is running. `apply-migrations.mjs` has to *assume* the newest cut release is live, so an undeployed cut reads as live. An unauthenticated version route served by the app itself (version plus git sha) would let that check, and `deploy.mjs`, be exact.
